                                                                                                                                                    hyperMILL
1 New in version 2018.1

New in version 2018.1

     Project Assistant

                         Use the Project Assistant to create a milling or MillTurn project step by step and in a simple
                         and clear manner. Information in section Creating a milling project / MillTurn project with the
                         Project Assistant.

     Name pattern for jobs and comments

                                 Define the names of jobs or comments individually and automatically by selecting job param-
                                 eters. Information in section Using name patterns for jobs and comments.

     Toolpath quickinfo

                                 Information is available for the following via a quickinfo (tooltip): frame, job ID, job name,
                                 comment, job type, linked job, tool ID and tool name. For further information, see section
                                 Information on calculated toolpaths.

     New cycle: Rollfeed Turning
                                 Machine turning parts by rolling the tool insert on the component contour.

     2D Contour Milling on 3D Model

                                 Contour definition via a surface selection. Information in section Contour Milling on 3D
                                 Model.

     3D Optimised Roughing
                                 Optimised machining of adaptive pockets with large lateral but small vertical infeed and high
                                 feedrate.
                                 · Automatic calculation of the lateral infeed based on the defined scallop height.
                                 · It is also possible to define the scallop height for plane level detection.
                                 · Smooth rolling in of the tool in the adaptive pocket area.
                                 Information in section Strategy.
                                 Feedrate reduction during full cut is also now available for 3D Optimised Roughing. Informa-
                                 tion in section Strategy.

     Slope dependent machining
                                 Use the Smooth overlap option to optimise the surface quality in the transition area between
                                 flat and steep areas with small retract movements of the tool. Available for the following
                                 cycles:
                                 · 3D Profile Finishing
                                 · 3D Complete Finishing
                                 · 3D Z Level Shape Finishing
                                 · 3D Z Level Finishing
                                 Information in section Strategy.

     Feature technology

                                 Contour feature: The Point option is now also available as a contour parameter (type). This
                                 provides improved automation during machining probing. Information in section Contour.

     Tool database

                         Extended coolant management

                         Define up to seven further coolants in addition to the standard coolants. A unique, consecu-
                         tive ID is allocated to each coolant. This makes an evaluation possible during the postproc-
                         essor run. Additional information (coolant properties, coolant type) can be allocated to a
                         coolant.

1-2                                                                                                          hyperMILL
           New in version 2018.1  1

           Simulation             Couplings
                                  The top coupling is no longer defined for the tool but is now defined for the holder. The cou-
                                  pling remains visible for the tool but cannot be edited.
                                  The Adaptor coupling type can now also be combined with tool holders and extensions.

                                  New tool: roll turn tool
                                  The new Roll turn tool, tool type is available in the new Rollfeed Turning cycle. Four different
                                  insert types are available for the roll turn tool to ensure an optimal rolling of the tool insert on
                                  the component contour.

                                  New inserts
                                  Four new insert types can be defined for the roll turn tool:
                                  · X Full Roll Turn
                                  · X Short Roll Turn
                                  · T Full Roll Turn
                                  · T Short Roll Turn

                                  X/Z setting length for turning tools
                                  Improved display of turning tools in the graphics area of the tool database by displaying the
                                  Setting length x and Setting length z for turning tools.

                                  External simulation
                                  Support of COLLISION SAFEGUARD as an external simulation program. Information in sec-
                                  tion External simulation.

                                  Improved rest material display
                                  Rest material is now displayed in four steps during the machine simulation. The steps are
                                  defined on the basis of the value of the maximum permissible rest material.
                                  Example: maximum rest material = 1. First step = <0.25, second step = < 0.5, third step = <
                                  0.75, fourth step = > 0.75.

         Overview

User interface

     Overview

                   This user's guide covers the CAM editing functions. For information on the CAD functions,
                   see the various online help texts (available on the Help menu).

     hyperMILL: Integrated CAM Application

                                The hyperMILL CAM solution requires you to have installed a working version of a CAD
                                application or the Geometric Engine from hyperMILL, into which it is fully integrated. It is
                                 used for generating 2D, 3D, 5-axis and turning NC programs for model and mold construc-
                                tion. hyperMILL is available as an integrated application for the following CAD systems:

                                · hyperCAD-S

                                · hyperCAD

                                 · Autodesk Inventor

                                 · SolidWorks

                                 Note that some of the functions described in this guide are not available in your installation.
                                 The range of functions depends on the licences obtained and the configuration of the soft-
                                 ware purchased.

     hyperMILL SHOP Viewer

                                The hyperMILL SHOP Viewer allows you to display, analyse and document processed CAD/
                                CAM data. The software works on the basis of hyperCAD-S and hyperMILL. The following
                                software documentation explains all the features of hyperMILL. The functions described may
                                not be available or may not be available to the extent described, in hyperMILL SHOP Viewer.

                                For further information on the functions of hyperMILL SHOP Viewer, please refer to the cor-
                                responding section in the product documentation for hyperCAD-S.

     Supported CAD formats

                                 Supports a wide range of geometry formats (e.g. DXF, DWG, IGES, VDA), which enable
                                 data exchange with the majority of CAD construction programs. Data conversion takes place
                                 in the background, while the model is loading.

                                 During conversion a log window with status information is displayed. The corresponding log
                                 file (*.log) can be opened and viewed later on from within the directory of the associated
                                 model file.

                   Direct interfaces are provided as modules for the following data formats: CATIA

                   V4, CATIA V5, PTC CREO, Siemens NX, Parasolid and SolidWorks. Please
                   contact your dealer. For more information, please see the product documenta-

                   tion for OPEN MIND direct interfaces.

2-2                                                       hyperMILL
           User interface         2 Overview
           Supported CAD formats

                                       The following formats are supported for saving model data and for CAM editing:
                                      · *.hmc: hyperCAD-S document format
                                      · *.hcplain: Uncompressed hyperCAD-S document format
                                      · *.hmct: hyperCAD-S format for saving a geometry as a template for a new document
                                      · *.hmcgeom: Native hyperCAD-S format. Contains only geometric and topological data

                                              in binary, uncompressed format including information on solids and meshes, but not on
                                              colours, attributes, etc.
                                      · *.e2 or *.e3: hyperMILL/hyperMILL in hyperCAD
                                      · *.ipt: hyperMILL in Autodesk Inventor
                                      · *.sldprt and *.sldasm: hyperMILL for SolidWorks

           Saving hyperMILL SHOP Viewer data

                                       When saving the data in *.hmc format, the following options can be enabled and included as
                                       components in the file in the Setup dialogue: stock data, toolpath entities, postprocessor
                                       configuration, prepared geometry.

           *.e3 data for hyperMILL in hyperCAD-S

                                      A *.e3 file must have been stored with a hyperMILL version 2009.2 or newer and with an
                                      active hyperMILL session in order to ensure that all selections in hyperMILL are restored for
                                      hyperCAD-S.
                                       Further information on exchanging data is available in the corresponding CAD manual.

         hyperMILL and CAD program

     hyperMILL and CAD program

                                hyperMILL is a CAM module that is fully integrated into the CAD program and is used for
                                 generating 2D, 3D, 5-axis, milling and turning programs. Individual machining steps (jobs)
                                 are created on the basis of machining cycles with the open CAD model in the form of one or
                                 more work schedules (joblists).

                                All functions of the hyperMILL toolkit, as well as all input pages, menus and programs that
                                 can be opened with icons can also be accessed using keyboard commands and repeated
                                 using <return> (for information on keyboard commands, see section Keyboard commands).

     Starting the CAM editing

     hyperMILL in hyperCAD-S

                                When you open a hyperCAD-S document, the hyperMILL browser opens automatically. All
                                CAM functionalities can be accessed through the entry hyperMILL in the hyperCAD-S menu
                                 bar.

           Layout of the browser

           The hyperMILL browser

                                      The hyperMILL browser is used to define job lists, tools, machining systems (frames) and
                                       features.

           Layout of the browser

                                      The hyperMILL browser consists of the following elements:

hyperMILL                         Tabs (1) Jobs, Tools, Frames, Models, Features and Macros.
                                  Browser window (2) with the defined elements (partly in a tree structure).
                                  Toolbar (3) with functions for editing and calculating the elements.

                                             Open the selected entry (job/joblist) for editing.
                                             Delete the selected entry (job/joblist).
                                             Display messages for the selected entry (job/joblist).
                                             Delete the toolpath for the selected entry (job/joblist).
                                             Open the tool database to select an NC tool.
                                             Display the model in a transparent manner in the graphics area.
                                             Show the removed material automatically when a job has been selected.
                                             Check the status of the toolpaths for the selected entry (job/joblist).

      Configure browser

                                  The tabs can be arranged anywhere in the browser or undocked from the browser window.
                                  To do this, click the tab and move it to the required place while holding down the left mouse
                                  button. Possible docking positions are indicated by a graphical feedback as blue, transpar-
                                  ent areas. Dock or undock the tab from the browser by double-clicking (left mouse button)
                                  the title bar in the browser.

                                Show or hide a tab. Right-click the tab and enable or disable the respective function on the
                                shortcut menu.

      View manager:

                                Use the View manager to control the visibility of tabs in the hyperMILL browser.

      Jobs tab                          To start the View manager, click Setup > View manager in the hyperMILL menu.
                                By default, all tabs are shown in the browser. To hide a tab, disable the respective option.
                                Use Reset layout to restore the default settings.

                                The top section of the browser displays joblists and jobs and the bottom section shows the
                                milling areas and stockmodels. An entry highlighted in red is a prerequisite for an entry high-
                                lighted in blue. An entry highlighted in blue is dependent on an entry highlighted in red. The
                                entry's marking in the browser indicates whether or not a job definition is complete and cor-
                                rect.

                                           Definition free of errors/warning. Calculate job with these parameters.

                                           Definition free of errors/warning. Definition free of errors/warning calculation status
                                           currently unknown (can be checked explicitly using command Toolpath status
                                           check).

      Models tab

                                The browser window contains milling and turning areas in the top section and stockmodels in

                                marking in the browser indicates whether or not a job is complete and correct.

                                Milling area contains no faults or warnings
                                Milling area contains warnings

                                Element (toolpath/stockmodel) does not exist, must be calculated

                                tion.

                                The macros that are applied are displayed in the browser window.

hyperMILL                                                                   2-13
2 User interface                                                       Dialogue control configuration
         Job definition dialogues

      Job definition dialogues

      Dialogue control configuration

                                  Set the dialogue control in the Setup > Settings dialogue, Application dialogue page.

                                  Dialogues
                                  Modal: The input dialogues contain the general function icons. For further information, see
                                  section Dialogue control functions. It is not possible to quickly switch the display between dif-
                                  ferent jobs.
                                  Modeless: The input dialogues do not contain any general function icons. It is possible to
                                  quickly switch the display between different jobs (see Dialogue positioning).
                                  The dialogue control functions can be accessed via the shortcut menu at the input dialogue
                                  header. Input dialogues can be fixed to any chosen position by clicking on a pin in the
                                  header. Jobs can be calculated when a dialogue is open
                                  In this mode all settings are applied immediately and are always saved when the dialogue is
                                  closed. It is not possible to exit without saving changes.
                                  Text: Dialogue tabs contain text that displays the contents. In the case of cycles with a high
                                  number of definition parameters, the different tabs cannot be viewed side by side.
                                  Icons: Dialogue tabs contain icons that display the contents. Even in the case of cycles with
                                  a high number of definition parameters, all the tabs can be viewed side by side.

           Dialogue positioning

                                       In the Modeless dialogue control mode, all input dialogues that are opened via the browser
                                       feature a pin that allows the dialogue to be fixed anywhere on the screen. Message windows
                                       always feature this pin, regardless of which dialogue mode is set.

                                     Dialogue is not pinned: The current dialogue window will close when you switch to
                               another dialogue or to the browser.

                                     Pinning dialogue: Pinning allows you to simultaneously display different dialogues for a
                               job (e.g. job, tool and frame definition as well as message windows). When you select a dif-
                               ferent job list entry, the display switches to the definitions for the currently selected list entry.
                               This means that you can quickly check all definitions for a job. The contents of the open
                               message window refresh immediately when you edit in other dialogue windows.

           Input field colours

                                       Black input value: The value is correct.

                                       Red input value: The job can be calculated with this value, however, collisions might occur.
                                       Read the warning in the message window. Change the respective values if necessary and
                                       check the job in simulation after calculating the toolpath.

                                       Input field with red background: The input value is incorrect (for example, bottom higher than
                                       top).The job cannot be calculated. Open the message window and edit value according to
                                       the messages.

           Input field values

                               There are several ways to enter values for parameters:
                               · Direct entry of required value into input field.
                               · Use of a predefined local cycle parameters.
                               · Definition of user variables.
                               · Definition using arithmetical expressions.

                                           Local parameters and user variables can be combined in a single expression.
                                           You can also enter any of the values directly into the input field.

                               Local cycle parameters
                               Depending on the cycle and input dialogue, you can also use predefined local cycle parame-
                               ters.

                                  Click the icon to select a local parameter directly from the shortcut menu (J:). All the
                               entries that you make directly in the input field can be made without the J: prefix (as long as
                               there are no user-defined variables with the same name). No distinction is made between
                               upper and lower case.

                               User variables

                                   Click the icon to define a user variable and select the ... option. The User Variable win-
                               dow opens. Right-click and then select New.... Enter the required data in the Code, Value
                               and Description fields. You can also enter predefined arithmetical expressions in the Value
                               field. Double-click the corresponding line of a user variable to change its definition. The most
                               recently used variables are displayed in the middle third of the shortcut menu (max.5 varia-
                               bles displayed). All data that you enter directly into the input fields has to be entered in
                               exactly the same way as defined in the variable. Upper and lower case is not freely defina-
                               ble.

Basics

            From the model to the NC program

                                             The modular structure of hyperMILL creates a flexible workflow from the model to the NC
                                               program. Important elements of this workflow include:

                                                                                CAM/CAD system

          Specify basic settings

          Define workpiece origin and frame(s)  Define tool

          Prepare manufacturing geometry        Structure CAM projects
          (contours, surfaces, stockmodel)      (joblist, compound job, job)

          Collision check preparations

           Calculate toolpaths
          Simulate toolpaths

          Generate NC program

     Specify basic settings

                                Define the measurement system and storage directories for hyperMILL data. Configure the
                                 dialogue control, configure the tool and macro database and define further basic settings.
                                 Information in section Specify basic settings.

     Define workpiece origin and frame(s)

                                 With the origin reference system (NC system), establish a connection to the machine coordi-
                                 nate system. For information on the NC system, see section NC system and frames.
                                 Using a frame, define the current machining side and machining direction. See the informa-
                                 tion in section NC system and frames.
                                 To machine identical component areas, use transformations to reproduce and position tool-
                                 paths as required. See the information in section Transformations.

                                 Use origins to control the NC output and apply origins when defining transformations. See
                                 the information in section Origins.

3-2                                                                           hyperMILL
           Basics           3
           Defining a tool

           Defining a tool

                                       Define a new tool or apply a tool from the tool database. See the information in section
                                       Defining a tool in the hyperMILL browser.

           Prepare manufacturing geometry (contours, surfaces, stockmodel)

                                       Both 2D contours and CAD models can be used for 2D machining. For information on con-
                                       tour selection, see section Selecting elements.
                                       3D, 5-axis and turning jobs are based on a CAD model. For information on the CAD model,
                                       see section CAD model.
                                       A stockmodel can be defined for various machining operations. Information in section Defin-
                                       ing stockmodels.

           Structure CAM projects

                                       Define job and joblist. See the information in section Defining a job and section Defining a
                                       joblist.
                                       Use compound jobs to structure the workflow within a joblist. For information on compound
                                       jobs, see section Compound job.

           Collision check preparations

                                       Specify a milling area or turning area to define the collision-checked part of the CAD model.
                                       See the information in section Define milling area and section Define turning area.
                                       Define a collision-checked clamping area to firmly fix the workpiece during machining. See
                                       the information in section Clamping area definition.

           Calculate toolpaths

                                      Either directly in the job definition (for an individual job) or in the hyperMILL browser (for an
                                       individual job, multiple jobs or all the jobs in a joblist).
                                       See the information in section Calculate toolpaths.

           Simulate toolpaths

                                      Use hyperVIEW, the internal simulation, the internal machine simulation or an external simu-
                                       lation program (for example, VERICUT).
                                       See the information in section Simulating machining.

           Generate NC program

                                      Output an NC program either via the Generate NC file shortcut menu in the hyperMILL
                                      browser or using hyperVIEW.

     Creating a milling project / MillTurn project with the Project Assistant

                                 Use the Project Assistant to create a milling project or MillTurn project in a predefined
                                 sequence of steps. The following are defined in the individual steps:
                                 · Model and machining technology
                                 · NCS orientation
                                 · Stock size and allowances
                                 · NCS position
                                 · Machining frames
                                 · Names for joblist, milling area/turning area, stock as well as material and machine.
                                 The steps can be in any order. Use Next to go to the next dialogue page and Previous to go
                                 to the previous dialogue page. Click OK to apply the settings you have defined. Click Cancel
                                 to close the Project Assistant without savings the settings.

     Starting the Project Assistant
                                 Go to the Jobs tab, right-click and select the New > Project Assistant ... function.

                                         Alternatively, use the hyperMILL Project Assistant menu to start the Project Assis-
                                 tant.

     Defining the machining technology

                                            Model and Process: Select Milling technology to create a milling project or MillTurn
                                 technology to set up a MillTurn project.
                                 Use Surfaces to select the surfaces or solids to be machined.

     Defining the orientation of the NCS

                                            NCS Orientation: Define the orientation of the NCS.
                                 Use one of the options provided for milling: Workplane, Surface or 3 Points.
                                 Reverse the direction of the Z axis of the NCS (1) using Reverse > z direction.
                                 Select an element (line, edge of the model) under X direction > Select to define the direction
                                 of the X axis. Alternatively, use the 2 Points / Point option to align the X axis.

                                        Rotate the X axis clockwise by the defined angle (2).

                                        Rotate the X axis anti-clockwise by the defined angle (3).

           Defining the position of the NCS

                                                   NCS Position: Define the position of the NCS.
                                       Mode: Select whether the NCS should be positioned at one of the predefined Basic positions
                                       or at a Userdefined position.
                                       Use Basic positions to select a position Relative to the model (1) or Relative to the stock.
                                       Under Userdefined, select the Origin directly in the CAD system.
                                       Milling: NCS position relative to the model (1), NCS position relative to the stock (2).

           MillTurn: NCS position relative to the model (1), NCS position relative to the stock (2).

           Available basic positions are located on the rotary axis (3), the centre of the turning surface.
           The rotary axis corresponds to the Z axis of the NCS.

           (A) NCS position = Z-, (B) NCS position = Z+.

                                 In the hyperMILL Setup > Settings menu.

                           The Setup hyperMILL dialogue is used to specify the basic settings that are valid for all sub-
                           sequent actions and definitions in hyperMILL. The dialogue contains the following dialogue
                           pages: Document, Application, hyperCAD-S, Database, Maintenance and Tire (only availa-

           Document

                           Units
                           Metric/Inch: The selected system of units applies to all input and output values.

           Colour setting                 Do not change the measuring system during CAM programming, otherwise
                                          definition values that have already been created will not be converted.
                                         Copying jobs between hyperMILL documents with different measuring systems
                                          is not allowed.

                           Directories
                           Project: Create project-specific directories to store your generated files.
                           Use Path to select a project folder. All generated files are stored in subfolders.
                           If you select Model path, all generated files will be stored in subfolders relative to the model
                           file.

                           Global working space: All files generated are stored under the default path set under Appli-

                           bottom), clearance plane, tool or coordinate systems.

                           Colours: Open the Colours dialogue, then open the Colour selection dialogue and define the
                           desired colour by clicking on it.

                           Define the colours for G0 and G1 movements, collisions, tool axis and clipped toolpaths.

                           Feedback colours

                           Colours for list display
                           Define the colours for list display (featurelists).
                           Used by Feature Mapping: Colours used for feature lists from the Feature Mapping.
                           Feedbacks (browser default): Activate if feedbacks are to be shown by default when creating
                           a new job (shortcut menu of job: feedbacks).

                           Max. number of origins: Limits the maximum permissible number of origins. Information in
                           section Origins.
                           Use global clearance plane: Select this option to use the global clearance plane of the frame
                           instead of the clearance plane from the job definition. The formula value for the global clear-

                                 ance plane will then be firmly linked with the Clearance plane parameter for the job definition

                                 Calculation

                                 These settings apply to toolpath generation.

                                 Display temporary graphics : Temporary toolpaths created during the calculation are shown
                                 on screen in the interim and are then replaced by the final toolpaths.

                                 Display toolpaths: The generated toolpaths are output graphically on the screen.

                                 Erase existing toolpaths: The next time a job is calculated, the existing toolpath is deleted.
                                 The newly generated toolpath is output graphically on the screen.

                                 Update cache automatically: After a geometry that is to be machined has been modified, the
                                 outdated geometry data is deleted from the cache before each calculation and the modified
                                 geometry is converted again.

                                 This function should always be enabled (it is active by default) in order to avoid
                                 faulty calculations.

                                 Notify changed geometry: A message is generated for the geometry to be machined before
                                 the job is recalculated to notify the user that modified geometry data has been found and that
                                 the stored data will be deleted.
                                 Delete temporary files: Deletes the temporary files (*.tmp) created during joblist calculation.
                                 Do not select this option if you are having problems with a component that requires the
                                 assistance of your OPEN MIND dealer.
                                 Preserve reports: Save your report file in the folder defined on the Application dialogue page
                                 of the Setup hyperMILL dialogue (default paths).

                                 Check toolpath status
                                 Check geometry: When geometry changes are made, the system checks whether the tool-
                                 path is still up-to-date.

                                        Following the toolpath status check, the modified geometry is displayed in the hyper-
                                   MILL browser. As this function uses up a lot of processing time, it is disabled by default.

                                 · Deletion
                                 · Deletion and geometry change
                                 · Deletion, geometry and attribute change

hyperMILL
                     Message mode
                     Specify the information to be displayed as messages during job definition. These settings do
                     not relate to message windows you call up manually. Each message mode (Severe errors,
                     Errors, Severe warnings, Warnings, Infos) automatically includes the respective next `level'.

                     Model check
                     Auto: Changes to the CAD model trigger a consistency check between the defined jobs and
                     the CAD model. If automatic model checking is switched off, it can be performed separately
                     for each job via the job or joblist's shortcut menu. Regardless of this setting, a model check
                     is always carried out before generating the toolpaths.

                     Licensing
                     Licence status: Shows the status of your hyperMILL licences.
                     All products: Locked and available products are displayed.
                     Locked products: Only locked products are displayed.
                     Licensed products: Only available (and licensed) products are displayed.
                     If you work with network licences, you can reserve specific licences for your computer when
                     you start hyperMILL. Select the product that you want to lock and enable the Lock on start
                     option.
                     For more information on network installations, refer to the installation guide for your product.
                     Show locked products only: When you create a new job, only those products that are availa-
                     ble for your computer (locked products) are displayed.

                     2D compatibility
                     Limit 2D jobs to NCS: You cannot select frames in 2D jobs. Select this setting if you are only
                     going to program on the NCS (program zero point) and your postprocessor is not suitable for
                     multi-axis indexing.

                     Default paths
                     Paths for saving files generated with hyperMILL. Use the following icons to make changes.

                                    Add/remove directory.

                            Change path.
                     Global working space: location for storing all data that is generated by hyperMILL (toolpaths,
                     models, databases and so on). Changes are possible only using the hyperMILL SettingsWiz-
                     ard (hmInit.exe).

                           hyperMILL search path: The directories are set by default but can be changed if
                     required. Once paths have been correctly set here, only the name of each file needs to be
                     entered for all further processes.
                     Temporary files: Only temporary files needed within the program, including, for example,
                     boundary files (.bnd), profile files (.prf) and calculation files for individual cycles (.omx).
                     Configuration files: User-specific default settings.
                     nightSHIFT: Path to the nightSHIFT program.
                     Projects: Files will be stored in this directory if you have selected the Project directories
                     option on the Document dialogue page of the Setup hyperMILL dialogue.
                     3DF files: Directory for polyhedron files (mathematical collision models for calculating tool-
                     paths).
                     Hmrep files: Directory for temporary geometry files.
                     Stock files: Directory for stock files in *.STL or *.VIS format.
                     Toolpaths: Directory for toolpaths with information that is required to generate an NC pro-
                     gram.

3 Basics                         Document
         Specify basic settings

                                  Backup files: Directory for *.hyperMILL backup files.
                                  Report files: Directory for report files with messages output from the program during toolpath
                                  calculation (error messages, warnings and so on).
                                  NC files: Directory for NC files (postprocessor run).
                                  Export- / Import files: Directory for the exported or imported jobs of a joblist.
                                  Macros: Directory for macro files.
                                  CPF files: Directory for Customised Process Feature files.
                                  AddIns: Not used currently.

                                  Performance
                                  Use all CPU resources for cycle computing: The majority of cycles support multi-core pro-
                                  cessors and perform calculations in parallel. If this option is selected, all of your computer's
                                  CPU resources will be used for cycle computing. Please note that the simultaneous use of
                                 hyperMILL for interactive work during a calculation may slow down the system.
                                  If the option is not selected, a part of your computer's CPU resources will be available during
                                 cycle computing for simultaneous hyperMILL use, which means that toolpath calculation
                                  may be slowed down as a result.

                                  Backup
                                 The Activate option allows hyperMILL to create backup copies of the CAD model files used
                                  (*.hmc /*.e3). Each backup file created in this way contains the following file names:
                                  [Original file name]_ [n].hmc.hyperMILL
                                 To open a backup file in hyperMILL, change the file extension to *.hmc /*.e3.
                                  Number of backup copies per document: Specifies the number of backup copies per CAD
                                  model file. At present, you can create up to 999 backup copies. Each time you save the
                                  model file, a backup copy is created. Once the maximum number of backup copies is
                                  reached, the backup copy created first is overwritten.

           NC system

           NC system and frames

           NC system  The NC system defines the position of the workpiece origin and the orientation of the
           Frame      machining axes (XYZ).
                      The workpiece origin must match the reference point of the workpiece on the machine.
                      hyperMILL calculates all the toolpaths in the NC system. The NC system applies to an entire
                      job list at one time.

                      A frame defines the current machining side and orientation. In multi-axis indexing, a frame
                      has to be defined for each machining side. The assignment of the frame to a job takes place
                      in the job definition.
                      NC system (1)
                      Frames (2-4)

hyperMILL                            All frames must be defined before generating the toolpaths. Subsequent move-
                                     ment or rotation will mean having to recalculate all tool paths affected by the
                                     change. If the NC system is modified, then the entire joblist has to be recalcu-
                                     lated. If frames are modified, the affected jobs must be recalculated.

                      Correct job definition and therefore machining can be achieved only if the tool coordinate
                      system is in the correct position and orientation for the job, because:
                      All definitions for the vertical machining area are in relation to the frame (top, bottom), clear-
                      ance distance, XY plane, horizontal stepover.
                      The frame shares responsibility for collision checking during machining.
                      Surfaces that cannot be recognised from the tool axis perspective (1) are not machined.

                                                                                                                                                          3-15
3 Basics                              Define Frames
         NC system and frames

                               In hyperMILL, the first point of a toolpath can also lie below the level given by the height of
                               the machining side in the z+ direction. This generally means below the uppermost point in

                               the model. The positioning movements made by the machine axes up to this first point are
                               not represented in the toolpath, but defined in the postprocessor. An OPEN MIND postproc-
                               essor positions the rotational axes first, and only then proceeds to the first point of the tool-

                               path along the linear axes. This needs to be taken into particular consideration during 5X

                               programming, for example when linking with the Clearance mode > Radial option or linking

                               triaxial toolpaths with differently oriented frames.

      Define NC system

                                  When a new (empty) joblist is opened, the NC system aligns with the world workplane.
                                  Before a joblist is defined, the NC system must be adapted to the machining conditions.
                                  These changes can be made via the joblist (Setup dialogue page) or the frame definition.

      Frame limit

                               The Frame limit dialogue page is only available via the Define frame dialogue in the job list
                               (Setup dialogue page > NCS).

                               Using the Frame limit, jobs with hole features may be automatically assigned to a joblist
                               (Apply macro function). Assignment is based on the direction of the hole features used in the
                               job that may either be defined using an angle limit from A/B and C axes or using plane nor-
                               mals.

                               Frame limit

                               None: The hole features may be in all directions.

                               Limit 3D range: Specify the permissible maximum angle range of the A/B and C axes. Here,
                               the A/B axes correspond to the X/Y direction and the C axis corresponds to the Z direction of
                               the selected coordinate system.

                               Limit by planes: Use the normals of the selected planes as limits. A graphical preview (1)
                               shows the defined frame limit. The following applies to the Limit 3D range option:

                               Yellow: All jobs with a hole feature direction within the area marked in yellow will be merged
                               into the corresponding joblist.

                               Green: All jobs with a hole feature direction within the area marked in green will be merged
                               into an additionally created joblist.

           General        The following example describes application of the Frame limit function.

                          Application
                          All holes with directions within the defined angle limit are to be merged into a single job list.

                          Procedure
                          1. Create the corresponding joblists and define the Frame limit necessary for the respec-

                                tive NC system by specifying a permissible maximum angle range for the rotation axes
                                (see description above).
                          2. Use the Feature Mapping function. Enable the Use Generic Hole Only function to do so.
                                hyperMILL creates a list of Generic Holes which correspond to the defined mapping
                                conditions.
                          3. Then select all Generic Holes with the same diameter and select the Apply macro func-
                                tion from the shortcut menu.
                          4. In the macro database, select the joblist with the required frame limit, enable the Check
                                frame option and click Apply.

                          Result
                          All jobs whose feature orientation lies within the defined maximum angle range will be
                          included in the selected joblist.
                          A new joblist will be created for all jobs whose feature orientation lies outside the defined
                          frame limit.

                          changed later in the frame list's tree structure.
                          Global clearance plane: clearance plane of the frame. To change the default value, enter a
                          new value, right-click the left side of the dialogue header and select the Save as default
                          option from the shortcut menu.

                               If you modify a frame later on, recheck all the jobs that use the frame.

      Origins

                               Influence your NC output by defining origins.

                               Make accuracy or tolerance corrections for a specific area of the part to be machined as well
                               as precise position adjustments.

                               postprocessing using an origin table.

                               The active Output origin is displayed as graphical feedback in the CAD window.

      Example of use

                               Contour Milling on 3D Model- Transformations

                               To machine a contour on four different sides of a cube in a job, for example, you just have to
                               program this on one side. The other three sides of the cube are machined automatically by
                               transformation. To do this in the job definition, proceed as follows:

                               1. Create an origin for each side to be machined. Then create a frame for each origin
                                     using the New frame from origin shortcut menu.

                               2. Make the required settings in each of the job dialogues. Make sure that the correct
                                     frame (defined for the contour) is set in the Tool > Frame area. Then switch to the
                                     Transformation dialogue page.

                               3. Define a General pattern where you specify each of the previously defined (origin-
                                     based) frames as the target reference system. Switch to the Transformation dialogue
                                     page of the job definition, set the transformation to Active, disable the Keep original job
                                     option and select the Use job frame option under Start reference.

           NC Output

           NCS and frame lie in one plane
                                      Using hyperMILL, it is possible to generate an NC output in these situations without switch-
                                       ing workplanes even when using indexing postprocessors.
                                       All toolpath points (coordinates) refer to the active origin/NCS. In addition, the Z axes of the
                                       NCS and the job frame must have the same direction.
                                       If you would like to have this type of NC output, please contact your OPEN MIND partner,
                                       who will be glad to assist you in enabling this new output.

           Switch workplanes for transformations in the plane
                                      Using hyperMILL, it is possible to force jobs with transformations to switch to a different
                                       workplane for each job created by a transformation if all these transformations are in the
                                       same plane as the job frame.
                                       If the job frame and NCS are in the same plane and an NC output was already enabled for
                                       the NCS, then this option is not available. Please contact your OPEN MIND partner to
                                       arrange this.
                                       For further information on transformations, see section Transformations.

                                       Generate graphical entities: Generate non-associative CAD elements for the display of the

                                       Usage: Display jobs in which the selected element is used.

                                       Feedbacks / No feedbacks: Turn feedback on/off for the currently selected coordinate sys-
                                       tem.

         Transformations

      Transformations

                                  Toolpath reproduction and positioning to manufacture identical and/or similar workpieces.

      Basics

                          A transformation is a relative movement within a reference coordinate system. The starting
                          point is a start reference (start coordinate system) and the end point is a target reference
                          (target coordinate system). The movement can comprise a linear and/or rotating movement.

                          Target reference                                Rotation around the X axis: 45°,
                                                                          rotation around the Z axis: - 45°

                          Movement in X, Y and Z direction with axis ro-
                          tation

                          Start reference

      Advantages

                          · Significantly shorter programming times for identical and/or similar geometries
                          · Associativity of the transformation when changes are made to the geometry
                          · Flexibility as a result of partial deactivation of the direct connection between the base

                                element and the transformed element
                          · No limitations for 2D, 3D and 5X machining
                          hyperMILL supports mirrors, linear, circular and general patterns.

                                         It is possible to use NC control functions (e.g., zero point moves, subprograms,
                                         etc.). However, they require a special adjustment to the postprocessor. Please
                                         contact your OPEN MIND dealer.

                          Transformations add a transformation rule to the toolpath calculated. hyperMILL does not
                          move or copy the toolpath to the target position, but displays the resulting jobs and job cop-
                          ies as graphical feedback.

                          The NC is output in exactly the same way as if the jobs had been created nor-
                          mally and a separate frame used for each. As a result, positioning movements
                          can sometimes occur on 5-axis machines when using rotation axes.

      Examples

                          Circular pattern in the plane with 3D postprocessor (no index postprocessor)

3-22                                                                                                         hyperMILL
           Basics                                  3 Transformations
           Examples

                     The postprocessor maps the frame system of all copies on the NCS and creates link rapids
                     on the clearance plane of the jobs.

                     Circular pattern in the plane with 5-axis postprocessor

                     Depending on the settings, the postprocessor outputs a different table/head orientation for
                     each position, if required. Additional movements occur between all copies, which correspond
                     to a safe positioning logic of the machine.

                                                       Linking movements created by the postprocessor are not collision-checked
                                                       against the 3D model. You therefore need to ensure that the clearance plane is
                                                       above all collision-relevant elements.

                                       Using the frame ID for postprocessors
                                       If your postprocessor requires you to define a frame ID or a frame comment, your postproc-
                                      essor is incompatible with toolpaths that were created using the hyperMILL Transformation
                                       function.
                                       For this reason, please only use toolpaths without transformations for these postprocessors.
                                       Structuring the NC output
                                       For recurring toolpaths that were created using transformations, a simplified NC output is not
                                       generally provided (for example, as a subprogramme or part of the programme that repeats).
                                       If you wish to have a suitable simplified NC output, contact your OPEN MIND dealer. Please
                                       also bear in mind that a fee may be required for postprocessor enhancements.

                                                       For toolpaths generated by a transformation, only one safety check with a toler-
                                                       ance of 0.05 mm will be carried out. Collisions with a sufficiently small overlap
                                                       may not be recognised under certain circumstances. Please check the geomet-
                                                       ric conditions and parameters of the transformation carefully before machining.
                                                       This constraint does not hold for the mirror.

           Defining transformations

                                       Transformations are defined in two steps:
                                       Step 1: Define base parameters.
                                       Step 2: Define manufacturing parameters.

           Defining base parameters:
                                      In the hyperMILL browser, switch to the Frames tab and select the required transformation
                                       from the shortcut menu in the Transformation area.

           Defining the manufacturing parameters
                                       Apply a transformation in the job. To do so, go to the Transformation dialogue page in the job
                                       definition and select the Active checkbox.
                                       Selection: Select the type of transformation, then select a transformation.

                     (1) Select a transformation.

hyperMILL            (2) Create a new transformation.

                           For toolpaths generated by a transformation, no precise safety check is carried
                           out.
                           Collisions with a sufficiently small overlap cannot be recognised under certain
                           circumstances.
                           Please check the geometric conditions and parameters of the transformation
                           carefully before machining.

                          ence option. The frame in use is displayed.

                         If you would like origin tables or other control functions to be supported, please contact your
                         OPEN MIND partner. To support these functions, we need to organise a special consultation
                         session, define an adapted clamping cube and modify the postprocessor.

                         This special type of transformation mirrors the base geometry. The prerequisite for proper
                         mirror application in hyperMILL is the symmetry of the workpiece in use.
                         hyperMILL then calculates new toolpaths on the basis of the mirrored geometry.
                         Advantages
                         · Full associativity between the base geometry and the mirrored element (job, compound

                               job or job list)
                         · No limitations for 2D, 3D and 5X machining
                         · Flexibility as a result of partial deactivation of the direct link between the base element

                               and the mirrored element
                         · Retention of technology parameters (such as auto climb, automatic macros or opti-

                               mised linking movements) in the mirror.
                         · Patterns can be combined.

3 Basics                  Examples
         Transformations

                                         The mirroring of turning jobs is no longer possible from Version 2017.2 due to a
                                         risk of collision. This also applies to the Turning drilling mode in drilling cycles.

                          You can use a mirror in a job, compound job or joblist.
                          When mirroring curve machinings in the 2D Contour Milling, 3D Free Path Milling and 5X
                          Contouring cycles, a distinction is drawn between whether machining takes place to the side
                          of the contour (options: left/right) or on the contour (option: On contour) .
                          When machining takes place on the contour, the curve is mirrored, including the start point,
                          to guarantee geometrically symmetric material removal, see figure (1).
                          When machining takes place at the side of the contour, the direction of the contour in the
                          mirroring is inverted to guarantee equal climb to the contour in the mirrored machining, see
                          figure (2).

                          changes to the original job are also taken into account in the copy during the recalculation.

                               Mirrors and stock models
                                  Stock models which are to be reflected, must be in *. format. To mirror a job list that uses a
                                  stock model:
                                  1. On the Mirror dialogue page in the joblist, select the mirror plane and enable the Copy

                                         option to create a (mirrored) copy of the joblist that you have already defined.
                                  2. On the Model data dialogue page in the mirrored joblist, define the stockmodel that you

                                         want to use for the mirror. For this purpose, use the resulting stock model of the original
                                         joblist.
                                  3. Assign this stock model to the first job contained in the joblist and enable the Generate
                                         resulting stock option. For information on the definition of stock, see section Defining
                                         stockmodels.
                                  4. Check the job status of the jobs contained in the joblist and calculate the mirrored job
                                         list.

                               Mirror resulting stock
                                  Resulting stock is also mirrored (joblist > mirror) during mirroring if the Manufacturing param-
                                  eter > Copy function is activated.

                               Mirror stock chain
                                  A stock chain is also mirrored (joblist > mirror) during mirroring if the Manufacturing parame-
                                  ter > Copy function is activated.

           External tools

           Defining a tool

                                       An external database and a document database are available for managing tools. Tools
                                       stored in the external database are called external tools. Tools stored in the document data-
                                       base are called document tools.

           External tools

                           Standard tools for manufacturing tasks are stored in the external OPEN MIND tool database
                           with all data specific to them, such as tool number, machining type, etc. While defining tools
                           in the CAM programming, you can access the external OPEN MIND tool database at any
                           time to import the appropriate tools into the current document. The external OPEN MIND tool
                           database is displayed in the hyperMILL settings dialogue, Database dialogue page. This
                           may be an application database or a global/user database. Related information can also be
                           found in section Database and in the installation manual. For further information about the
                           external tool database.

           Document tools

                                       If the external database does not contain a tool you need, you can set it up as a new docu-
                                       ment tool in the current document (model file). Document tools are stored in list form on the
                                      Tools dialogue page of the hyperMILL browser in the Milling tools, Drilling tools and Turning
                                       tools sections.

                                       Click the Tools dialogue page with the right mouse button to show all available tabs of the
                                      hyperMILL browser. Enable the desired view options.

           Icons in the tool browser:

                           Hide tools (milling, drilling, turning tools) as a list in the browser.

                                 In the hyperMILL browser, switch to the Tools tab, highlight the tool and choose Export to
                                  tool database from the shortcut menu. If the ID of the tool already exists in the external data-
                                  base, a dialogue box (Constraint Violation) is shown; here, the ID highlighted in red must be

                                  components that are already present in the external database, these are not created again.
                                  The system checks whether an exact match of the parameters exists. If no exact match
                                  exists, the differences will be displayed in a dialogue box.

                          A password is requested when exporting to a password-protected database.
                          The database remains password- protected after a successful export. For a re-
                          export you need to re-enter the password.

           2D machining

           Prepare manufacturing geometry

           2D machining

                         You can select the following contours:

                         · lines, circles, polylines, splines, graphics loaded in omx format (Contour Milling, Pocket
                               Milling and Helical Drilling).

                         · Points (drill positions)

           Generate contours from toolpaths

                                       Curves extracted from previously calculated toolpaths can be used both as 2D contours and
                                       as help contours for 3D or 5-axis machining. For information on contour selection, see sec-
                                       tion Selecting elements.

           3D and 5-axis machining

                                       3D and 5-axis machining are based on a CAD model. This contains:
                                       · All areas to be machined.
                                       · Adjacent areas that are not to be machined for optimising machining and collision

                                              checking.
                                       · 2D or 3D lines, limitation contours (boundaries), leading curves for profiles.

           CAD model

                         The basis for the creation of an NC program for 3D machining is the CAD model created in
                         the CAD program and consisting of surfaces and/or surfaces and solids. It contains all areas
                         to be machined, as well as adjacent areas that are not to be machined in order to optimize
                         the machining procedure and the collision check. 2D or 3D lines used as limitation contours
                         or leading curves for profiles that are used in the course of the job definition.

           Surface gaps

                         Be sure that the model creation between adjacent surfaces or between surfaces and solids
                         do not contain large gaps. Large surface gaps can cause unwanted nose-diving of the cutter
                         in the course of machining. Gaps with a size below the used cutter radius are not critical.

           Overlapping surfaces

                                       Overlapping surfaces can result in unwanted rest material areas. These areas cannot be
                                       removed by the Automatic Rest Material cycle, as they are not the result of too large cutter
                                       diameters but of intersecting surfaces.

hyperMILL                               In the course of, and after creating machining cycles, the CAD model must nei-
                                        ther be moved nor changed in its position in space.

                         The machining area

      Stockmodel: general information

                                  A stockmodel in * STL format (Stereo Lithography) or * VIS (Visicut) can be defined for vari-
                                  ous machining operations. Stockmodels in the format *.VIS are recommended if you require
                                  greater accuracy and want to use the stockmodels that are generated in further stockmodel
                                  calculations (= stockmodel update).

                                         If an STL-formatted stockmodel is used for a stockmodel update, it has to be a
                                         closed solid. For information on how to generate closed solids for a stockmodel
                                         update, see section The Stock model dialogue box.

                                         Please note that hyperMILL cannot display stock files larger than 25 MB.

      Collision check

                                  The updated stock model is checked for collisions. This guarantees that both tracked and
                                  calculated stock models are always collision-checked.

      Defining stockmodels

                                 1. In the hyperMILL browser, go to the Jobs tab and double-click to open the required job-
                                         list. On the Model data dialogue page, select the Defined option and select a stock-
                                         model.

      2.                                 Click the icon to define a new stockmodel or

      3.                                 click the icon to modify an existing stockmodel.

      Alternatively, open the dialogue via the Job definition on the Setup dialogue page or using
      the New stock shortcut menu in the lower area of the hyperMILL browser on the Models dia-

      logue page.

      The Stock model dialogue box

      General

      Name/Comment: You only need to specify a name if the stockmodel is to be generated by
      extrusion or rotation. A descriptive comment can help you identify the stock model later.

      Mode

      In general, the following options are provided for generating stockmodels: Extrusion, Rota-
      tion, Surfaces, From job, File, Bounding geometry, From job chain.

      Extrusion: Define a (closed) stockmodel based on a contour and a (positive/negative) offset.
      It can be used for a stockmodel calculation and for a stockmodel update.

      Extrusion
      Resolution: Define the fineness of the curve resolution.

                                         Profile: Select contour.

              Offset 1/ Offset 2: Specify the height of the stockmodel in the Z direction (+/-).

      Mode
      Rotation: Define a (closed) stockmodel based on an (open) contour between the start and
      end point along the rotation axis. It can be used for a stockmodel calculation and for a stock-
      model update.

                                 define a cylindrical stockmodel, you can also specify the outer diameter and stock height.

      basis of the current polyhedron. After the calculation, the current stock size and minimum
      stock size are shown in the list display.
