      Stockmodel calculation via the shortcut menu
                                 In the hyperMILL browser, select the required joblist or job on the Jobs tab and use the Utili-
                                  ties > Create stockmodel function on the shortcut menu.
                                  The Stock model calculation dialogue box opens.

                                  Stock
                                  File: Select a closed stockmodel as the base stock.
                                  Click Path to select the required file in *.STL or *.VIS format. The path and file name are dis-
                                  played.
                                  From stockmodel: Select a defined stockmodel from the list or define a new stockmodel.

                                  Resulting model
                                  Click Path to select the required file in *.STL or *.VIS format. The path and file name are dis-
                                  played.
                                  STL/VIS: Specify the file format and tolerance for the calculation. For medium accuracy, a
                                  default resolution of 0.5 is adequate.
                                 Create stockmodel: Select this option to generate an entry in the hyperMILL browser for the
                                  stockmodel.
                                  Optimised stockmodel generation in 5X machining
                                  The prerequisite for optimised stock model generation is that the Cutting length parameter is
                                  defined in the tool definition of the underlying job. The following tool types are not subject to
                                  this requirement: Lollipop, Barrel cutter, T-Slot cutter and Woodruff cutter.
                                  The following applies to tapered and non-tapered tools: If no Cutting length is defined (value
                                  is 0), then the Tip length parameter is used. The following applies for ball and bullnose end-
                                  mills: if the Cutting length is smaller than the Corner radius, then the Corner radius is used.
                                  Fast stock calculation: Select this option if you require accelerated stock model generation.

                                         Models generated in this way do not show a realistic display of the milling
                                         results. The option should therefore be preferentially used with large models for
                                         which stockmodel generation would otherwise take a very long time.

                                         This option is not recommended when machining prismatic components (2.5D
                                         machining).

      Mirror stock

                    Each stock mirror is based on an existing stock and the definition of a mirror. You can either
                    mirror individual stockmodels in the stock browser or all the stockmodels of a joblist.

                    Mirroring individual stockmodels in the stock browser
                    To mirror an individual stock model:
                    1. Select the stockmodel that you want to mirror in the stock browser and choose the Mir-

                          ror stock function from the shortcut menu.
                    2. Specify the mirror you require or define a new mirror in the Mirror stock dialogue box.

                          For information on defining a mirror, please see section Mirror.
                    The mirrored stockmodel is displayed in the stock browser as follows: <Stock name[mir-
                    rored]>.

                    Mirroring all stock in a joblist
                    When you mirror a job list you also have the option of mirroring the related stocks.
                    To mirror all stock models in a job list:
                    1. Double-click the joblist entry and switch to the Mirror dialogue page.
                    2. Set the mirror function to Active and enable the Copy option for Manufacturing parame-

                          ters.
                    3. Answer the question Would you like stocks to be mirrored? with Yes.

3-44                                                           hyperMILL
           Basics                Prepare manufacturing geometry  3
           Defining stockmodels

                                 Mirrored stocks are created for all stocks used in the job list. These are displayed in the
                                 stock browser as follows: <Stock name[mirrored]>.

                                 Please note: Stocks in *.vis format (see Stock dialogue box > File) cannot be
                                 mirrored, as is the case for resulting stock, cast offset and compound stock.

                                 Stockmodels resulting from mirrors (mirrored stock) are not associative, in other
                                 words, if the original stock or the mirror plane changes, the stockmodels are not
                                 updated.

           Creating a compound stock
                                       If you want to machine several components together that each have a separate stockmodel,
                                       you can merge the stockmodels to form a Compound stock. A component can be machined
                                       and checked against the compound stock at the same time.
                                       To create a compound stock model:

                                       1. Right-click the stock browser and select New compound stock.

                                       2. Then select the required stocks in the list of available stock models and confirm your
                                              selection.

           Edit stock (split and clean)
                                       The Edit stock function can be used to further process stock resulting from the preceding
                                       stock calculation.

                                       1. Select the stockmodel that you want to process further and

                                       2. select the Edit stock function from the shortcut menu.
                                       Two functions are available in the Edit stock dialogue.
                                       The Split stock function splits the selected stockmodel into independent scopes arising as
                                       the result of a preceding machining job (see section Stockmodel calculation: prerequisite for
                                       the stockmodel update). Each scope is created as a new stock entry in the stock browser
                                       (Stock[Split1].vis, Stock[Split2].vis, and so on).
                                       The Clean stock function creates those stock scopes connected with the selected milling
                                       area as a new stock entry in the stock browser (Stock[Cleaned].vis).

           Create stock chain

                                       Use the Create stock chain function to create a resulting stock model for any job in a
                                       sequence of machining steps, based on the stock model of the preceding job and the tool-
                                       path of the current job. This function is available for joblists, any jobs in a joblist, an individual
                                       job or a compound job.
                                       Requirements: A start stockmodel must be present. All toolpaths of the jobs for which a
                                       stockmodel is to be created must have been calculated.
                                       Procedure:

                                      1. In the hyperMILL browser, select the jobs for which you want to create a stock chain.

                                       2. Select the Stock > Create stock chain function from the shortcut menu.

                                            hyperMILL creates a stock object in the stock browser for each of the selected jobs.

                                 3. To calculate the stockmodels, use the Stock > Calculate (update) function on the short-
                                       cut menu.

                                                 hyperMILL calculates the stockmodels for each of the generated stock objects. The
                                       stockmodels are indicated by a corresponding icon in the stock browser.

           Job list

           Structuring CAM projects

                                      Structure CAM projects in the hyperMILL browser.

           Job list

                        Uppermost administration level in the hyperMILL job browser. If projects have a simple struc-
                        ture, the joblist (work schedule) is usually sufficient for including all the jobs required to
                        machine a workpiece in the correct sequence. Several job lists can be assigned to one CAD
                        model. A joblist can be transferred to other CAD models that have a similar machining
                        sequence.

                        For information on joblists, see the following sections: Defining a joblist, Exporting/importing
                        a joblist and Joblist settings.

           Job

                        Lowermost administration level in the hyperMILL job browser. A hyperMILL job is a typical
                        machining step within a joblist. The following machining strategies are available for defining
                        jobs: Probing, Turning, Drilling, 2D Milling, 3D Milling, 5-axis Milling.

                        For general information on defining jobs, see section Defining a job.

                        For information on the various machining strategies, see the following sections: Probing,
                        Turning, Drilling, 2D machining, 3D machining and .

           Compound job

                                       Organise your joblists with compound jobs and clearly structure extensive CAM projects.
                                       Use compound jobs to structure transformations or assign individual transformations to sev-
                                       eral jobs. In contrast to joblists, which only permit mirrors, compound jobs also allow linear
                                       patterns and circular patterns in addition to mirrors.

                                       For information on compound jobs, see section Compound job.

           Linking job

                        Link jobs with each other in such a way that approach and retract movements for the entire
                        machining sequence and all linking movements between the individual jobs can be opti-
                        mised and monitored for collisions.

                        For information on linking jobs, see section Linking job.

           NC event

                        Structure your programming, independent of joblists and jobs, with control-specific functions
                        and commands that are forwarded directly to the postprocessor.

                        For information on the NC event, see section NC event.

           Defining a joblist

                                       A job list is automatically created when you call up a machining cycle for a job definition.
                                      In order to create another joblist in the hyperMILL browser, switch to the Jobs tab, right-click
                                       New > select Joblist.

                                       Joblist settings can be defined separately for each joblist. You must make the settings before
                                       you calculate the toolpaths.

                                       To edit, double-click the joblist or select the Edit function from the shortcut menu.

           Exporting/importing a joblist

                                       Save a joblist with all its parameters and settings in *.jst format and transfer to other CAD
                                       models.

                                       Advantages: Job archiving is independent of the drawings, fast programming of frequently
                                       occurring procedures, transfer of jobs to workpieces with the same drawing parts when
                                       machining sequence is the same.

      Linking job   A linking job contains other jobs that can be linked with each other in such a way that
                    approach and retract movements for the entire machining sequence and all linking move-
      Advantages
      Requirements  ments between the individual jobs can be optimised and monitored for collisions.

                    · Shortened machining times.
                    · Option to perform complex machining tasks.
                    · Improved product flexibility.

                    To combine multiple jobs into a linking job, the following conditions must be met:

                    2D/3D machining:
                    · All sub-jobs use the same tool.
                    · Only mirrors are permitted in the sub-jobs, not linear or circular patterns.

                    Turning jobs
                    · All sub-jobs use the same tool.
                    · Tool angle and tool orientation (Invert tool) are the same for all sub-jobs.
                    · The following combinations of the Cutting side parameter are possible in the sub-jobs

                          (see Strategy dialogue page):

                                   Cutting side       Outside            Inside            Plane
                                                      machining          machining         machining
                                   Outside machining
                                   Inside machining              x                  x                   x
                                   Plane Machining                                  x                   x
                                                                 x                                      x

                    3D/5X machining
                    · All sub-jobs use the same tool.
                    · Only mirrors are permitted in the sub-jobs, not linear or circular patterns.

                                   Drill machining cannot be combined with a linking job.

      Defining a linking job
                                  Right-click and select the New > Linking job / Linking job turning function.

      Add a linking job to a job

                                  Select the job(s) and then select the Add to linking job function on the shortcut menu or hold
                                  down the SHIFT key to move the jobs to the previously created linking job.

      Tool

                    All of the jobs combined into a linking job must contain the same tool. This also applies to 2D
                    mode and 5X mode.

      Parameters

                    Linking mode
                    The following linking methods may be used:
                    2D: Linking of 2D, 3D, drill jobs and turning jobs.

3-56                                                                                                            hyperMILL
           Basics                   3 Structuring CAM projects
           Defining a compound job

           5X: Linking of 3D and 5-axis jobs. It is also possible to link the 2D cycles Pocket Milling and
           Rest Machining in 5X mode.

           Rapids
           Specify the mode for the fast travel movements (rapids) of linked individual jobs.
           Skip first and last: Skip the first infeed movement and last retract movement of the individual
           sub-jobs.
           Keep all rapids: Keep all infeed and retract movements of sub-jobs within the linking job.

           Conditions
           Use min. dist. G0: The movements between the jobs are executed as a direct link between
           pairs of contour points in G1.
           Min. G0 distance: Distance between two machining areas that can be traversed ­ without
           tool contact ­ close to the surface with machining feedrate (G1).

           Clearance mode
           Planar / Radial: Specify how the toolpaths of the linked sub-jobs are linked. (1) Planar, (2)
           Radial.

hyperMILL  Linking job turning

                          As of Version 2017.1, in Linking job turning only jobs with tools which include
                          cutting point setup can be combined.
                         A linking job created with an earlier version of hyperMILL can be opened in Ver-
                          sion 2017.1. The linking job can be used if the consistency check is successful,
                          otherwise a new one must be created.
           Clearance
           Clearance radius X: radius for rapid tool movements in the X direction (1).
           Clearance plane Z: plane for rapid tool movements in the Z direction (2).
           Clearance distance: distance from the tool to the workpiece in the X direction during linking
           movements (3).

      Retract mode / Clearance
      Information on

                                   Clearance plane, clearance distance        in chap. Safety
                                   Production mode, axial and side clearance  in chap. Parameters

      Rapid smoothing

      Available for the Clearance distance retract mode. Enable the High speed option to activate
      Rapid smoothing (1).

      When machining in 5X mode, the linking movements are defined without abrupt changes of
      direction. The Smooth factor affects the shape of the smoothed movement as a ratio of the
      length of the connection line (2) to the required "height" of the movement (3). If the selected
      smooth factor potentially leads to a collision, the movement is automatically rendered colli-
      sion free.
      The Clearance distance retract mode must be active. The Linking movement with the Dis-
      tance angle limit (Setup dialogue page) must match the rapid smoothing.

      Multi-Axis Indexing

                                  Prerequisites for multi-axis indexing:
                                  · A machine with C axis and/or swivelling milling head (5-axis machining).
                                  · A drawing in the form of a 3D model.
                                  Programming always takes place in the G17 workplane:
                                  · Infeed in (negative) Z direction; Z axis is perpendicular to the machining side
                                  · Machining in the XY direction.
                                  Hence in multi-axis machining, you first have to define the coordinate system and the frame
                                  for each machining side. See the information in section NC system and frames.

                                                                                 Frame 3

           Tool Change Optimization
                                       Before generating the toolpaths, it is possible to optimize tool changes by sorting individual
                                       jobs according to different criteria. Macro job lists for holes must be expanded into individual
                                       jobs prior to tool change optimization. Use the Explode function on the shortcut menu for
                                       this.
                                       It is possible to sort by different criteria. Use the function your require from the joblist's short-
                                       cut menu.
                                       Sort by tool: Starting with the first tool in the expanded joblist (drilling cycles expanded into
                                       individual drillings), the jobs are sorted by tool number in ascending order, regardless of the
                                       frame in the job. The job sequence can also be sorted again manually.

                                       Sort by frame: The jobs are sorted by frame number. The job and tool sequence already
                                       defined for each frame is retained.

      Associative job copy

                                  Copy of a job in which all parameters correspond to the parameters of the original job. A job
                                  copy is associatively linked with the original job. If a parameter is changed in the original job,
                                  then this parameter will also change in the associative job copy. Parameters cannot be
                                  edited. Exception: transformations and contours.

      Creating an associative job copy
                                 Select the job in the joblist in the hyperMILL browser, right-click and select the Associative
                                  job copy function from the shortcut menu.
                                 Unlink the copied job and the original job: Select the copied job in the hyperMILL browser
                                  and select the Unlink associative copy function on the shortcut menu.

                               Overview
                                  All changes to the original job are summarised on this dialogue page.

                                   The associative job copy corresponds to the Copy option when using a mirror
                                   within a job definition (Transformation dialogue page).

                                   If you define a mirror on joblist level and have enabled the Copy option, a mir-
                                   rored associative copy of the original job is created from all jobs in the joblist
                                   with the parameters and settings of the original job.

                                       To deactivate the associative link between the original job and the associative job copy for

                                       versely, the parameter can now be edited directly in the job copy without affecting the origi-

      Collision check preparations

      Milling area, Turning area, Clamping area

      General information

                                  The Milling area or Turning area defines the area of the CAD model to be machined that is
                                  checked for collisions at the same time. The Fixture area is also checked for collisions; this
                                  includes those areas of the CAD model that are used to fix the part during machining.

                                 hyperMILL automatically generates a polyhedron model (3DF format) at a suitably high sur-
                                  face resolution (accuracy) for the Milling area, Turning area or Clamping area. For this pur-
                                  pose, the CAD model is subdivided into separate machining areas as required by the
                                  collision-checking function.

                                  All subareas of the model not inside the milling area, turning area or clamping area are not
                                  collision-checked. Inside the milling area/turning area, you can exclude areas from machin-
                                  ing (with the help of stop surfaces, for example).

                                  The machining area within the milling area is defined

                                  · by defining a boundary (possible for all 3D and 5X cycles) or

                                  · by defining milling surfaces (possible for the following cycles: 3D / 5X Profile Finishing,
                                         3D / 5X Z Level Finishing, 3D Z Level Shape Finishing and 3D / 5X Rest Machining).

      Define milling area              In the hyperMILL browser, double-click to open the joblist. On the Model data dialogue
                                  1.   page, select the Defined option and select a milling area.

      2.                               Click the icon to define a new milling area or

      3.                               click the icon to modify a milling area.

      Alternatively, open the dialogue via the job definition on the Setup dialogue page or using the
      New milling area shortcut menu in the hyperMILL browser on the Models dialogue page.

      The Milling area dialogue

                                  The dialogue consists of the Definition and Milling area dialogue pages.

                                  On the Definition dialogue page, define the elements that belong to the milling area. On the
                                  Milling area dialogue page, define the name and storage location for the milling area.

      Definition dialogue page

      Mode

      Define the mode for the milling area definition.

      Surface selection: hyperMILL automatically calculates the resolution for the selected milling
      areas depending on the machining tolerance. You can select a total of five surface groups
      with different resolutions and stock allowances.

      File: Click the Path button to select a 3DF or STL file.

                     You cannot use an external polyhedron file to define the milling area for the fol-
                     lowing cycles: 3D Profile Finishing, 5X Profile Finishing, 3D Z Level Finishing,
                     5X Z Level Finishing, 3D Automatic Rest Machining and 5X Rest Machining.

      Current selection
      Group name: Specify the Surface Group's name. A surface can only be allocated to one Sur-
      face Group. You assign the groups in the job definition.

           Collision checking with the hyperMILL Converter

                                      A collision check can either be performed by defining milling areas in the hyperMILL browser
                                      or using the hyperMILL Converter (polyhedron model). Model areas located on disabled lay-
                                       ers are not converted.
                                       You have to create at least one 3DF file (polyhedron model) for each CAD model. Areas with
                                       a different accuracy and different stock allowances can be entered in a 3DF file.
                                       Several 3DF files are required for CAD models that exceed the travel range of the machine
                                       and therefore need to be moved and reclamped during machining.
                                       Recommendation: Always convert as many surfaces and solids as possible in one process.
                                       The conversion of individual areas with a higher resolution should always include adjacent
                                       surfaces.

hyperMILL                                                                                     3-69
3 Basics                               Milling area, Turning area, Clamping area
         Collision check preparations

                                                  All 3DF files belonging to a model become invalid if the model changes position
                                                  in the coordinate system, is turned or scaled.

                                          Use the hyperMILL Converter menu to start the Converter.

      The hyperMILL Converter dialogue

                               Tab: Setup
                                  3DF file: Select the storage location for the 3DF file. Set the default storage location in the
                                 hyperMILL settings dialogue. The model name with the *.3df file extension is used as the file
                                  name.

                                  Resolution
                                  Mathematical resolution: Specify the resolution of curve segments in G1 lengths, by supply-
                                  ing the maximum chordal height. Set the surface resolution to be somewhat finer than the
                                  dimensional accuracy required in production.
                                  Recommendation: roughing 0.5 to 0.1 mm, finishing 0.05 to 0.01 mm, HSC machining 0.005
                                  to 0.001 mm.
                                  Max. facet length: Controls the maximum facet length within the 3DF model. Can be defined
                                  for each group in group definitions.

                     If a sufficiently precise definition cannot be achieved using the Mathematical
                     resolution function (for example, with surfaces that are only slightly curved), a
                     limit can be set.

      Selection options
      All solids, All surfaces, All: Select one of these options if no user-specific selection for con-
      version is to be used and the selected areas are all to be converted with the same mathe-
      matical resolution.
      User-defined

                        Surfaces: Select solids or surfaces to be converted. The same mathematical
      resolution applies to all selected surfaces/solids.

           Milling area, Turning area, Clamping area

           Groups
           Group definition: Select this option if you want to convert areas with different mathematical
           resolutions and/or different stock allowances, in order, for example, to define different colli-
           sion and protected areas. A coarse resolution is sufficient for roughing areas. A finer resolu-
           tion should be defined for different fine machining processes.

                          The group definition is relevant for: Profile Finishing, Equidistant Finishing, Iso
                          Machining, Free Path Milling.

           Groups
           A 3DF file can contain up to five groups of surfaces and/or solids with different mathematical
           resolutions and different stock allowances. A surface can only be allocated to one Surface
           Group.

                             Surfaces: Select the solids or surfaces to be converted.
           Mathematical resolution: Surface resolution of the model.
           Allowance: Remaining material on the workpiece. If more than five groups are required to
           machine a model, create the respective number of 3DF files with different names. You
           assign the 3DF files in the job definition.
           Max. facet length: Maximum facet length of the surfaces within a group.

           Tab: Options

           Mode of conversion
           New 3DF file: The selected objects will be converted at the set mathematical resolution and
           a new 3DF file will be created.
           Add to existing 3DF file: The selected objects will be converted at the set mathematical reso-
           lution and added to the existing 3DF file. In this way, several areas with different mathemati-
           cal resolutions can be combined into one 3DF file and later modifications to the model can
           be included.
           Does not apply to group definitions.

           Save existing 3DF file
           Yes: When adding surfaces, the existing 3DF file that the current conversion process is
           going to expand can be backed up by saving it under a different name.
           Save as: Select the path and file name for saving the existing 3DF file.
           No: An existing 3DF file is saved under an existing path and file name with the addition of the
           new surfaces/solids to be converted.

hyperMILL                                                                           3-71
3 Basics                                                  Prerequisites for calculating toolpaths
         Calculating tool paths and simulating machining

      Calculating tool paths and simulating machining

                                  Prerequisites, information and options for calculating toolpaths.
                                  Deleting, reading and updating toolpaths.

      Prerequisites for calculating toolpaths

                                  1. Correct job sequence: The sequence of jobs in the job list matches the machining
                                         order.

                                  2. Correct job definition: Before calculating a toolpath check jobs that have an error or
                                         warning notification. Use the Messages function on the shortcut menu for this. If these
                                         are not manually checked, all messages will be displayed prior to the toolpath calcula-
                                         tion.

                                  3. For 3D and 5-axis machining, a milling area must be present in order to calculate a tool-
                                         path.

                                                  Jobs whose machining ended with an error should only be post processed after
                                                  an extensive check.

      General settings

                                  The system of units that has been set is valid for the toolpath calculation. Changes to the
                                  measurement system are not permitted after the jobs, tools and frames have been defined.
                                 Relevant settings for calculating toolpaths are specified in the hyperMILL Settings dialogue,
                                  on the Calculation tab. See the information in section Document.

      Joblist-specific settings

                                  The following are defined on a job-specific basis:
                                  · Name and path of toolpaths, see the information in section Setup.
                                  · NCS (program zero point), see the information in section Define NC system.
                                  · Original stock (if necessary) and model, see the information in section Model data.
                                  · Postprocessor-specific settings, see the information in section Postprocessor.

                                                  The NCS must be identical for all jobs within a job list. If the NCS is moved, pre-
                                                  viously calculated jobs become invalid.

      Job-specific settings

                                  The frame is set on a job-specific basis. See the information in section Frame.
                                  The display colours and sizes for the toolpath and collision output can also be set on a job-
                                  specific basis.

      Calculate toolpaths

                                 Either directly in the job definition (for an individual job) or in the hyperMILL browser (for an
                                  individual job, multiple jobs or all the jobs in a joblist).
                                  In the job definition

                                         Calculate: The main purpose of this method of creating a toolpath is to enable a quick
                                  check of the work-through of an individual job.
                                 In the hyperMILL browser
                                  Select the required jobs or joblist and then select the Calculate function from the shortcut
                                  menu.

3-72                                                                                               hyperMILL
           Basics            Calculating tool paths and simulating machining  3
           Delete Toolpaths

                             When calculating/updating one or more linking jobs, the system displays a mes-
                             sage asking whether you want to recalculate all sub-jobs. If you choose No,
                             only the linking job, and not its sub-jobs, are recalculated.

                             Prior to the calculation, the messages stored for the jobs or joblists to be calculated are dis-
                             played.

                             Ignore: Ignore the messages and calculate the job.

                             Ignore all: Ignore all messages and calculate all jobs.

                             Cancel: Cancel the calculation.

                             Edit: Open the dialogue (Job/Joblist) and edit the settings.
                             During the calculation, the message window displays information on the status of the calcu-
                             lation. The calculation can be controlled as follows:

                             Cancel the toolpath calculation.

                             Stop the toolpath calculation.

                             Continue the toolpath calculation.

           Displaying Toolpaths

                                       If specified in the job list settings, the generated toolpaths are continuously added to the
                                       CAD file.

           Temporary Toolpaths

                                       For some machining cycles, temporary toolpaths are displayed initially that correspond to the
                                       calculation sequence. When job calculation is complete, the final machining strategy is dis-
                                       played accordingly.

           Collisions

                             If the system identifies collisions while calculating the toolpaths, they are also displayed
                             graphically.

           Information on Calculation

                                       Information on the calculation process is displayed in the window that appears at the same
                                       time. In addition, depending on your job list settings, various messages can be viewed in the
                                       report file.

                                       The report file (*.rep) is stored by default in the global working space. For further information,
                                       see section Document.

           Delete Toolpaths

                                              Delete all toolpaths using the hyperMILL Delete toolpaths menu or the Toolpaths >
                                       Delete all shortcut menu.
                                       Delete the toolpaths of one or several jobs via Toolpaths > Delete on the shortcut menu.

           Read toolpaths

                                       Read toolpaths and display in the CAD system.
                                       You must distinguish between the following:
                                       1. Reading of toolpaths for a job (for example, after deletion) via the Toolpaths > Read

                                              shortcut menu.

hyperMILL                                                                     3-73
3 Basics                                                  Update calculated toolpaths
         Calculating tool paths and simulating machining

      2.  Reading of any toolpaths (for example, for purposes of analyses) via the Read

          toolpath hyperMILL menu. Open the dialogue from the shortcut menu of a joblist or job.

      Toolpath properties

      Use job settings: Take the colours for G0 and G1 movements and the tool axis from the job.
      Disable this option if other colours should be used. Set the display of the tool axis (Off,
      Small, Normal, Large).

      Show clipped paths: Show the parts of the toolpaths that are in collision (clipped). Specify
      the colour for clipped areas.

      Update calculated toolpaths

                                  Changes to the feedrate, spindle RPM or comment do not require a full recalculation of the
                                  job for the following cycles.
                                  - all 3D cycles except Form Pocket
                                  - all 5X cavity cycles except Z-level roughing and cutting edge
                                  - all 5X surface cycles
                                  - 5X Blade Top Milling
                                  - 5X MB Point Milling
                                  To change the spindle RPM or feedrate of the tool, choose one of the following options:

                                  1. Change the value for this job only directly on the Tool tab of the job definition. To do so,
                                         select the Unlink command from the Spindle RPM / Feedrate shortcut menu in the Cut-
                                         ting profile section. Enter the value directly into the dialogue.

      2. Change the value for the tool in the Technology tab of the tool definition.   Click on

          the icon to open the Edit tool dialogue and enter the desired changes on the Technol-

          ogy tab.

      Then update the toolpath file in the hyperMILL browser using the Update shortcut menu.

      Information on calculated toolpaths

                                  Information is available for the following via a quickinfo (tooltip): frame, job ID, job name,
                                  comment, job type, linked job, tool ID and tool name.

                                 Configure the information displayed on the hyperCAD menu File > Options > Tooltip content.
                                  To do this, move the elements from the Available TAGs area to the Tooltip content area.

      Functions on the shortcut menu

                                 The following hyperMILL functions are available on the shortcut menu of a calculated tool-
                                  path:

                                  Internal simulation: Start the internal simulation and simulate the calculated job.
                                  Internal machine simulation: Start the internal machine simulation and simulate the calcu-
                                  lated Job.

                                  Hide: Hide the toolpath.

                                  Show G0 only: Only display G0 movements of the toolpath.

                                  Show G1 only: Only display G1 movements of the toolpath.

                                  Show all: Display the complete toolpath.

      The Toolpath Edit cycle

                                  The Toolpath Edit cycle makes it possible to delete certain sections in already calculated
                                  toolpaths easily and safely using a boundary and to link the remaining parts together.

                                  All linking paths and any arising approach and retract macros are automatically checked for
                                  collisions. The function is available for all 3D cycles (except Arbitrary Stock Roughing and
                                  Form Pocket) and all 5X Cavity Cycles (except Z Level Roughing and Cutting Edge).

      Axis coordinates
      The coordinates are displayed in relation to the NCS of the job list. If the Frame option is

      Material Removal Simulation
      The material removal simulation is used to simulate complete material removal for the
      machining step (job) in question, based on the currently calculated or assigned stock.

             Start the material removal simulation. In this procedure, hyperMILL analyses whether a
      previous calculation has generated a resulting stock model and uses this as the starting
      stock model. If no stock model is present for one or more previous calculations, the Stock
      calculation dialogue will appear first before the removable material simulation begins.

      In the Setup area, first define the Stock and the Tolerance to be used in the material removal
      simulation.
      Activate the Fast stock calculation option if you want to accelerate the stock generation.
      Please note that models generated in this way do not show a realistic display of the milling
      results. This option should therefore be preferentially used with large models for which stock-
      model generation would otherwise take a very long time.
      This option is not recommended when machining prismatic components (2.5D Machining).
      Furthermore, you can define in the Jobs to calculate section, for all jobs for which no result-
      ing stockmodel was calculated, whether these should be calculated prior to the stock
      removal simulation and then used as the starting stockmodel. To do so, activate the corre-
      sponding job in the list of displayed jobs.

                     Show the model defined in the joblist.

                     Create a cut through the stockmodel at the current tool position.

                     Open the Measure dialogue.

           rest material display. The rest material is displayed in four steps that are defined on the basis
           of the value of the maximum permissible rest material. Example: maximum rest material = 1.
           First step = <0.25, second step = < 0.5, third step < 0.75, fourth step > 0.75.

           ent (yellow > green > blue) in the lower left area of the dialogue box.
           The defined Allowance is represented by the yellow colour and the defined Max. rest mate-
           rial by the colour blue.
           Comparison tolerance: Sum of Model and Stock tolerance (Simulation tolerance).
           Model tolerance: Accuracy of the model used.
           Simulation tolerance: Accuracy of the material removal simulation.

                 Measuring

           the first point. Then, left-click again to specify the second point. The measurement results
           are shown as:

           Info two faces

           Surface distance (2): Distance between the first clicked surface (here B) to the second
           clicked point.
           Surface distance point 2 (3): Distance between the first clicked point to the second clicked
           point (here A).
           Point distance (4): Distance between two clicked points.

      components (model, stockmodel, fixture, and so on) on the machine model.

      Output project
      Define the directory and name of the VERICUT project file (*.vcproject). This file is used for
      information exchange between hyperMILL and VERICUT. OPEN MIND supports VERICUT
      from version 7.0 up.
      Generate NC files: While creating the VERICUT project data, the postprocessor run is auto-
      matically triggered and an NC file is generated.
      Generate project data: Generate the VERICUT project data without subsequently starting
      VERICUT.
      Run VERICUT: Generate the VERICUT project data and start VERICUT.

      Output folder
      Define the directory for generating the COLLISION SAFEGUARD project data.
      Project ID: Define the required project ID.
      Project name: Displays the name of the COLLISION SAFEGUARD project (directory name).
      The project that is generated contains the following elements:
      · NC file
      · Fixture file: .stl
      · Model file: .stl
      · Stock file: .stl
      · Tool file: .tls
      · Project file: .vcproject
      Generate project data: Generates the COLLISION SAFEGUARD project data.

           Extract circles and arcs

                                       Only hyperCAD. This utility can be used to extract circles and arcs from contours (for
                                 example, boundaries and holes of surfaces and solids). The extracted circles and arcs can
                                 be used for drilling cycles and for circular pockets. The dialogue box is divided into the fol-
                                 lowing sections:

                                 Selection
                                 Curves/Surfaces: Use these buttons to select curves and surfaces (including solid faces) in
                                 which circles and arcs should be recognised.

                                 Recognise
                                 Circles/Arcs: Here you can specify whether circles and/or arcs should be recognised.
                                 Tolerance: Specify the tolerance that should be applied.
                                 Coordinate system: Specify the coordinate system. The circles generated are stored on
                                 planes parallel to the XY plane belonging to the specified coordinate system.

                                 Filter
                                 Use filter: The diameters for circles and arcs to be recognised can be limited here.
                                 Use extended filter: It is possible to combine two filters.

                                 Result
                                 Here, you specify how the recognition results are to be stored (i.e., the newly created circles
                                 and/or arcs).
                                 Insert height > Absolute: Specify an absolute value for the insert height interactively in the
                                 CAD model. If this value is zero, all the generated circles and arcs will reside on the XY
                                 plane of the selected coordinate system.

           CAD Utilities

                                      Prepare CAD models for machining with hyperMILL.

           hyperCAD

                           The following CAD utilities are available for hyperCAD:

           Placing erroneous surfaces on layer

                                     hyperMILL runs a plausibility check on the selected surfaces before each milling
                           area recognition. If one or more surfaces with errors are recognised, you can use this func-
                           tion to save the found surfaces with errors to a layer.

                           If you start the function, the Surface error window is opened, which shows all surfaces with
                           errors. Enter the layer number or layer name on which the recognised surfaces are saved in
                           the lower right input field.

                           Click the Move & Exit button to save the surfaces on the defined layer and to end the func-
                           tion. To analyse the surfaces with errors, show only this layer. You can repair the surfaces
                           (for example, reconstruct) or remove them from the milling area if they are not relevant to
                           CAM editing.

           Close surfaces

                                     You can use this function to close the (sub)surfaces of a CAD model whose bounda-
                           ries lie within one surface. If you call up the function, the newly generated surfaces have the
                           colour that is set to active in the CAD programme and are stored on the first available empty
                           layer.

           Split Solids

                                                  Use the Split Solid function to split solids along curves. The resulting solids remain
                                       as single solids.

                                       First select the Solid to be cut. Then select the curve(s) that you want to use as cutting
                                       edges. Finally, all you need to do is select the solid surface (base surface) whose normal will
                                       define the cutting direction (direction: Normal). If you do not want to use the surface normal
                                       of the base surface as the cutting direction, you can also define the cutting direction via Two
                                       points. You can also define colours and layers for the resulting solids (optional).

           Change entity properties

                                     You can use this function to change the properties (layer and colour) of any elements
                           (surfaces and curves). First, select the elements (surfaces/curves) that you want to change.
                           Then select the properties to be changed (Layer, Colour or both) and close the dialogue box.

           Thicken planes

                                                   This function allows you to increase the thickness of any planes in a CAD model.
                                       Under Input, first select the kind of object definition. You can either thicken all planes of a
                                       certain colour or layer or select the planes manually (option: Select). Afterwards, define the
                                       height and output layer of the plane to be changed.

           Export parameter

hyperMILL                            With this function, you can change parametrised CAD models by exporting a param-
                           eter list. Choose a path and file name in order to save the content of a parameter list. Conse-
                           quently, the name and value of each parameter are saved.

       Produce electrodes

                                  hyperCAD-S electrode offers functions for designing, managing, programming and docu-
                                   menting complete tool electrodes with electrode holders and with product manufacturer
                                   information for the die-sinking EDM with the spark erosion behaviour. Fully program elec-
                                  trodes for milling based on hyperMILL with the electrode feature and macro programming.

       Preparing milling NC programming

                                   Various prepared tasks are to be performed. Prepare the electrode holder library. Determine
                                   default settings. Read in the electrode colour pallet and assign the electrode colours. Design
                                   and map the electrodes and output the electrode reports. Detailed information on this work
                                  can be found in the hyperCAD-S software documentation.

       Defaults for NC programming

                                  In the hyperCAD-S dialogue File > Options > Electrode options > Reference with Electrode
                                   name and Increment for names, define the name of the electrode geometry and of the milling
                                   project for producing an electrode.

                                   Example:

                             Electrode name  Increment for names  Derived electrode geometries /
                             Electrode       10                   milling projects

                                                                  Electrode_10.hmc
                                                                  Electrode_20.hmc

       Transferring production-related data to hyperMILL

                                   Production-related information such as undersize, stock size, material, areas of electrode
                                   geometry and the position reference are mapped during the electrode design. The informa-
                                  tion in hyperMILL is evaluated and provided for programming.

       NC Programming

                                   NC Programming is performed semi automatically. Joblist, milling area, stock, fixture and
                                   electrode feature are automatically created in the New > Electrode milling dialogue in the
                                   shortcut menu of the job browser. The linking of electrode feature and job, the creation of
                                   macros and the linking of electrode features and macro are intuitively guided by the user.

       Milling project directory
                                  In the hyperCAD-S dialogue File > Options > Electrode options > Directories, define the mill-
                                   ing project directory. In the milling project directory, the data for NC programming is saved,
                                   among other items:

                                   · the mapped electrode(s) (1, 2): [Electrode_10.hmc], in subdirectory [Electrode_10],
                                          [Electrode_20.hmc] in subdirectory [Electrode_20],
                                        (the data is generated with the hyperCAD-S function Electrodes > Map and mill or Elec-
                                          trodes > Mill),

                                   · for each electrode geometry: the milling area [Electrode10_Milling area], in sub-direc-
                                          tory [3DF], the stock [Electrode10_stock] in sub-directory [STOCK] and the clamp [Elec-
                                          trode10_clampl] in sub-directory [CLAMP]
                                        (the data is generated to activate the hyperMILL functions Milling area, Stock and
                                          Clamp in the Electrode milling dialogue).

                             (4) Reference zero clamping system
                             Based on the selected zero point position, zero point and frame are created as elements in
                             the hyperMILL browser.

                                Macros
                                   Available macros and selected macros are displayed on the dialogue page. To use a macro
                                   during programming, move this to the Selected macros area. Generate the required macro
                                   beforehand. This is carried out based on the generated electrode feature using the New
                                   macro from feature function.
                                   Use the Allow multiple apply function to enable multiple use of feature-based macros.
                                   For information on creating a feature-based macro, see section Creating feature-based mac-
                                   ros.

                                Setup
                                   On the dialogue page, the milling project directory is displayed for producing the electrode.
                                   With comments provided, production-related information is offered for the jobs. The Calcu-
                                   late function is used to create toolpaths.

                                   Save file
                                   The milling project directory is displayed.

                                   Job list
                                   Comment 1-10: Create optional comments. Comments are copied into the joblist created as
                                   joblist comments.

                                             Enter the comments using a text editor. Each line in the text editor corresponds to a
                                   joblist comment.

                                   Options
                                   Calculate: The toolpaths are calculated.

       Joblist and electrode feature

                                             A Joblist and Electrode feature are created if the Electrode milling dialogue is closed
                                   with OK. In the joblist, the functions stock, model and clamp are activated and the previously
                                   created elements are selected.
                                   In the electrode feature, the production-related elements of the electrode geometry, such
                                   erosion area, extension, etc. and the stock geometry are saved as feature parameters.

                                       · The Electrode milling dialogue is closed with OK

                                       variables dialogue (shortcut menu of the job browser) and can be used for programming in

                                       Spark gaps
                                       Check the size of the spark gap for machining tasks Roughing, Re-roughing, Pre-finishing
                                       and Finishing and adjust, if necessary. The size of the spark gap corresponds to the under-
                                       size in NC production (negative value).
                                       User variables in the CAD parameter and milling parameter areas are only displayed and
                                       cannot be changed.

   The advantages of feature technology

Feature and macro technology

            The advantages of feature technology

                                               Feature technology processes geometry information present in the CAD model for CAM pro-
                                               gramming in a way that significantly reduces programming effort. In addition to the assigned
                                               geometry, features also contain information relevant to manufacturing, such as tolerance
                                               values or fits.
                                               The automatic derivation of manufacturing geometries makes it possible to transfer data
                                               directly from a feature to the job definition (Feature Job Connector) for use across jobs and
                                               job lists.
                                               Furthermore, Customised Process Features make it possible to define company standards
                                               for similar geometries, thus increasing programming automation even further. In this pro-
                                               cess, work processes are defined and stored as technology macros, which can be applied to
                                               similar machining tasks.
                                               Feature technology provides you with enormous potential to increase efficiency and save
                                               time in manufacturing.

            User interface

                                               The user interface of the feature module comprises
                                             · The Feature browser (Feature tab in the hyperMILL browser) with representation of the

                                                      feature lists and features,
                                               · The Feature editor (Feature dialogue) for defining feature parameters and
                                               · The Feature job connector (Feature dialogue page of the job definition) for selecting

                                                      and using features in a job.

              The feature browser

                                             The feature tab in the hyperMILL browser is known as the Feature Browser. The Feature
                                               Browser comprises
                                               · The top range with feature lists and shortcut menu functions (1),
                                               · The bottom range with feature and shortcut menu functions (2),
                                               · A toolbar with filter functions and functions to control the visibility of features (3).

                 Control the visibility and representation of features                                                      hyperMILL

     The Feature Editor

                                 The dialogue for defining feature parameters is called the feature editor. The feature editor

     The Feature job connector

                                 The Feature dialogue page of the job definition is known as the Feature job connector. It is
                                 used to link features with the current job and comprises
                                 · the icons to select features (1),
                                 · the top area with the list of linked features (2),
                                 · the bottom area with representation of the feature parameters (3).

     Connected features
     Features linked to the job are listed in the Feature Job Connector. The number of features is
     displayed.

                             Click on the icon to open the Select feature dialogue in order to link a
                             feature with the current job.

                             Features which should be used in the jobs can be moved to the right win-
                             dow by double-clicking or clicking on the button (1).

                             Features which should not be used in the jobs can be moved to the left
                             window by double-clicking or clicking on the button (2).

     Feature derived: Production-related feature parameters are represented in the bottom area
     of the Feature Job Connector. A feature parameter, whose status is set to active, is used in
     the job definition for calculation purposes. If the status is inactive, the parameter is not used.

      General information

                                  Define the Name for the feature. The type is set automatically.
                                  If required, define a Name for the feature class and structure the work with feature classes
                                  and features. Features which are used to edit an area of the model, can be combined in a
                                  Feature class and quickly selected and re-used when creating Macros using filters.
                                  To allocate a feature to a Feature class, enter the name of the feature class in the Feature
                                  class line. The name is freely definable and may reflect a typical machining sequence, for
                                  example. It is displayed in the feature browser and in the macro database.

      Example

      Simple Hole               <D5 Through      Multi-Axis Indexing 1>
      Feature name              <Parameter name  Feature class name>

           To allocate a feature to a Feature class, open the Select feature class dialogue and
      select the respective feature class. The feature type and use of the feature are displayed. If
      the Check feature type option is enabled, only feature types are displayed, which correspond
      to the currently selected feature.

                                If the feature is linked to a macro, the link is saved in the macro database. This
                                allows the Feature class parameter to be used as a filter independently of the
                                model when using macros.

                                This function therefore makes it easier to reuse features and feature classes
                                that are already defined.

      Generic Hole

                    Generic holes are universally applicable, from Simple Holes right through to complex coun-
                    terbored holes. Generic holes are structured according to manufacturing elements and
                    related properties.
                    Generic Holes were developed to replace in the medium term the Simple Hole, Sink Hole
                    and Free defined Hole features.

                                   Generic Holes offer significant advantages when using macro machining. In
                                   particular, when setting up a macro database with macro rules, OPEN MIND
                                   recommends exclusive use of Generic Holes.

           Customised Process Feature (CPF)
                                       Using a customised process feature, recurring machining tasks can be resolved largely auto-
                                       matically by linking relevant geometric information with a machining mode and technology
                                       parameters and manually defining the structure of a CPF.

                                    Prerequisites for use
                                       To use a CPF for machining models from a family of parts that are designed in a similar way,
                                       the following conditions should be fulfilled:
                                       1. The models have common geometric characteristics.
                                       2. The machining sequence is specified in the job list.
                                       3. Geometric elements of the CPF are linked with job parameters.

hyperMILL                                                                                         4-27
4 Feature and macro technology                                    General information
         FeatureCatalogue

      Example pocket machining

      1. Using common geometric characteristics: Profiles (1), Bottom plane (2) and Side sur-
            faces (3), other pockets of a part family, such as hexagonal or octagonal, flat or deep,
            small or large pockets, can also be described.

      2. Machining sequence in the job list:

      Machining step                                        Job/Cycle
      1. Roughing the pocket                                3D Arbitrary Stock Roughing
      2. Finishing the hub surface                          3D Arbitrary Stock Roughing
                                                            (Plane level detection > Optimised - planes only)
      3. Finishing the side walls                           3D Profile Finishing

      3. Assigning the geometry elements (CPF) to job parameters:

      Geometry element (CPF)                                Job parameters
      1. Orientation                                        Frame
      1. and 2. surface group                               Milling surfaces (hub and side surfaces)
      1. Profile group                                      Boundary (hub surface boundary)
      Milling area/stock                                    Milling area/stock

      Defining the CPF structure

      2. Right-click and select New > Customised Process Feature > Machining object.

            The Customised Process Feature dialogue opens.
      3. Name the CPF according to the machining planned.
      4. Specify the CPF elements to be used in the Select area.
      5. Select 1 for Orientation number.

      6. Click the icon to display further options. Leave the default settings Frame for Usage
            in job and W (`write') for Mode.

      Icons in the Customised process feature dialogue box:

                                Insert graphic from a file

                                Paste graphic from the clipboard

           Using the CPF
           The aim of using the CPF is to automate extensive machining processes. Before the CPF
           can be used, the data from a CAD model must be assigned. This link between the CAD
           model and the CPF supplies a job with the required information when using the CPF.

           Linking the CPF to CAD data
           To link CAD data of a model to the CPF, proceed as follows:
           1. Right-click the feature browser and open the CPF dialogue.
           2. Select New > Customised Process Feature > [CPF name]. A corresponding entry is

                 created in the lower part of the feature browser [CPF name] and all previously defined
                 geometry elements are displayed in the CPF dialogue.
           3. For Orientation 1, select the required Frame for machining.
           4. Select the hub and side surfaces of the pocket for Surfaces 1 and 2.
           5. Select the limit of the hub surface for Profiles 1.

                                                                                                                                               4-29
4 Feature and macro technology  General information
         FeatureCatalogue

      6. Finally, define the Milling area and Stock.

      If all parameters of the CPF are clearly named and the corresponding data from the CAD
      model assigned, the CPF can be used in the job definition. The job and CPF are linked in the
      Feature Job Connector.

      Using the CPF in the job definition

      Usage of a defined CPF using the example of rouging a pocket. This is based on the
      assumption that

      · all the jobs required for machining are created in the joblist in the correct sequence and

      · all job parameters, which are not to be taken from the CPF, are correctly defined.

      To use a CPF in the job definition, proceed as follows:

      1. In the job definition, switch to the Feature dialogue page and select the corresponding
            CPF.

      2. The cycle recognises that the profile (boundary) as well as frame, milling area and stock
            can be used from the CPF for roughing and automatically sets these to active. At the
            same time, the corresponding parameters are "greyed out" in the job definition and can-
            not therefore be machined manually.

      3. Deactivate CPF parameters that are not used in the job definition. To do this, double-
            click the entry in the lower area of the Feature job connector. The status changes from
            Active to Deactivated.

      4.                        The job definition is free of errors and warnings and the job can be calculated.

      Re-using the CPF in the new CAD model

      To reuse the CPF and the machining sequence with modified CAD data, proceed as follows:

      1. Save the CAD file without the current model. Only save the joblist, jobs and the CPF as
            the template file.

      2. Use the hyperCAD menu Insert > From file to insert the new CAD model, which
            includes all geometric elements used in the CPF.

      (1) Model for the assignment of elements in the CPF and (2) shows the use of the CPF in the
      job definition.

                     If you have defined filters in the CPF, the model must be constructed according
                     to the filter definition so that the data can be read correctly.

      3. Select the CPF in the feature browser, right-click and select Update filter definition(s).
            All elements of the CPF for which filters are defined are updated. This also applies to fil-
            ters that were not directly defined in the CPF (such as filters for the milling area).

      By updating the filter, the data is read from the model and transferred to the jobs via the
      CPF.

      Generating features

                                  A feature can be created as follows:

                                  1. In the job definition by selecting contours, boundaries, milling surfaces, stop surfaces or
                                         additional surfaces. In the first step, define the geometric element, then call the function
                                         (Create Contour Feature, Create Surface Group Feature, Create Strategy Curve Fea-
                                         ture).

                                  2. Manually in the feature browser and feature editor. See the information in section Man-
                                         ually in the Feature browser / Feature editor.

                                  3. Automatically in the feature browser by copying hole features from a CAD model using
                                         Feature Mapping (Hole).

                                  4. Automatically in the feature browser through user-friendly copying of features (holes,
                                         pockets, planes, boundaries) from a CAD model using Feature Recognition.

      Manually in the Feature browser / Feature editor

                                 For manual creation of a feature in the hyperMILL browser, switch to the Feature tab, in the
                                  top area of the feature browser select the desired feature via the shortcut menu and in the
                                  Feature editor define the parameters required. See chap. The Feature Editor for information
                                  on the feature editor.

      Feature Mapping (Hole)

                                 Automatic assignment of geometric feature information from a CAD model (solid) to a hyper-
                                  MILL feature.

                                 To start feature mapping in the hyperMILL browser, switch to the Feature tab and in the top
                                  area of the feature browser in the shortcut menu select the Feature Mapping (hole) function.

      General settings

                        Tolerance: Specifies the accuracy level for transferring the geometric data from the CAD
                        model.

      Options

                        Check slot: Enable this option if slot recognition is required.

                        Slot tolerance: Tolerance for the axial distance between concentric part-holes of the same
                        diameter. See the information in section Single Hole Recognition.

                        Slot as hole element: A slot is regarded as part of a hole. Part-holes are combined into one
                        multi-step freely defined hole, whereby the slot area is defined as a through (B).
                        If this option is disabled, part-holes that go through a slot (depending on the defined toler-
                        ance) are recognised either as Simple Holes or Sink Holes (A).

                        (A) Function not enabled: (1) Simple Hole, (2) Simple Hole.

                        (B) Function enabled: freely defined hole, consisting of three steps: cylinder (1), through (2),
                        cylinder (3).
