           More Options

                         Offset to bottom: Features based on through-holes are created with the bottom offset speci-
                         fied here.

                         Use feature list: if this option is enabled, the drillings are saved as features in the existing
                         feature lists. Feature assignment is in reference to the frames assigned to feature lists. Fea-
                         ture lists that do not contain frames are ignored.

                         Frame creation mode

                         2D: A feature list is created for each hole orientation and a frame is assigned to each feature
                         list.

                         5X: All recognised features are combined into one feature list, but a frame is not assigned to
                         this list.

                         Mixed: If several holes have the same orientation, a feature list is created for this orientation
                         and a frame is assigned to the feature list. All other holes are combined into one feature list,
                         but a frame is not assigned to this list.

                         Split by diameter: In the case of multi-step holes, the diameter of the individual steps is taken
                         into account when arranging the features in the feature list (B). The machining direction (4) is
                         included.

                         If, from the direction of machining, the diameter of a subsequent step is greater than the
                         diameter of the preceding step, the hole is divided into two or more Simple (3) and Sink
                         Holes (2).

                         If the split by diameter function is disabled (A), this multi-step hole is included in the feature
                         list as a freely defined hole (1).

4 Feature and macro technology  Manually in the Feature browser / Feature editor
         Generating features

      Check machinability: If this function is enabled (B), only holes that are in accessible areas
      are recognised as a feature and displayed. In figure (A), the function is disabled; (1) shows
      the machining direction.

      Use colour table
      When importing feature information from a CAD model, hyperMILL also recognises feature
      properties such as thread, ISO fits or feature classes if these are defined in a colour table.
      hyperMILL evaluates the assignment of colour information to feature properties when gener-
      ating features and incorporates the corresponding parameter directly in the feature. At the
      same time, this parameter is also included in the feature name and is thus available for
      selection when creating and using macros.
      To read information from a colour table, enable the Use colour table option in the Feature
      Mapping dialogue box, select a file (in *.xml format) (Select colour table) and confirm your
      entries. Note regarding content of the XML file: In order for hyperMILL to be able to correctly
      recognise the Thread and Fits feature properties, they must be defined as follows:
      Example:

       <Color_Table>

         <Color_Machining_Definition R="128" G="64" B="64"
       FitDesignation="H7" ThreadDesignation="Mx" FeatureClass="Special FC"
       UseThreadNominalDiameter="1"/>

       <Color_Machining_Definition R="128" G="0" B="128"
       FitDesignation="H12"ThreadDesignation="M;G"
       UseThreadNominalDiameter="0" />

       </Color_Table>

      The R (Red), G (Green) and B (Blue) identifiers can be assigned colour values between 0
      and 255.

           Feature and macro technology                      4 Generating features
           Manually in the Feature browser / Feature editor

           The entity type FitDesignation can assume fit designations (example H7) and the entity type
           ThreadDesignation the values M = Metric Coarse Pitch, Mx = Metric Fine Pitch, W = Whit-
           worth and G = Gas Uni.

           Several thread types are separated by `;', with the order of the list determining the order of
           the search.
           The FeatureClass element type can accept designations of defined feature classes (for infor-

           For information on using feature-based macros, see section Applying a feature-based
           macro.

           Use Generic Hole only: During the assignment of feature information from the CAD model,
           Simple Holes, Sink Holes and Free defined Holes are transferred directly to the feature
           browser as Generic Holes.

           Min. tip angle: Define from which angle holes can be recognised as a tip or through hole
           type. If the defined tip angle is larger than the angle in the hole, these holes are recognised
           as the through hole type. If the tip angle is smaller, the holes are recognised as the tip hole
           type.

           Example:

           (1) Min. tip angle = 75°. Holes 50°/ 60° = Through, hole 90° = Tip.

           (2) Min. tip angle = 55°. Holes 50° = Through, holes 60°/90 = Tip.

           (3) Min. tip angle = 45°. Holes 50°/ 60° / 90° = Tip

           Create associative point: display and edit point coordinates of hole features relative to a
           selected frame.

           Grouping features: features with the same geometry are summarized to a feature for each
           frame. 1) Function is not enabled, 2) Function is enabled.

           Feature Recognition

                                       Feature Recognition describes the interactive detection of geometric feature information
                                      from a CAD model. The following modules are available in hyperMILL:
                                       · Single Hole Recognition
                                       · Plane Recognition
                                       · Pocket / T-Slot Recognition
                                       · Boundary Recognition
                                       Procedure
                                      1. In the hyperMILL browser, switch to the Feature tab
                                       2. and select the desired function from the shortcut menu in the upper area of the browser.

           Single Hole Recognition
                                       Geometric information is gathered from the holes in a model in two steps: by defining a sam-
                                       ple hose and searching for (comparison) holes, whose parameters are compared with the
                                       base hole (= sample hole).

                                    Sample hole
                                       The Sample hole parameters always form the basis for recognizing a hole.

                                       Machining Strategy
                                       Automatic recognition: Only select the surface of the base hole. All other surfaces are auto-
                                       matically recognised.
                                       Manual Definition: Select all surfaces of the base hole.
                                       Reference feature: The parameters of a reference feature are used as the basis for creating
                                       Generic Holes based on points/circles on surfaces. On the Search dialogue page, use the
                                       Points and surfaces option and select the surfaces/points that are to be used to create the
                                       hole features. The orientation of the newly created hole features follows the surface normals
                                       in the area of the selected points.
                                       Use the Move to featurelist function to select an existing feature list to which the features will
                                       be assigned. With the New option, a new feature list can be created.

                                       Selection

                                                     Select surfaces of the hole.
                                       Sample search: Start recognition of the sample hole.
                                       Reverse direction: Reverse the direction of the sample hole.
                                       Use the Reference feature strategy to select a feature from the list as reference features.

                                       Parameters

                                              List of recognised parameters of the base hole.

                                               Further parameters can be defined if necessary See the information in the Simple Hole
                                       and Freely defined hole sections.
                                       Name: Define a name for the hole. The name is automatically copied to the feature list.
                                       Thread: Yes, if you want to use a Thread.
                                       Thread: Standard: Select a thread form from the Standard Options offered for the thread
                                       form Metric Coarse Pitch, Metric Fine Pitch or Whitworth. To define an individual thread
                                       form,
                                       1. Select User, define the designation and
                                       2. specify the values for Diameter, Pitch, Type and Length.

hyperMILL                                                    4-39
4 Feature and macro technology  Manually in the Feature browser / Feature editor
         Generating features

      Search
      Here you can determine which hole surfaces should be compared with the base hole. As the
      result of this comparison, holes are found which have the same parameters as the base
      hole.

      Group selection
      User: Select the required holes, whose parameters are to be compared with those of the
      base hole.

                     You can also search for holes using the Window selection function in the CAD
                     program. This is particularly useful with very complex models, for which Feature
                     Recognition is only partly relevant.

      Complete model: All holes in the model with the same parameters as the base hole are auto-
      matically recognised.
      Start: Start the automatic recognition of the holes. All recognised holes are shown under
      Result in a list display. The numbers mean:
      Example: 3 (2)
      (3) Number of directions
      (2) Number of holes in this direction

                     Recognised holes are transferred to a feature list as a Generic Hole or Com-
      pound Feature.

                     Holes with the same parameters (direction, depth) are collected in a feature.
                     Please note that the defined base hole is also always included as a component
                     of a feature.

      Filter
      Use a filter to limit the hoes to be recognised.
      Same colour: Only holes of the same colour as the base hole are recognised.
      Same layer: Only holes on the same layer as the base hole are recognised.
      Same orientation: Only holes with the same orientation as the base hole are recognised.
      Frame limit: Define a frame limit (angle) for the recognition process.
      Frame: Define the frame to be used for the frame limit. Information in section NC system and
      frames.
      B axis / C axis: Use the two tool rotary axes to limit the angle for the hole recognition pro-
      cess. The B axis corresponds to the X/Y direction and the C axis corresponds to the Z direc-
      tion of the defined frame.

4-40                                                                              hyperMILL
           Feature and macro technology                      4 Generating features
           Manually in the Feature browser / Feature editor

                          The defined angle limit in each direction is shown in colour on a rotary ball. Yel-
                          low = machinable area (directions from which holes are recognised). Grey =
                          unmachinable area (directions from which holes are not recognised).
                          Example: angle B axis: 0° to 90°, angle C axis: 0° to 90°.

           Same depth: Only holes of the same depth as the base hole are recognised.
           Depth limit:Only holes are recognised which correspond to the depth limit (from/to).
           Remove hole: Mark hole and in the short-cut menu select the Remove function.
           Reverse hole direction: Mark hole and in the shortcut menu select the Reverse function.
           If the Reference feature is selected as the Strategy, the following functions are available:

           Group selection
           Points and surfaces: Select surfaces / points which should be used to create the hole fea-
           tures. The orientation of the newly created hole features follows the surface normals in the
           area of the selected points.
           Use the Move to featurelist function to select an existing feature list to which the features will
           be assigned. Alternatively, create a new feature list (option: New).
           Circles: Select circles which should be used to create the hole features. The orientation of
           the newly created hole features follows the surface normals in the area of the selected cir-
           cles.
           Reverse direction: Reverse the direction of the newly created drill feature..

           Setup
           Tolerance: The required tolerance of the curve resolution for the holes. For further informa-
           tion, see section Contour offset.

hyperMILL                                                    4-41
4 Feature and macro technology  Manually in the Feature browser / Feature editor
         Generating features

      Slot tolerance: Tolerance for the axial distance (1) between concentric part-holes of the
      same diameter. The following rule applies: if the distance is smaller than the tolerance, one
      hole is recognised (A); if the distance is larger than the tolerance, two holes are recognised
      (B).

      Use solid info: If the option is activated, an attempt is made to copy the direction of the drill
      features from the CAD model (solid). If the option is not activated, the direction of the drill
      features is calculated (based on surface information).

      Use Generic Hole only: As a result of the recognition, only generic holes are created.

                                       Selection
                                       User: Plane Recognition is performed based on the defined surfaces. Select the surfaces to

                                       Automatic: Plane Recognition is performed automatically based on the entire CAD model.

                                       Use frame: When this option is enabled, only planes that have the same orientation as the

                                       Ignore circular planes: Enable this option when circular planes (of holes) are to be excluded

                                       Apply: Create a feature from recognised planes. All recognised planes are transferred as
                                       features to a feature list.

      Pocket / T-Slot Recognition
                                  The model used should be a (static) solid. Closed solids offer the strongest guarantee that all
                                  bottom surfaces (surface normals) will be recognised correctly. In open solids, surface gaps
                                  may mean that some topological information is missing and consequently yield incorrect
                                  results. Also , in rare cases it may be necessary to check the surface normals manually.

                               Functioning
                                  Pockets with bottoms, through pockets, open and closed pockets and T-slots are recog-
                                  nized. Recognition is performed through the use of manual or automatic surface selections.
                                  The Pockets dialogue comprises the dialogue pages Sample pocket, Search and Setup.
                                  Sample pocket: Define the pocket type which should be recognised. Select the surfaces of a
                                  sample pocket. Define search options and filter criteria. Recognised bottom surfaces and
                                  pockets are presented in a list.
                                  Search: For comparison pocket(s) based on the defined sample pocket(s). Limit the search
                                  for sample pockets to a section of the model (user-defined) or search the entire model (com-
                                  plete model). Recognised pockets are presented in a list.
                                  Setup: Limit the search using filter criteria. Define comparison parameters for the search.
                                  Define conditions for accessibility of pockets and the creation of feature lists.

                               Pocket example

                                  Option
                                  Pocket type: Define a pocket type for recognition purposes. You must distinguish between
                                  the following:
                                  Pocket with bottom: Pockets with a bottom are recognised.
                                  T-slot: T-slots are recognised.
                                  Pockets with bottom and T-slots: Pockets with bottom and T-slot are recognised.
                                  Through pocket: Through pockets are recognised.
                                  Tolerance: The required tolerance of the curve resolution for the selected feature.
                                 Name: Define a name for the pockets. This is used in the hyperMILL feature browser; it also
                                  contains the smallest radius in the pocket. This name is used when performing a tool search
                                  in the macro database.
                                  Example: Number Name <open R3.0>
                                  If a pocket has this name, it can be machined using tools with a radius of 3 mm or less.
                                  If you want pockets with bottoms to be recognised, you can use the following options to more
                                  accurately specify the sample pockets:
                                  Suppress chamfers/planes: Enable if you want to exclude planes and chamfers from recog-
                                  nition. In this case, the following will be excluded from recognition
                                  · Planes (pocket bottoms) that do not have any pocket walls and
                                  · Planes that have been recognised as chamfers (see Setup dialogue page).
                                  Open pocket reduction: Enable to reduce the number of open pockets that are recognised. If
                                  there are several adjacent planes which can potentially be used as bottom surfaces, the larg-
                                  est plane (by area) (1) is used as the pocket bottom.

           Combine pockets
           Enable if individual pockets of a model are to be automatically combined into a complex
           pocket.
           When used in a job, combined pockets are processed more efficiently than individual pock-
           ets
           It is possible to combine the following: pockets with bottoms (1), through pockets (2) and
           open (2) and closed (3) pockets. The pockets must have a common edge (4) and the same
           frame in order to be combined.

                          Pockets connected to one another through an open pocket (5) are not consid-
                          ered for automatic combination.

hyperMILL  If the pockets have chamfers or fillets, the values for the corner radius (fillet) or chamfer
           angle and chamfer height parameters must be identical. It is not possible to join chamfers
           and fillets for combination.
           The individually recognized pockets, the combined pockets and the Generic Pocket are dis-
           played in the feature browser as a result of the Pocket Recognition.

           Manually combine pockets
           Generic Pockets can be manually combined either in the feature browser via the shortcut
           menu or using the colour table. The pockets must have a common edge and the same frame

           Pocket comparison parameter
           These two parameters relate to the comparison between the sample pocket and the pockets
           that are to be recognised (see Comparison dialogue page).
           Scale limit: The minimum / maximum scale limit defines the recognition of pockets in the
           model on the basis of characteristic geometric parameters.
           Comparison tolerance: The degree of accuracy with which the characteristic geometric
           parameters (see Scale limit) of one or more sample pocket(s) are compared with the pockets
           to be recognised.
           Pocket Recognition can be restricted to certain pockets through the Pocket filter using
           geometric features.

                          All pocket filters are in effect when the sample pocket is defined. If they are acti-
                          vated, the options under Accessibility check are effective when searching for
                          comparison pockets.

           Accessibility
           Since not all pockets are directly accessible and can be processed, conditions for the acces-
           sibility of a pocket are defined here.
           Accessibility check: the accessibility is checked in the direction of the surface normals of the
           respective bottom surfaces, and in the opposite direction.
           Approach length (1): defines the minimum distance between a potential bottom plane and
           another surface that may prevent access to the bottom plane.

           Polyhedron offset (2): Accessibility of the bottom plane (pocket bottom) is determined on the
           basis of this contour allowance over an extrusion surface. This should always be larger than
           the value for polyhedron tolerance.

hyperMILL                                                    4-51
4 Feature and macro technology  Manually in the Feature browser / Feature editor
         Generating features

      Polyhedron tolerance: accuracy of the polyhedron representation for the accessibility check
      (faceting of the model).
      All recognised pockets are transferred as Generic Pocket feature (close/open) to a feature
      list. Pockets with the same Z direction are combined into one list (frame). The colours of the
      feature lists that you create are defined in the hyperMILL settings (see the Document > Col-
      ours dialogue page).

      Feature list generation
      Use feature list: if this option is enabled, the pockets are saved as features in the existing
      feature lists. Feature assignment is in reference to the frames assigned to feature lists. Fea-
      ture lists that do not contain frames are ignored.
      Use colour table: When reading feature information, pocket bottoms with a specific colour
      value (RGB value) are automatically recognised and the respective features are assigned to
      a corresponding feature class. For this purpose, both the colour value and the name of the
      feature class are defined in an XML file. The name and location of the XML file can be
      selected freely.
      Example:

       <Color_Table>

         <Color_Machining_Definition R="214" G="214" B="214"
       IsPocketBottom="1" FeatureClass="Special Pocket"/>

       </Color_Table>

      To read this information, activate the Use colour table option, select the corresponding file
      (format: *.xml) and confirm your entries. The Pocket feature created contains the designation
      of the feature class in the feature name.

      Example: Generic Pocket <Closed R10 Special Feature> The feature class is displayed in
      the feature editor (section: General).

      Use all colours: Even pocket bottoms whose colours are not contained in the XML file will be
      recognised. The recognised pockets are, however, not assigned to a feature class.

      If the function is disabled, only pocket bottoms (or the corresponding pockets) which corre-
      spond to a colour in the XML file will be recognised.

                                      Apply: Generate a hyperMILL feature that is created as an entry in the feature browser. Con-

                                       contour are simply connected with a straight line.

      Use feature

                   A feature defined in hyperMILL is shown as an entry in the hyperMILL Browser and is directly
                   available during job definition. Two basic options are available to use a feature during job
                   definition: from feature to job or from job to feature.

      From feature to job

                                 1. Open the hyperMILL browser, go to the Feature tab and select the feature that you
                                         want to use in the job definition.

                                  2. Right-click with the mouse and select New Job with feature.
                                  A list appears with the cycles in which you can use the selected feature.

                                  3. Select the cycle you require and go to the Feature dialogue page.

                                  4. The feature currently connected with the job and the status of the geometric data are
                                         displayed in the Feature Job Connector.

                                  For information on the structure of the feature job connector, see section The Feature job
                                  connector.
                                  To edit a feature, proceed as follows:

                                  1. Select the feature, right-click and select Edit.

                                  2. Make the desired changes in the Feature editor and close the editor.
                                  To select additional features,

                   1.           Click the icon to open the Feature selector.

                   2. Drag the desired feature into the right window and confirm with OK.

                                In 2D cycles, only those features with the same frame as the one already being
                                used in the job can be added.

                   To change the geometry status of a feature, select the geometry to be changed in the right
                   window, click the right mouse button and select Active or Inactive.

                   If there are several geometries in the Feature Job Connector, but only one of these is to be
                   active, select the geometry to be changed in the right window, click the right mouse button
                   and select Active only.

      From job to feature

                                 1. Start the hyperMILL browser, go to the Jobs tab and select the desired cycle.
                                  2. Specify the required settings and go to the Feature dialogue page.

                   3.           Click the icon to open the Select feature dialogue, drag the feature to the right win-

                       dow and confirm with OK.

                   To define a new feature for a job, right-click in the left window of the Feature Job Connector
                   and select New > [Feature Name]. Select the desired feature from the list of possible fea-

                   tures that can be linked to the job concerned.

      Reverse direction

                                  If you use a feature in the job definition, the correct feature orientation is important. You can
                                  reverse the feature orientation directly in the feature browser for through holes and through
                                  pockets. To do so, select the feature and then select the Reverse hole or Reverse pocket
                                  function from the shortcut menu.

                                  If the feature orientation is not identical to the frame orientation of the corresponding feature
                                  list, the feature is marked with an exclamation mark and a corresponding message is output.

4 Feature and macro technology   Advantages and uses
         Macro technology

      Macro technology

                                  Macros link machining strategies and tools for machining characteristic geometries (= fea-
                                  tures) and thereby considerably reduce programming expenditure during production.

      Advantages and uses

                                  · Automation and recycling of workflows: Workflows can be automated and recycled
                                         using macros. This significantly reduces programming time, particularly when it comes
                                         to producing 2.5D parts.

                                  · Efficient macro management: Your macros reside in a macro database. This provides a
                                         production knowledge base that is efficiently and easily managed.

                                  · Updating workflows: You can modify your existing macros at any point to match user-
                                         specific new production requirements as they arise.

                                  · Higher degree of automation thanks to `intelligent' macros: Using `intelligent' macros,
                                         operations that were previously assigned to a feature manually can be automatically
                                       linked. Rules and conditions are defined to allow hyperMILL to automatically decide
                                         which machining will be applied. This method can therefore reduce the number of mac-
                                         ros needed to machine a complete model.

      Creating macros

                                  A macro includes features and job information. It is created based on a job or features

      Creating job-based macros
                                  To generate macros on a job
                                 1. Open the hyperMILL browser and select the Jobs tab.

                                  Macro

                                      In the hyperMILL job browser, use the Macros > Apply macros function on the shortcut menu

           The Apply Macro dialogue box
                                       Specify which macros should be applied in the Apply macro dialogue. Use filters to restrict or
                                       increase the number of macros displayed. The filters differ depending on whether a job-
                                       based or a feature-based macro is to be used.

                                       Options
                                       Use feature macros: When job-based macros are used, all feature-based macros are dis-
                                       played.
                                       Check geometry parameters: When job-based macros are used, only features that match
                                       the geometric parameters of the selected feature are displayed.
                                       Check feature class: Only features that are allocated to the same class as the selected fea-
                                       ture are displayed.
                                       Check rule: Only feature-based macros are displayed which correspond to the defined
                                       rules..
                                       Check frame: .When using feature-based macros, the only macros used are those which
                                       correspond to the defined frame.
                                       Select joblist: Available if the Check frame function is activated. The target joblist is applied
                                       to the Check frame function.
                                       Use tools from depot: Available for job-based and feature-based macros.

                                              Select depot. The system searches for suitable tools with the following priority when
                                       performing a tool search: 1.) Tool from depot, 2.) Reference tool (the tool used in the macro)
                                       and 3.) Shortest, collision-free tool from the tool database.
                                       Allow multiple apply: Use a feature-based macro several times.
                                       The Reverse preferred machining direction parameter enables the machining direction of the
                                       feature applied in the macro to be reversed.

                                       Macros
                                       Grouping features: Group together several features with identical parameters.
                                       Material group / Machine group: Limit display to macros that are allocated to the correspond-
                                       ing material group or machine group. The left-hand side of the dialogue box differs depend-
                                       ing on whether a job-based or feature-based macro is used.
                                       If a job-based macro is used, the macro group to which the macro was assigned and the
                                       number of macros contained in this macro group are displayed.
                                       If a feature-based macro is used, the feature upon which the macro was created and the
                                       number of macros available for the feature are displayed.

                                       DB: the tool used for the job is taken from the tool database (numbered NC tool).

           Automatic macro search
                                      When running an automatic macro search, hyperMILL searches the database for macros

           Macro optimisation
                                       Jobs that can be machined using the same tool are processed in sequence (tool change
                                       optimisation).

           Intelligent macros

                                       Macros link (machining) strategies and tools with geometric information. Intelligent macros
                                       include rules that evaluate geometric information and define when a machining strategy is
                                       executed. Intelligent macros are available for all types of features.
                                       Initial situation: The workpiece to be machined contains many holes of various depths, diam-
                                       eters and sink types. A typical procedure in production may then be as follows:

                                       1. Using Feature Mapping, the drilling geometries are recognised automatically and saved
                                              as a feature.

                                       2. The assignment of the machining methods of these features (jobs) and the saving as a
                                              macro are initially done manually.

                                       3. The rules are now defined in the next step. They determine which part of a macro is to
                                              be executed under specific conditions.

           Defining rules for macros
                                       How to define a rule for an intelligent macro:

                                       1. Open the macro database and select the macro for which you wish to define a rule.

                                       2. Right-click it and select Free feature parameter.

                                       3. Using the subsequent dialogue box, select the parameters you want to free. This way,
                                              the linking of the feature parameters with the corresponding macros is severed so that
                                              they can be used for the purpose of the rule definition.

                                       A part of the macro name is then displayed in square brackets (example: F:D8[Through]).
                                       This indicates that the feature parameters have been freed.

                                       4. Now open the job to which you wish to assign a rule by double-clicking the job entry in
                                              the lower area of the macro database (macro jobs). On the Rule dialogue tab, click the
                                              Job active entry and then click the icon .

                                       5. Set the conditions for enabling a machining mode (of a job) based on simple IF-THEN
                                              rules.

         Available machining cycles

Probing

     Available machining cycles

                                 3D Point Probing: Measure the coordinates of any 3D points to measure the accuracy of a
                                 machining job.

                                 Rectangular Probing: Measure the size and location of rectangular bosses and pockets to
                                 measure the accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and
                                 the origin set.

                                 Circular Probing: Measure the size and location of cylinders and holes to measure the accu-
                                 racy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference tool can be adjusted and the origin set.

                                 Axis dependent Probing: Measure the location of points depending on the X, Y and Z axis of
                                 the machining frame to measure the accuracy of a machining job. Optionally, a reference
                                 tool can be adjusted and the origin set.

     3D Point Probing

     Tools     Permissible tool types are touch probe tools. The geometry parameters correspond to the
     Contours  geometry parameters of the lollipop tool type. Possible tool reference points are Tip and
               Centre.

               Probing mode
               Automatic (1): Select when the probing direction is to be detected automatically.
               Manual (2): The probing direction can be set manually for individual probing points. To do
               this, activate under Contour attributes the required points and the Reverse option.

               Contour selection / faces

                                     Select points and surfaces. The points to be measured must be located on
                                     the selected surfaces.

           Parameters

           Parameters

                        Infeed

                        Infeed length (1): Length of the toolpath at the feedrate to the surface contact of the ball of
                        the probing tool.

                        Additional infeed length: Added to the infeed length in the component direction to ensure that
                        the touch probe contacts the component. This should be used in particular in cases with a
                        negative offset (electrode machining).

                        Retract mode
                        Defines the Z level where retract movements are executed.
                        Safety distance/ clearance plane: All retract movements are executed via the clearance dis-
                        tance/clearance plane. .

                        Clearance
                        Security plane: Specify the level of the security plane.
                        Axial clearance/lateral clearance: Minimum distance in an axial or lateral direction from the
                        surface of the model.

         Rectangular Probing

     Rectangular Probing

                                 Using the Rectangular Probing cycle, the size and location of rectangular bosses and pock-
                                 ets can be measured and the machining accuracy can therefore be assessed. Optionally, a
                                 reference tool can be adjusted and the origin set.

     Tools

                              Permissible tool types are touch probe tools. The geometry parameters correspond to the
                              geometry parameters of the lollipop tool type. Possible tool reference points are Tip and
                              Centre.

     Contours and parameters

                                 Contour selection

                                    The following elements can be selected as a contour: rectangle, rectangle with corner
                              radius, point, arc centre and snap point. The contour entities must be level with the Z axis of
                              the machining frame.

                              Contour attributes
                              Select rectangle. Centre (1) relative to the machining frame and length of the contour (2) are
                              displayed in the X and Y direction.
                              Select point, arc centre or snap point and specify length of the contour (2) in the X and Y
                              direction. The centre (1) is displayed relative to the machining frame.

                                             The length of the contour must be greater than the diameter of the touch probe.

                              Measure position: Use Inside or Outside to specify whether probing is to be inside or outside.
                              The allowance (3) is added to each side of the length in the X or Y direction (Outside
                              machining) or subtracted from it (Inside machining)

                                    Measuring depth (4): Corresponds to the contour depth. The measuring depth is meas-
                              ured in the centre of the ball of the probing tool. It is specified either relative to the contour
                              (option: Relative to contour) or as an absolute value relative to the job frame (option: Abso-
                              lute (jobframe)).

                              Infeed
                              Infeed length (5): Toolpath (at the feedrate) up to the contact of the probing tool with the con-
                              tour (+ allowance).

                              Retract mode / Clearance

                                     Specify the level of the security plane. The collision check is carried out with a rectan-
                              gle of the size of the rectangle to be measured + 2*tool diameter + 2* infeed length.

6 Turning        Definition

Turning

     Available machining cycles

                                 Roughing: Roughing of a turning stock of any shape axially or radially to contour.

                                 Contour Parallel Turning: roughing of turning stock of any shape in parallel to contour.
                                 Finishing: Contour parallel finishing of workpieces of any shape based on a preceding rough-
                                 ing operation.
                                 Rollfeed Turning: Machining of workpieces by rolling the tool insert on the component con-
                                 tour, ensuring a very high surface quality.

                                 3X simultaneous Roughing: Roughing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.

                                 3X simultaneous Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with a simultaneous swivel axis.

                                 Groove Turning: Axial roughing of workpieces with grooves or shoulders.

                                 Grooving: Radial Roughing of workpieces with grooves and shoulders.

                                 Groove Finishing: Radial finishing of turning workpieces with grooves or shoulders.
                                 Face Groove Turning: Radial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoul-
                                 ders. The tools used normally have three cutting edges.
                                 Face Groove Plunging: Axial roughing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoul-
                                 ders. The tools used normally have three cutting edges.

                                 Face Groove Finishing: Finishing of workpieces with axial oriented grooves or shoulders.

                                 Parting: Radial machining to separate the component from the bar stock, optionally with
                                 chamfer. Parting off can be done on the front or at the back of the workpiece.
                                 Thread Cutting: Creation of single or multiple start, cylindrical or conical, external and inter-
                                 nal threads with constant pitch. Infeed can be performed either with constant chip section or
                                 with constant X value.

     Definition

                 Turning is a production process for manufacturing rotationally symmetrical internal and
                 external surfaces by removing wood from turning stock of any shape. The external shape of
                 a workpiece is created by using the Outside option, and the internal shape by using the
                 Inside option.

                 The millTURN module allows for the combination of milling and turning tasks in a job list.

                 Stockmodel for subsequent machining tasks: As with milling jobs, a stockmodel can also be
                 generated for subsequent turning operations (resulting stock).

                 NC files: The NC files created with the millTURN module can be used for both milling and
                 turning tasks.

                     Turning contour, (3) turning model.

           Contours  Contour selection
           Strategy  Contours: Define contours for turning operations. These may correspond to the contour of
                     the turning model.

                     Contour attributes
                     Start point / endpoint: define the start and end points for machining, either by selecting a
                     point or by entering coordinates.
                     Reverse: Invert the machining direction of the selected contour.

                     Strategy
                     Axial roughing (1): Machining is performed parallel to the axis of the turning surface.
                     Radial roughing (2): Machining is performed perpendicular to the axis of the turning surface.

hyperMILL            6-3
6 Turning                                                                                                 Contours
         Roughing
                   Cutting side
                   Outside (1)/Inside (2): The external shape of a workpiece is created by using the Outside
                   option, and the internal shape by using the Inside option.
                   Plane (3): Machining of the top face of the workpiece is performed perpendicularly to the axis
                   of the turning surface.

                   Infeed direction

                   To left (1)/To right (2): Machining is performed from right to left or from left to right in the
                   direction of the axis of the turning surface.

                   Outside-in (3)/Inside-out (4): Machining is performed perpendicularly to the axis of the turn-
                   ing surface (in the X direction) from the outside inwards or from the inside outwards.

                   Options
                   Finish path: Removes machining marks during axial roughing.

6-4                                                                             hyperMILL
           Turning                                    6 Roughing
           Contours
                       Falling contours allowed: Contours in X direction can be machined (1). Function disabled (2).

           Parameters  Radial limit/Axial limit: Limits the machining area of the tool used in the radial or axial direc-
                       tion.

                       Infeed
                       Radial / axial infeed to the next machining plane.
                       Constant (1): Constant infeed depth over the entire machining area.
                       Ascending (2): Based on a starting infeed (a) the infeed value is increased by one value per
                       cut. The Maximal cutting depth (b) prevents infeed depths that can cause tool breakage.
                       Descending (3): Based on a starting infeed (a) the infeed value is increased by one value per
                       cut. The Minimal cutting depth (b) prevents infeed depths that are too small.
                       Ramp (4): The infeed alternates between tapered and horizontal. By defining the infeed (a)
                       and the minimal cutting depth (b), the ramp angle is calculated automatically in relation to
                       the contour.

hyperMILL              6-5
6 Turning          Contours
         Roughing

                                  Using the options Oneway up, Oneway down and Ramp, the wear of the tool on
                                  the cutting edge can be reduced as a result of an ever changing intervention
                                  point of the insert cut into the material. This is particularly important in connec-
                                  tion with ceramic inserts.
                                  The options are available for all roughing strategies of the Turning cycle in com-
                                  bination with all Cutting side options.

                   Chipbreak Z: Enable this option to control the chip break and chip removal in combination
                   with the Dwell time or Rotations parameters.
                   Specify the length of the infeed motion in the Z direction (1) after which the tool stops, and
                   define the Unit for the tool stop in dwell time or rotations.
                   Available for: outside, inside and plane machining.
                   Advantage: flexible adjustment to materials of different hardness.
                   Prerequisite: the Falling contours allowed option is disabled.
                   Use sections: Enable if machining should be done in sections (2).
                   Infeed in Z direction = Chipbreak Z * number of sections.
                   Advantage: greater stability for long workpieces.
                   Example:
                   a) Chipbreak Z = 20, Use sections = disabled
                   b) Chipbreak Z = 20, Use sections = 1
                   b) Chipbreak Z = 20, Use sections = 2

                     movements in G0.

                     Clearance distance (1): clearance movement at feedrate before the rapid movement begins.

hyperMILL            Turning model
                     A turning model is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour that is located in the X-Z
                     plane of the turning frame.
                     Collision check: If this option is selected, the holder of the tool used is permanently checked
                     for potential collisions against the current stockmodel (tracked stockmodel) and the current
                     turning model.

                                  Open the Turning area dialogue. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for
                     the turning area.

                            Generate a turning area by selecting a closed contour.

                            Open the Create turning area from model dialogue to create a turning area from sur-
                     faces or solids.

                     Frame for turning axis
                     Select a frame for the turning axis from the list.
                     Define the Colour and Layer of the turning contour. Select Use model colours to adopt the
                     current colours from the model.

                     Surfaces
                     Resolution: Define the resolution (fineness) of the turning area.

                                 Select surfaces or a solid. hyperMILL automatically creates a turning contour that
                     defines the turning area. An entry is created in the hyperMILL browser and a Contour feature
                     is created in the feature browser.

                     Turning stock
                     Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turn-
                     ing frame and the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.

                            Open the Stock dialogue. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning
                     stock. Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock. For information on the
                     available options, see chap. Mode.
                     Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stockmodel for subsequent turning jobs based on the
                     current turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
                     Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stockmodel for subsequent milling jobs based on the
                     current turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
                     From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.

                                    From existing mill stock: Should only be used if the following conditions are ful-
                                    filled:
                                    Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
                                    The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
                                    If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of
                                    different resolutions during stock tracking.

                     For further information, please refer to The Stock model dialogue box.

      Finishing

      Tool:

                    Free angle: Defines the minimum angle to be maintained between the tool insert and the cal-
                    culated toolpath (1). Defining a free angle automatically calculates the tool plunge angle. (2)
                    Turning contour, (3) turning model.

                    Contour selection
                    Contours: Define contours for turning operations. These may correspond to the contour of
                    the turning model.

                    Contour attributes
                    Start point / endpoint: define the start and end points for machining, either by selecting a
                    point or by entering coordinates.
                    Reverse: Invert the machining direction of the selected contour.

                    Segments
                    Assign segments of a contour a cutting speed and feedrate to reduce tool wear and improve
                    surface quality.
                    Select the desired contour and use Edit segments to open the Segments dialogue.
                    Add through three points: Select start point, end point and a further point on the contour.
                    Add through curves: Select a curve. The starting point and end point are calculated automat-
                    ically.
                    The Cutting speed and Feedrate technology values depend on the usage and can be modi-
                    fied either manually or on the basis of factors.
                    Change manually: Select segment and click the link icon (1) for cutting speed or feedrate.
                    The icon changes (2). Enter the required value.

                    Cutting speed  Cutting speed

                    Changing on the basis of factors: Select the segment, click the link icon and enter the
                    required factor directly.

           Turning                                   6 Finishing
           Contours
                       Cutting speed
                     Cutting speed and Feedrate apply to the Usage that is set on the Tool dialogue page under
                     Cutting profile. The values are displayed for each contour segment.

                     Behaviour in sharp corners

                     Angle (1): angle between two contour elements to allow chamfering or rounding.

                     Automatic corner brake: enable when sharp corners of a contour should be automatically
                     rounded or chamfered. Define the chamfer length (2) and the chamfer angle (3) for chamfer-
                     ing (A); for the rounding (b), define the rounding radius (4).

hyperMILL            A contour can be either chamfered or rounded in a single step. If both chamfering and round-
                     ing should take place, define the step twice and combine both steps in a linking job.
                     The Automatic corner brake function is available for outer edges of the turning contour. Fil-
                     lets or chamfers of inner edges should already be included in the rotation model.

           Contours

                     Options

                     Falling contours allowed: Contours in the X direction are machined (1). Function disabled
                     (2).

hyperMILL            Radial / axial limit: Limits the machining area of the tool used in the radial or axial direction.
                     Enable path compensation: When this option is activated, path compensation is handled by
                     the controller, that is, the cutting radius is calculated by the controller (G41 and G42). If this
                     option is not enabled, the cutting radius is calculated beforehand in hyperMILL.
                     Machining mode
                     Limit machining to selected areas.
                     Flat and steep areas are separated from each other by a slope angle. 0° corresponds to par-
                     allel to the turning axis and 90° is perpendicular to the turning axis.
                     Off: Steep and flat areas of the defined contour are machined (1).
                     Steep areas: Only the steep areas of the defined contour are machined (2).
                     Flat areas: Only the flat areas of the defined contour are machined (3).

                    Select the Roll (standard) option if you want edge rolling. This produces rounded corners (1).
                    Select the Extend option if you want to tool to move around edges with tangential extension.
                    This produces corners with sharp edges (2).

      Rollfeed Turning

                                  Machining of workpieces by rolling the tool insert on the component contour, ensuring a very
                                  high surface quality.

      Tool

                           Contours: Define contours for turning operations. These may correspond to the contour of
                           the turning model.

                           Contour attributes
                           Start point / endpoint: define the start and end points for machining, either by selecting a

                           Add through curves: Select a curve. The starting point and end point are calculated automat-
                           ically.
                           Profile type: To mark the contour elements, use the Turning (1) Side Roll (2) or Bottom Roll
                           (3) options.
                           Suitable inserts for the profile types are:
                           Profile type: Side Roll (2): T Full Roll Turn (A), T Short Roll Turn (B)
                           Profile type: Bottom Roll (3): X Full Roll Turn (C), X Short Roll Turn (D)

                           retract movements. If the tool is closer to the turning area, a macro is generated automati-
                           cally, which ensures that the tool does not touch the turning area for approach and retract
                           movements in G0.

hyperMILL            Turning model
                     A turning model is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour that is located in the X-Z
                     plane of the turning frame.
                     Collision check: If this option is selected, the holder of the tool used is permanently checked
                     for potential collisions against the current stockmodel (tracked stockmodel) and the current
                     turning model.

                                  Open the Turning area dialogue. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for
                     the turning area.

                            Generate a turning area by selecting a closed contour.

                            Open the Create turning area from model dialogue to create a turning area from sur-
                     faces or solids. Define the frame, colour and layer of the turning contour.

                     Frame for turning axis
                     Select a frame for the turning axis from the list.
                     Define the Colour and Layer of the turning contour. Select Use model colours to adopt the
                     current colours from the model.

                     Surfaces
                     Resolution: Define the resolution (fineness) of the turning area.

                                 Select surfaces or a solid. hyperMILL automatically creates a turning contour that
                     defines the turning area. An entry is created in the hyperMILL browser and a Contour feature
                     is created in the feature browser.

                     Turning stock
                     Turning stock is defined on the basis of a closed, planar contour in the X-Z plane of the turn-
                     ing frame and the associated turning axis in the X-Z plane.

                            Open the Stock dialogue. Specify a name and, if necessary, a comment for the turning
                     stock. Enable a mode that is to be used to create the turning stock. For information on the
                     available options, see chap. Mode.
                     Generate turn resulting stock: Create a stockmodel for subsequent turning jobs based on the
                     current turning job. The stock model is named after the job that was used to create it.
                     Generate mill resulting stock: Create a stockmodel for subsequent milling jobs based on the
                     current turning job or a combination of milling and turning jobs.
                     From existing mill stock: Select base stock from which a mill resulting stock is to be created.

                                    From existing mill stock: Should only be used if the following conditions are ful-
                                    filled:
                                    Prerequisite: mill/drill machining with non-rotationally symmetrical removal.
                                    The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
                                    If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of
                                    different resolutions during stock tracking.

                     For further information, please refer to The Stock model dialogue box.

                                    The milling job begins when the turning job is complete.
                                    If these conditions are not fulfilled, computing times may increase as a result of
                                    different resolutions during stock tracking.

                     For further information, please refer to The Stock model dialogue box.

                     stock function from the shortcut menu. Specify the required resolution and click OK to con-
                     firm. The created milling stock model appears as an entry in the hyperMILL model browser.

           Groove Finishing

           Tool      The retraction feedrate can be increased for all machining strategies for which retraction
           Contours  occurs without a ramp movement (see the Strategy dialogue page).

                     Contour selection
                     Contours: Define contours for turning operations. These may correspond to the contour of
                     the turning model.

                     Contour attributes
                     Start point / endpoint: define the start and end points for machining, either by selecting a
                     point or by entering coordinates.
                     Reverse: Invert the machining direction of the selected contour.

                     Segments
                     Assign segments of a contour a cutting speed and feedrate to reduce tool wear and improve
                     surface quality.
                     Select the desired contour and use Edit segments to open the Segments dialogue.
                     Add through three points: Select start point, end point and a further point on the contour.
                     Add through curves: Select a curve. The starting point and end point are calculated automat-
                     ically.
                     The Cutting speed and Feedrate technology values depend on the usage and can be modi-
                     fied either manually or on the basis of factors.
                     Change manually: Select segment and click the link icon (1) for cutting speed or feedrate.
                     The icon changes (2). Enter the required value.

                     Cutting speed  Cutting speed

                     Changing on the basis of factors: Select the segment, click the link icon and enter the
                     required factor directly.

                       Cutting speed

                     Cutting speed and Feedrate apply to the Usage that is set on the Tool dialogue page under
                     Cutting profile. The values are displayed for each contour segment.

hyperMILL                                          6-69
6 Turning                  Contours
         Groove Finishing

                           Behaviour in sharp corners

                           Angle (1): angle between two contour elements to allow chamfering or rounding.

                           Automatic corner brake: enable when sharp corners of a contour should be automatically
                           rounded or chamfered. Define the chamfer length (2) and the chamfer angle (3) for chamfer-
                           ing (A); for the rounding (b), define the rounding radius (4).

      Strategy             A contour can be either chamfered or rounded in a single step. If both chamfering and round-
                           ing should take place, define the step twice and combine both steps in a linking job.
                           The Automatic corner brake function is available for outer edges of the turning contour. Fil-
                           lets or chamfers of inner edges should already be included in the rotation model.

                           Finishing: Fine machining, in which the material left by the preceding roughing operations is
                           removed.

6-70                                 hyperMILL
           Turning   6 Groove Finishing
           Contours

                     Cutting side

                     Inside (1)/Outside (2): The external shape of a workpiece is created by using the Outside
                     option, and the internal shape by using the Inside option.

                     Infeed direction

                     To left (1)/To right (2): Machining is performed from right to left or from left to right in the
                     direction of the axis of the turning surface.

hyperMILL            6-71
6 Turning                  Contours
         Groove Finishing

                           Options
                           Radial / axial limit: Limits the machining area of the tool used in the radial or axial direction.
                           Enable path compensation: When this option is activated, path compensation is handled by
                           the controller, that is, the cutting radius is calculated by the controller (G41 and G42). If this
                           option is not enabled, the cutting radius is calculated beforehand in hyperMILL.
                           Change reference side: The reference side of the recessing tool changes (left/right) during
                           machining. Only available if path compensation is enabled.

                           Machining mode
                           Limit machining to selected areas.
                           Flat and steep areas are separated from each other by a slope angle. 0° corresponds to par-
                           allel to the turning axis and 90° is perpendicular to the turning axis.
                           Off: Steep and flat areas of the defined contour are machined (1).
                           Steep areas: Only the steep areas of the defined contour are machined (2).
                           Flat areas: Only the flat areas of the defined contour are machined (3).

                           Radial offset

                           Pre-plunge: During finishing, the tool is plunged at the transition of the defined contour from
                           the axial to the radial direction. Removing material here prevents the tool from engaging with
                           two sides of the insert at the same time in the following machining step. The Pre-plunge
                           option also supports smaller retraction movements.

                           Type of cut

                           Finishing one direction: Material is removed with up and down movements. Since upward
                           movements on vertical walls can lead to a risk of collision between the tool holder and the
                           stockmodel geometry, not all geometries can be machined.

6-72                                 hyperMILL
           Turning     6 Groove Finishing
           Contours

                       Downward: Material is removed with downward movements only.

                       Side allowance (1): Allowance in Z direction.

                       Overlap (2): A path overlap to avoid collision with perpendicular walls (residual stock). The
                       value should always be slightly larger than the radius of the tool.

           Parameters

                       Clearance

                       Macro clearance: Minimum distance of the tool to the turning area during approach and
                       retract movements. If the tool is closer to the turning area, a macro is generated automati-
                       cally, which ensures that the tool does not touch the turning area for approach and retract
                       movements in G0.

                       Clearance distance (1): clearance movement at feedrate before the rapid movement begins.

hyperMILL              6-73

         Groove Finishing

                           Clearance radius (X): Radius for rapid tool movements in the X direction (1).

                           Turning model
                           Model allowance (1): Global allowance on the model.
                           Additional allowance Z (2): Allowance in Z direction.
                           Additional allowance X (3): Allowance in X direction.
                           Both the model allowance and additional allowance can have either positive or negative val-
                           ues.

              Macros       Approach macro / Retract macro
                           Additional movement during infeed to the first path or during retraction after the last path.
6-74                       Radial (1): Define length.

                               alternating manner until the total radial infeed is reached.

                     Axial offset
                     Pre-plunge: The tool is plunged at the transition of the defined contour from the axial to the
                     radial direction. Removing material here prevents the tool from engaging with two sides of
                     the insert at the same time in the following machining step. The Pre-plunge option also sup-
                     ports smaller retraction movements.

                     Axial compensation value (1): Axial deviation from the model contour. The axial compensa-
                     tion value is necessary due to the deflection of the tool, which is affected by the following fac-
                     tors: feedrate (f), cut depth (ap), geometry of the tool, cutting speed (Vc), and workpiece
                     material.

                                Type of cut

                                Up and down: Material is removed with up and down movements. Since upward movements

                                geometry, not all geometries can be machined.

                                Downward: Material is removed with downward movements only.

                                movements in G0.
                                Clearance distance (1): clearance movement at feedrate before the rapid movement begins.

                     Strategy

         Parting
                  Options
                  With chamfer:enable when a chamfer is to be created at the trailing edge of the model and
                  define the desired chamfer dimension (1). The chamfer angle is fixed at 45°.

                  Type

                  Defines how the tool should proceed after parting off.

                  Parting off and rapid (1): a retraction movement is performed at feedrate in Z direction to
                  clearance distance, then rapid retract to the clearance radius.

                  Parting off and rapid (2): a retraction movement is performed at feedrate in Z direction to
                  clearance distance, then rapid retract at feedrate up to the clearance radius.

                  Stop at X position (3): the tool stops at the X position after parting off.

6-102             Machining mode
                  Normal (1): parting off is done in one pass without interruption over the entire Contour length
                  in feedrate.
                  Retract clearance distance (2): parting off is done in multiple passes, each with the defined
                  plunge depth (4). Between each parting, there is a retraction to the clearance distance
                  Retract to clearance radius (3): parting off is done in multiple passes, each with the defined
                  plunge depth (4). Between each run, a retracting movement is performed at feedrate in Z
                  direction to clearance distance, then rapid retract to the clearance radius.
