7 Drilling
         Contours

Drilling

     Available machining cycles

                                 Centering: Enables centrings with various parameters.

                                 Simple Drilling: Machining of Simple Holes in one infeed.

                                 Drilling with Chip Beak: Machining of Simple Holes in several drilling strokes.

                                 Drilling with Pecking: Machining of Simple Holes with rapid retract to the clearance distance
                                 between each drilling stroke.

                                 Optimised deep Hole Drilling: Machining of holes with feedrate optimisation for cross holes
                                 or breakthroughs.

                                 Reaming: Reboring to improve the quality of the surface when chip thickness is reduced.

                                 Tapping: Drilling of threads with various parameters.
                                 Boring: Drilling with a boring bar for large drilling diameters. Input parameters similar to Sim-
                                 ple Hole.

                                 Helical Drilling: Machining of circular pockets with helical stepdown and horizontal grooving
                                 on the pocket floor. Roughing, grooving on pocket floor, finishing and chamfering can be car-
                                 ried out in one job.

                                 Thread milling: Using a helical stepdown, this cycle produces single and multiple inside and
                                 outside threads with a definable chamfer. A hole must have been predrilled for internal
                                 threads.

                                 Circular Pocket: Machining of holes in parallel to the contour, with specifiable machining
                                 direction using climb milling or conventional milling.

                                 Gun Drilling: Drilling very deep holes with a long tool with small diameter. This requires a
                                 previously drilled hole of the same diameter as the hole to be created by Gun Drilling.

                                 5X Helical Drilling (MAXX Machining): This cycle produces circular holes through helical
                                 toolpaths. The tool is executed in a 5-axis manner with a given lead and tilt angle.

     Tool

                   For information on tool definitions, see section Defining a tool in the hyperMILL browser.

                   The following applies to all drilling cycles that support the parameter Tip angle compensa-
                   tion:

                   When using stepped tools with multiple reference points (for example, reference point 1 = 0
                   and reference point 2 = 25), this option should not be enabled.

     Contours

                   Define the drilling strategy, contour selection for the holes and the vertical machining area
                   (top and depth) of the holes.

                   Drilling mode

                   The drill cycles can be used in all drilling modes. The Turning mode is available
                   for turning jobs with a rotating spindle.

                   2D Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is always aligned with the Z axis of the defined
                   frame system. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature definition. All drill
                   holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.

                   2D multi-axis drilling: the direction of any number of drillings can be aligned with the different
                   frames/planes. For infeed movements in XY direction, a relative clearance (automatically
                   calculated for each frame) can be defined. The conditions for collision-proof linking move-
                   ments between the planes can be made available using the Lateral clearance and Globally
                   highest point parameters. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.

7-2                hyperMILL
           Drilling                                     7 Contours
           2D Drilling
                        5X Drilling: The direction of the drill holes is aligned with the normals of the selected surfaces
                        or with the selected lines. When using features, the frame system is part of the feature defini-
                        tion. All drill holes can be collision checked using the milling area.
                        The following applies to multi-axis indexing:

                        1. in Drilling mode: the frame specifies the machining direction. The linking movements
                              between the frames are controlled by the postprocessor.

                        2. in 5X Drilling mode: several sides can be machined in one job. The linking movements
                              between the machining sides are collision tested and are executed as 5X simultaneous
                              movements. A machine is required that supports this type of movement.

                        For further information, see section Settings.
                        Turning: With this option, turning jobs can be carried out with a rotating spindle and fixed
                        tool. The machining direction is defined by the Z axis of the frame. The drill position is always
                        located in the centre point of the workpiece being turned.
                        Frame dependent: Available for the 5X Helical Drilling cycle. The direction of the drill holes is
                        aligned with the Z axis of the defined frame system. When using features, the frame system
                        is part of the feature definition. All drill holes can be collision checked using the Milling area.

                        Contour selection
                        Drill positions are selected either directly on the Contours input page or by allocating a previ-
                        ously defined feature on the Feature input page.
                        For information on linking features and the machining cycle, see section From job to feature.

           2D Drilling  The following CAD geometries are recognised as drill holes: points, lines, but no line points
                        (e.g. end points) or grid points. For information on the general procedure for selecting con-

                        You can select all the drill holes for a drilling job the are produced with the same tools and
                        have the same collision parameters (clearance distance, clearance plane).

                        Lines: In the case of contour selection using lines: The selected contour (line) automatically
                        defines the Top and Depth of the drill hole. You can also define absolute values for these two
                        parameters (Top/Depth) (Parameter dialogue page, Absolute top/depth). This option is avail-

                                       The direction of the drill hole is determined by the Z-axis of the defined frame (-
                                       Z).

                        Points: In the case of contour selection using points: The following methods are available for
                        defining the Top and Depth: Absolute, Top of contour, Bottom of contour, Relative to the top
                        (depth only).

                        lute values relative to the zero point of the defined frame (3). They are independent of the
                        actual position of the selected geometries.
                        Top / Depth (B): The dimension entered relates to the top edge and/or bottom edge of the
                        selected contour (4).
                        Relative to top (C): The dimension entered for the depth relates to the defined top of the drill
                        hole (5).

           Turning

           Turning   Reverse: The defined direction of the drill hole can be reversed in all contour selections.

                     Contour selection
                     Outer line: The start and end of machining in the Z direction and the machining diameter are

                     the X direction automatically.

           Optimisation

                                       Drilling point optimisation allows any drilling patterns to be optimised in accordance with var-
                                       ious criteria (not available for the Turning strategy), so that the stresses and heat that are
                                       generated during drilling are distributed as evenly as possible over the entire surface.

                                   hyperMILL generates a graphical feedback of the drilling points that have been
                                    selected for machining. Since a large number of drilling points requires a corre-
                                    spondingly powerful computer to calculate and display this graphical preview,
                                    the preview display is limited to 1000 drilling points by default.

                     Sorting strategy
                     Off: Drill holes are machined in the order in which they were selected.
                     Shortest distance: Machining is carried out starting with the (drilling) point closest to the ori-
                     gin of the specified coordinate system (frame), followed by the next closest in each case.
                     Circular: The drill holes to be machined are divided into concentric circle segments starting
                     from a centre point.
                     X or Y parallel: The drill holes to be machined are divided into segments that are referenced
                     on the X or Y axis of the selected machining coordinate system (frame).
                     Contour parallel: The drill holes are machined along the outline of the outer contour of the
                     drilling point pattern.
                     More information about the various parameters is provided in the next few chapters.

hyperMILL            7-5
7 Drilling             Circular drilling strategy
         Optimisation

     Circular drilling strategy

                                 Start
                                 Use start reference: Define any point as the start point. This start point can be inside or out-
                                 side of the drilling point pattern. In this case, machining starts from the defined start refer-
                                 ence and moves to the neighbouring point in accordance with the Machining direction and
                                 Orientation.

                                 Z-Optimisation
                                 The Z height of the selected drill holes is taken into account during optimisation. Define the
                                 value for the Max. Z depth.

                                 Orientation
                                 The parameters for controlling orientation relate to the machining of the segments.
                                 Clockwise: The segments are machined in clockwise order.
                                 Counterclockwise: The segments are machined in counterclockwise order.
                                 Zigzag: The orientation (clockwise/counterclockwise) is reversed after each segment of the
                                 circle.

                                 Machining
                                 Inside-Out: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the
                                 inside outwards.
                                 Outside-In: With this option, the drill holes are machined within radial distance from the out-
                                 side inwards.

                                 Parameters
                                 Radial width (1): Width of a circle segment, measured from the centre of the machining area.
                                 Centre point: In order to obtain a correct toolpath calculation, it is essential to define a centre
                                 point. The centre point to be defined represents the centre point of all circle segments that
                                 define the machining area.

     Example:                         In the following, the surface between two concentric circles will be referred to as
                                     a circle segment. The term circle segment is not used in hyperMILL. It is only
                                      used in this documentation to describe the drilling optimisation functionality.

                       In the example (see illustration), all the drilling points that lie within the radial distance in a
                       circle segment are machined. In this context, machining continues with the neighbouring
                       drilling point. Once all the drilling points in a circle segment have been processed, the
                       machine moves to the next circle segment.
                       The machining sequence in the example is: circle segment A, circle segment B, circle seg-
                       ment C. Machining is clockwise from the outside in.

           X / Y parallel drilling strategy

           X / Y parallel drilling strategy

                      Orientation
                      Zigzag: The machining direction of the segments changes after each segment.
                      Oneway: The segments are always machined in the same direction.
                      Shortest distance: Machining continues from the last drilling point of a segment to the closest
                      drilling point in the next segment.

                      Machining
                      Revert X: The machining direction oriented on the X axis of the frame coordinate system is
                      reversed.
                      Revert Y: The machining direction oriented on the Y axis of the frame coordinate system is
                      reversed.

                      Parameters
                      Segment width (A): Width of a segment extending in the X or Y direction. Corresponds to the
                      maximum distance between points in the X or Y direction within a segment.

7 Drilling             5X Drilling
         Optimisation

      5X Drilling

                       Two different optimisation methods are available for 5-axis drilling.

                       5X

                       Frame view: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are calculated from the frame
                       view, while taking account of the selected drilling strategy. All of the drilling strategies that
                       can be applied during 2D drilling are available.
                       Grouping: The machining paths for the selected drill holes are grouped together and calcu-
                       lated according to the shortest distance method (see chap. Optimisation). The grouping
                       depends on the tool axis (B axis/C axis) that must be moved first.

                       The machining paths from one frame to the next can be checked for collisions (optional) if
                       the corresponding parameter (Setup dialogue box) is enabled (see chap. Settings).

                       Start
                       Use start reference: Select a start point, if you want optimisation to begin at a defined start-
                       ing point.

                       Z Optimisation: Use the Max. Z depth parameter to specify the conditions for optimised
                       machining of drill holes at different Z levels. If the distance between two levels is greater than
                       this value, all of the drill holes on one level are fully machined first before moving to the next
                       level. XY optimisation takes place on every level, while taking account of the relevant starting
                       points.

                       This method reduces the number of empty paths.

                       (1) without Z optimisation, (2) with Z optimisation.

7-10                                hyperMILL
           Drilling     7 Optimisation
           5X Drilling

                        Parameters

                        Move B axis first / Move C axis first: Control the grouping of drill holes and thus specify the
                        machining sequence. The drilling points are always processed in a vertical direction first (Z
                        direction of the NCS). Afterwards, the method for 5X movement is used.

7 Drilling           5X Drilling
         Parameters

      Parameters

                     Define the machining areas (in addition to definitions on the Contours dialogue page), the
                     infeed and clearance parameters plus other machining parameters.

                     Machining area

                     Bottom offset: The drill depth is reduced by the specified amount.

                     Absolute top / bottom: The defined absolute values are considered in each case. This facili-
                     tates simple machining if the drill hole(s) must be made before the material removal (of the
                     stock model).

                     Tip angle compensation: Available for all drilling cycles except Centring, Helical Drilling,
                     Thread Milling and Circular Pocket. Extends the toolpath by the length of the tip so that holes
                     may be machined completely.

                     Break through length: Extends the toolpath in the axial direction. In the case of a through
                     hole, approach must continue by this value to ensure that no burring occurs and the thread is
                     completely formed.

                                    The Break through length option is used without taking the bottom type (Flat or
                                    Through) into account. Collisions with the model may occur if the option is used
                                    for blind holes.
                                    The Break through length option cannot be used in combination with blind or
                                    through holes if the Check hole function is enabled.

                     (1) Break through length and Tip angle compensation not activated.
                     (2) Break through length not activated, Tip angle compensation activated.
                     (3) Break through length and Tip angle compensation activated
                     .

                     Hole security

                     These parameters apply for all drilling cycles.

                     Clearance distance (1): This distance holds the tool to a theoretical edge of the unchamfered
                     hole.

           5X Drilling

                        Retract distance: Dimension of the axial distance between the top of the drill hole and the
                        retract movement to the clearance plane.
                        Clearance plane: The J:Ft variable sets the Clearance plane for all drilling cycles to the
                        height of the highest selected feature relevant for machining. Entering J:Ft+50 results in
                        additional clearance between the clearance plane and the highest feature selected in
                        machining.

                        Retract mode/clearance
                        For general information on the retract mode and safety, see section Machining parameters.
                        Available for 2D multi index drilling:

                        Retract mode
                        Clearance plane (A): The start and end position of any machining plane are located on the
                        clearance plane. Auto clearance: height of the infeed between the drill holes, see (1) in the
                        detailed graphic.
                        Clearance distance (B): Start and end position of any machining plane are located on the
                        clearance plane. Infeeds between the drill holes take place at the Clearance distance, see
                        (2) in the detailed graphic.

                        Detailed graphic:

hyperMILL                                  7-13
7 Drilling                                                        5X Drilling
         Parameters

                     (1) Auto clearance, (2) Clearance distance.

                     Plane on global highest point: Plane through point on the model at the greatest distance to
                     the origin of the current frame.

                     Plane with lateral clearance: the start and end position are calculated so that the approach
                     and retract motion is executed in the Z direction of the current frame free of collisions. The
                     start and end positions are tested with the Lateral clearance distance option. In the event of
                     a potential collision, infeed will take place starting from the Plane on global highest point.

                     Relative safety
                     Auto clearance (1): Distance to the highest point of the model (5) from the machining direc-
                     tion.

                     Movement clearance (3): Distance to be maintained in XY direction when infeeding between
                     drill holes to avoid collision (available only for retract mode Clearance distance). In the event
                     of a collision, the machining follows with clearance distance to the first collision-free point
                     from the machining direction.

                     Lateral clearance (4): Additional lateral safety allowance for the start position. The start and
                     end position are calculated so that the approach and retract motion is executed in the Z
                     direction of the current frame free of collisions. The start and end positions are tested with
                     the Lateral clearance distance option. In the event of a potential collision, infeed will take
                     place starting from the Plane on global highest point.

                     This option is only available for retract mode plane with lateral clearance (C).

7 Drilling                 Tool
         Helical Drilling

      Helical Drilling

                                  This cycle uses helical stepdown to produce circular pockets with horizontal grooves in the
                                  pocket bottom. In this operation, the following can be carried out: roughing, grooving on
                                  pocket bottom, finishing during the retract movement and chamfering.

      Tool

                           This cycle requires a special tool.

                           Tool chamfer
                           Chamfer length: The chamfer length of the tool is taken into account when calculating the
                           toolpath.

                           Spindle RPM
                           Define the spindle RPM for roughing, finishing and the slots area.

                           Feedrate
                           Define the feedrate for roughing, finishing and the slots area.
                           Edge control: Select this option to adapt the feedrate depending on the tool diameter to the
                           drill diameter ratio. This ensures that machining does not take place with a feedrate that is
                           too high (output to tool centre) when a small tool diameter and large drill diameter are used.

      Parameters                          If you use this option, check the NC output before using it on the machine. Your
                                          postprocessor may not support this function yet. In this case, please contact
                                          your OPEN MIND partner.

                           For further information on tool definitions, see section Defining a tool in the hyperMILL
                           browser.

                           Machining parameters
                           Pitch (1): pitch of the machining helix. The specified pitch applies to the roughing and finish-
                           ing steps.

                                          If the drill depth is not an integer multiple of the pitch, the start point of the
                                          thread is above the defined drilling geometry and the value of the surface is cor-
                                          rected.

                           Groove depth (2): Pay attention to the tool dimensions when defining the groove depth.
                           Chamfer length (3): length of the chamfer along the surface of the pocket.

7-22                             hyperMILL
           Drilling                                 7 Helical Drilling
           Parameters
                       Chamfer angle (4): values between 0 and 89.99° are advisable.
                       Stepdown chamfering (5): stepdown in Z direction when chamfering. This is made up of the
                       chamfer length (Parameters dialogue page) and the chamfer length of the tool (Tool dia-
                       logue page).

                       Allowances
                       Roughing allowance XY (6): material remaining on the hole wall during roughing. The rough-
                       ing allowance must always be specified as > 0.
                       Finishing allowance XY (7): material remaining on the hole wall during finishing. Only applies
                       if the finishing step has been activated.
                       Bottom offset (8): material remaining on the machining base.
                       Finishing: if a helical finishing step is to take place during retraction, the finishing function
                       must be activated.

                       Path compensation
                       If the Centre path option is enabled, no NC file can be generated.
                       You can use repointed tools with the Compensated centre path option and the Path compen-
                       sation parameter. For information on the compensated centre path, see section Parameters.

           Circular Pocket

                                       For this cycle, you can define the contours as circles (or points) or lines.
                                       Horizontal stepover factor: Infeed in the XY plane is defined as a factor of the tool diameter
                                       (< 1).

           Optimised deep Hole Drilling

                                       Drilling with an initial stockmodel, a stockmodel update and start drilling strategies as well as
                                       crosshole and breakthrough drilling. Optimised deep Hole Drilling breaks down all move-
                                       ments into G1/G0 movements.

           Tool

                     Cutting profile
                     The values for spindle speed and axial feedrate are taken directly from the definition of the
                     tool in the OPEN MIND Tool database.

                     Technology optimisation
                     You can also set the spindle speed and (axial) feedrate for the various drilling phases. The
                     values in the Feedrate and Spindle speed columns correspond to the value set in the cutting
                     profile, whereby the adjustment defined in the % Feedrate or % Spindle speed columns is
                     taken into account.
                     To manually adjust a value for Feedrate / Spindle speed:
                     · Select the line, right-click the Feedrate / Spindle speed column and
                     · select the Unlink option.
                     For the feedrate/spindle speed in this drilling phase, only the values set in the Feedrate/
                     Spindle speed column apply. Changes in the Cutting profile or in the columns %Feedrate
                     and %Spindle speed are not considered.
                     To establish a new connection between Feedrate / Spindle speed and % values:
                     · Select the line, right-click the Feedrate or Spindle speed column and
                     · select the Link option.

                                    Threading with standing spindle, retract while turning backwards

                                    The spindle speed 0 and negative values for the spindle speed are allowed in
                                    sections 1, 7 and 8 of the hole. This is useful, for example, for the "threading" of
                                    an ELB-TLB in a pilot hole or for retracting the tool. A negative value represents
                                    the switch in the spindle orientation of the tool.
                                    When using a negative spindle speed or 0, the system checks of the postproc-
                                    essor is prepared for this. If the postprocessor is not ready, the generation of
                                    the NC File will terminate with the following error message:

                                    Postprocessor not ready for changing spindle orientation (Optimised deep Hole
                                    Drilling).

                     Movement sequence of the tool

      Parameters  Feedrates and spindle speeds assigned to the tool during its movement:
                  (1a) Guide sleeve: rapid movement up to the start of the guide sleeve; with F1 and S1 until

                  pilot hole.
                  (2) With F2/S2 until the start of the crosshole.
                  (3a) Crosshole: from the start of the crosshole until the end of material removal with F3/S3.
                  For crossholes with F4/S4. From the start of material removal until full material removal with
                  F5/S5.

                  hole/material removal with F6/S6.
                  (4) Outlet for a through hole/crosshole) with F3/S3 or F4/S4.
                  Retract movement: to the clearance distance or the start of the guide sleeve in F7/S7.
                  Linking movements: between drill holes with F8/G0 and S8 (reduced feedrate/spindle
                  speed).

                        Accuracy: Defines the quality of the model (mesh) against which the check takes place.

                        Max. angle increment

                        Define parameters for the linking movements between drilling.
                        Distance angle limit: Difference of angle value for different tool inclinations between two dif-
                        ferent machining areas (for example: drilling sequences) of a model.
                        If the defined value (default = 91°) is exceeded or the Distance angle limit is equal to the
                        defined value, the linking movement between the two machining areas takes place at the
                        height of the clearance plane, even if Clearance distance is defined as the retract mode
                        (Parameters dialogue page) (1).
                        If the angle value falls below the defined value, the linking movement takes place at the
                        height of the clearance distance (dialogue page: Parameters) (2). If there is no angle
                        change, the tool moves rapidly to clearance distance. If there is no angle change, the tool
                        moves rapidly to clearance distance.

         5X Helical Drilling (MAXX Machining)

      Clearance straighten angle: If the angle between the Z axis of the current machining frame
      and Z axis of the tool is greater than the defined Straighten angle (default = 45°), the tool
      turns to the defined value for the Straighten angle, after it has reached the clearance plane.

      If the angle between the Z axis of the current machining frame and Z axis of the tool is
      smaller than or equal to the defined Straighten angle, the tool moves to the clearance plane
      without changing the tool inclination (3).

                                                  The rotation angle: clearance plane provides collision avoidance, in particular

      Machining area
      Offset top: Specify offset for the start of the Helical Drilling.
      Bottom offset: material remaining on the machining base.
      Absolute top / Absolute bottom: The values for top and bottom refer to the origin of the
      defined frame.
      Break through length: Area above the lead in or the tip of the tool. Extends the toolpath in the
      axial direction. In the case of a through hole, approach must continue by this value to ensure
      that no burring occurs.
      Pre-drilled hole: Activate if there is already a pre-drilled hole. The area of the pre-drilled hole
      is not machined. Specify the pre-drilled hole diameter via Diameter.
      Finish bottom: Activate if a final horizontal circular path is to be inserted at the bottom of the
      hole, to remove any remaining rest material.

      Machining parameters
      Pitch height (1): Pitch of the spiral-shaped path. Corresponds to the height of a full 360°
      travel.
      Adapt pitch height: Enable if the pitch height of the spiral-shaped path is to be adapted in
      narrow areas and specify the lower limit for the pitch with Min. pitch height.

      Stock model
      Roughing allowance XY (2): Material remaining on the hole wall.

           Tool

                     Infeed

                     Step height / Horizontal stepover: Machining on several infeed planes / radial intermediate
                     steps. If the step height (3) or horizontal stepover (4) is smaller than the depth or diameter of
                     the hole, machining will be done by way of vertical and horizontal multiple infeed.

                     Cutting direction
                     The path direction is either clockwise or counterclockwise.

                     Retract mode
                     Information in section Retract mode.

                     Clearance
                     Clearance plane: Plane for rapid tool movements.
                     Clearance distance (1): Distance between the defined surface of the hole and the start of the
                     helical drill movement.
                     Axial retract distance (2): Axial distance between the end of the helical drill movement and
                     the start of the rapid movement to the security plane.

      Reposition feedrate (1): Feedrate of the tool during repositioning between infeed planes (see
      Step height parameter) or radial intermediate steps (see Horizontal stepover parameter).

      5 axes

      Setup A/B axis
      Tilt angle (1): Tool axis angle to the Z axis of the frame in use. The value should be greater
      than the lead angle of the helix, so that the tool mills using the top face. The axial load thus
      reduced helps to protect the tool and machine.

                     Lead angle (2): Angle by which the tool is tilted in the infeed direction. Relative angle to the
                     tangent on the helical toolpath.

hyperMILL            Hole collision avoidance A/B
                     Hole collision avoidance: If the option is active, collision avoidance occurs around the A/B
                     axis. First, the tilt angle is reduced. If this is not sufficient, the lead angle is reduced as well.
                     Tilt angle max. range/Lead angle: For collision avoidance, the defined tilt angle/lead angle
                     may be changed only by this value at the most in both directions.
                     Example: Tilt angle 10, Tilt angle max. range 4. As a result, the minimum permitted tilt angle
                     is 6 and the maximum permitted tilt angle is 14.
                     Hole check offset: Offset for checking the tool for collisions using the model geometry of the
                     hole.

8 2D machining                Contour selection
         General Information

2D machining

     Available machining cycles

                                 Pocket Milling: Machining perpendicular pocket walls and adaptive pockets with automatic
                                 island recognition and calculation of rest material areas.

                                 Contour Milling: Milling open and closed 2D contours with optional path compensation and
                                 different approach and retract strategies. Rest material areas can be calculated.

                                 Contour Milling on 3D Model: Milling open and closed contours with collision control, optional
                                 stop faces and automatic approach and retract strategies.

                                 T-slot cutting on 3D model: Roughing and finishing of T-slots along plane contours. Different
                                 axial infeed modes allow a free definition of Z infeed. Multiple tool reference points ensure
                                 precise milling results. Collision control and infeed movements based on a 3D model.
                                 Chamfer Milling on 3D Model: Machining of prismatic workpieces. It is possible to differenti-
                                 ate between the Modelled chamfer and Deburr / chamfer sharp edges machining strategies.

                                 Inclined Contouring: Machining same as for Contour Milling, but with inclined pocket wall.

                                 Inclined pocketing: Machining same as for pocket milling, but with inclined pocket wall.

                                 Rectangular pocket: Machining rectangular pockets in parallel to the contour with specifiable
                                 machining direction using climb milling or conventional milling.

                                 Rest Machining: Machining rest material areas left after pocket or Contour Milling.

                                 Face Milling: Roughing of larger surfaces with parallel cuts within one or more contours,
                                 optionally with several steps in Z direction.

                                 Playback Milling: Milling on tool paths, manually generated with mouse interaction in a plane.
                                 Plunge Milling: Guided by a contour, the cycle generates a Plunge Milling toolpath. Possibil-
                                 ity to perform collision control and stock update.

     General Information

                                 If workpiece-specific parameters (top, bottom, clearance distance, contours) are entered in
                                 the drawing, they can be interactively transferred from this drawing.

                                 Adjust the existing default values in the first operation to a joblist, if necessary, in order to
                                 coordinate, for example, the top to the stock size. The modified values are transferred for all
                                 subsequent operations of the joblist.

     Tools

                              For more information on selecting the tool and defining tool parameters, see chap. Defining
                              a tool in the hyperMILL browser.

     Contours

                              Define machining contours, the vertical machining area and cycle-specific contour parame-
                              ters.

     Contour selection

                                 The following can be selected as 2D machining contours: points (drilling only), arcs, circles,
                                 reference lines, curves and curves of surfaces. Several contours or holes can be machined
                                 in one job. The number of selected contours is displayed.

     Visualisation

                              Selected contours (2) are shown in the model at the Z level of the defined top (1) and bottom
                              (3). Depending on the current cycle, the contour directions are also shown. The contour list
                              in the dialogue box shows other parameters such as start, end and plunge.

8-2                                              hyperMILL
           2D machining                                   8 Contours
           Visualisation
                          Top and bottom contours of selected 3D contours are projected into the corresponding
                          planes from the point of view of the current frame.(4). Please observe:
                          · Relative = 0: Upper edge of the selected geometry (5).
                          · Thickness = 0: Bottom edge of the selected geometry (6).

                          Contour attributes

                          To define contour attributes (top, bottom), select the machining contour in the contour list. By
                          making multiple selections in this contour list, you can quickly define the same top and bot-
                          tom values for several contours.

                          Top: Start of machining in Z direction (1).

                          Bottom: End depth of machining in Z direction (2).

                          Both parameters are relative to the frame.

                          It is possible to have various vertical machining areas for the different machining contours in
                          a job. By making multiple selections, the same top and bottom definitions can be applied
                          simultaneously to different contours.

hyperMILL                 Both parameters can be defined as absolute and relative values, and as thickness. Thus top
                          and bottom definitions can be made with various measurements.
                          Absolute (jobframe) (A): The values you set are relative to the current frame. Use the abso-
                          lute dimensions when a drawing has no defined Z coordinates (2D drawing). In these cases,
                          define the top (1) as absolute and the bottom as relative or as absolute depending on the
                          dimensions in the drawing (3). Selected contour (2)
                          Specifying relative dimensions (B): Relative values are relative to the position of the CAD
                          geometry selected in the model. This way of specifying top (1) and/or bottom (3) should be
                          used for drawings that have Z information (e.g., 3D contours, solids, defined thicknesses).
                          Here, (2) stands for Z = 0 as the upper edge of the geometry.

           Parameters

                         Define infeed, approach and clearance parameters.

                         The following describes all parameters available in each 2D milling cycle. Cycle-specific
                         parameters are described in the chapters on the respective cycles.

                         Infeed

                         Vertical stepdown (1): choose the stepdown to the next machining plane, from the Z direc-
                         tion of the active frame. This gives the number of machining planes. If a top is situated
                         between two defined machining planes, the system will automatically reduce the vertical
                         stepdown and insert an intermediate step.

                         Lateral infeed area

                         Horizontal stepover factor (2): stepover in the XY plane is the distance between the centre
                         points of two adjacent milling tool paths and is generally given as a factor of the milling tool's
                         diameter

hyperMILL                Allowance
                         Choose stock allowance XY (1) and stock allowance Z (2). Both allowances are remaining
                         material that is to be removed in subsequent finishing machining (= distance from the final
                         contour that the cutter has to keep).

                                                                                                                                                               8-5
8 2D machining       Examples:
         Parameters

                     Clearance
                     Select the clearance plane (1) as plane for rapid travel movements along all three axes
                     (absolute dimensions). Below this plane, only the infeed in Z direction is in fast travel mode
                     up to the clearance distance. For a 3D model, the clearance plane values can be taken from
                     the drawing.

                                    The clearance plane is always situated above the workpiece boundaries in the
                                    Z direction.

                     Define a clearance distance (2) as a distance from the current surface (3), for fast travel Z-
                     stepdown infeed (relative dimensions). Below the clearance distance, Z-stepdown takes
                     place at feedrate.

                     Retract mode

                     Clearance plane (1): all vertical retract and stepdown movements to the next machining
                     plane take place via the clearance plane.

                     Clearance distance / Lead-in position (2)

                     The stepdown movement to the next workplane is realised with Contour Milling at the clear-
                     ance distance (A), with pocket milling at the lead-in position (start position + lead-in macro)
                     without retraction in the Z direction (B). Approach and retract macros are executed at each
                     machining plane.

                                  Rest material recognition applies to machining which only contains one contour

           Contours

                         Open areas: Define the open areas of the pocket.

                         The optimum starting point for machining the selected contour pockets is determined auto-
                         matically. If it is not possible to reach all machining areas from one plunge point, the pro-
                         gramme automatically looks for additional plunge points. Rapid infeed between plunge
                         points takes place across the clearance plane.

hyperMILL                Plunge point: A plunge point can be freely chosen for any contour pocket contained in the
                         cycle. Since the user-defined plunge point is not collision checked, you must ensure that col-

                         User-defined plunge point and stock mode are mutually exclusive. In stock mode, machining
                         always proceeds from the outside in.

         Pocket Milling

                         The tool moves exactly to the specified plunge point and then machines from there to the
                         centre. The pocket will always be cleared from the inside out.

                         In stock mode, machining always proceeds from the outside in.

                         If the plunge point is outside the pocket contour, the tool moves into the contour pocket
                         along the shortest path (G1).

           Strategy      Reference job

                                 In 2D mode, define the plunge points by selecting a reference job. Prerequisites: High
                         Performance Mode has been enabled and the orientation of the frame's Z axis in the refer-
                         ence job corresponds to the orientation of the Z axis of the pocket machining.

                         Optimisation
                         Sort contours: Select this option to sort the traversing movements between the pocket con-
                         tours according to the shortest distance in each case. By default, the traversing movements
                         are performed according to the selection order of the pocket contours. Available for 2D
                         mode, 3D mode and Stock mode as well as for the Use adaptive pocket option and MAXX
                         Machining.

                         Specify the machining strategy.

                         Machining mode
                         2D mode: the machining is performed with 2D data. Milling area and stock cannot be
                         defined.
                         3D mode: In 3D mode, use the milling area to define the CAD model's machining area (see
                         the Setup dialogue page). This also means it has already been checked for collisions. For
                         more information on the milling area dialogue box, see chap. The Milling area dialogue.
                         You can also generate a stock (see the Setup dialogue page). This can also be used for
                         stock update.
                         In addition to the tool tip, you can check the holder and shaft for collisions. For more informa-
                         tion on tool checks, see chap. Check tool.
                         Stock mode: in this mode, the outermost contour is defined as the stock section contour.
                         Contours lying inside are considered islands. Machining is always performed from the out-
                         side in.

                         Path direction
                         Select the climb milling or conventional milling option for the tool cutting mode. The cutting
                         mode relates to tools rotating clockwise.

           High Performance

                                       High Performance Roughing
                                       High Performance Mode: to use the function, select the check box for High Performance
                                       Mode.

                         Opening cut: enable function when an opening cut should be carried out.
                         Zigzag: enable function when machining with alternating orientation should be enabled.
                         Two different strategies are available in High Performance Mode: Opening cut and Side mill
                         only.
                         The following applies to both strategies: the toolpaths created with hyperMILL are optimised
                         in terms of the minimum machining time at maximum removal rate, taking into account
                         dynamic feedrate values for different machining situations.

                                        The following also applies to both strategies: the Fillet radius must be at least
                                        5% of the tool diameter.

                         Opening cut (1): if this option is enabled, narrow, inaccessible areas (A) with several vertical
                         stepdowns (full cut) can be opened. A trochoidal strategy may be used. hyperMILL deter-
                         mines the most suitable strategy for the particular machining situation internally in terms of
                         the shortest overall machining time.
                         Side mill only (2): if this option is enabled, no full cut behaviour is allowed. Narrow, inacces-
                         sible areas (A) are opened with trochoidal movements.

         Pocket Milling

                         Reposition

                         For both strategies (Opening cut and Side mill only) the following applies:

                         Safety (1): axial movement (in the Z direction) away from the plane currently being
                         machined. Default value: Clearance distance * 0.1.

                         Feedrate: Value for the maximum achievable feedrate for all movements to reposition the
                         tool without material removal.

                         Infeed

                         Dense area stepover (factor) (1): The value is multiplied by the Stepover (factor of diameter)
                         (see Parameters dialogue page) and defines the lateral infeed for trochoidal movements in
                         narrow, inaccessible areas. A reduction in the horizontal stepover in narrow areas may be
                         particularly useful for hard materials.

hyperMILL                Example: If the total infeed is 2 and the vertical stepdown for the opening cut is 0.5, machin-

                         A targeted feedrate adjustment at the moment of entry into the material can be especially
                         useful with hard workpiece materials.
                         Factor side entry regulates the lateral approach (not when the position is tangential to the
                         contour) from outside and is referenced to the feedrate XY of the tool.

         Pocket Milling
                         Factor plunge entry affects the helical or ramp plunge into the material from above. This fac-
                         tor is calculated with plunge feedrate.

                         Zigzag feedrate
                         Feedrate: factor influencing the feedrate of the opposite direction. If climb milling is chosen
                         as cutting mode, the opposite direction feedrate, i.e., the conventional milling feedrate, is
                         reduced by the specified factor. The 0.8 factor equates to a feedrate reduction of 20%.
                         The following restrictions apply to the High Performance Mode:
                         Dialogue page Tool
                         Corner fillet radius must be greater than 0.05* tool diameter. In the case of tools with a core,
                         the core diameter must be smaller than 0.9* tool diameter, and smaller than the flat part of
                         the tool. Ball endmills with core are not permitted. For bullnose end mills, the following
                         applies: core diameter *0.5 must be smaller than the radius - corner radius.
                         Dialogue page Strategy
                         Plunge points are not supported. The Use adaptive pocket option is not available. No G2/G3
                         movements can be generated in the 3D Mode.
                         Dialogue page Parameters
                         Fillet all toolpaths is enabled by default. The Radius for horizontal infeed parameter is not
                         available. The negative stock allowance XY must not be greater than 0.25 * tool diameter in
                         the 2D mode / Stock mode.
                         The conditions that govern the 3D Mode depend on the tool type:
                         Endmill: no negative XY allowance allowed. If (stock allowance XY - stock allowance Z) < 0,
                         the absolute value of this difference must be smaller than the tool radius.
                         Ball endmill: Absolute value of the negative stock allowance XY < tool radius. Stock allow-
                         ance XY must be greater than stock allowance Z.
                         Bullnose endmill: negative stock allowance is only permitted up to the absolute value <= cor-
                         ner radius. If (stock allowance XY - stock allowance Z) < 0, the absolute value of this differ-
                         ence must be smaller than (radius - corner radius) of the tool.
                         The retract mode is set to retraction plane.
                         Dialogue page Macros
                         Only the Ramp or Helical plunge macro is available as a macro. When using the Helical
                         plunge macro, the helix radius of the cycle is calculated automatically. The angle must be
                         greater than 0.01.

           Contour Milling

                                       Milling open and closed contours with optional path compensation (cutter radius compensa-
                                       tion), automatic rest material recognition and machining of difficult to access undercut con-
                                       tours.

           Tool

                         The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill, chamfered cutter
                         and T-slot cutter.

           Contours

                         Contour selection
                         Contours must exist as Polylines (2D), Circles, Ellipses or Splines.
                         For information on contour selection, see section Contours.

                         Contour attributes
                         Specify the top, bottom, start point, end point and plunge point parameters for the selected
                         contours. For information defining top and bottom, see the section Contours. Enable the
                         Start point, End point or Plunge point checkboxes and select a point.
                         Freely select the start point (1) for each contour.

                         Set an end point (2) if the contour is to be machined only partially or if there should be an
                         overlap.

hyperMILL                8-23
8 2D machining                                                                                                         Tool
         Contour Milling
                          Overlap: An overlap is only permissible for closed contours. The toolpath will move the tool
                          past the start point (1) until it reaches the given end point (2).

                          Plunge point: The plunge point (1) applies for the infeed to the first work plane. The cutter
                          moves directly from the plunge point to the starting point or to the approach macro position.
                          The plunge point is not collision checked.

                          Reverse: In the default setting the machining direction follows the direction of the selected
                          contour. This can be seen in the graphic preview. If the generated toolpaths do not result in
                          the intended machining direction, select the relevant contours and select the Reverse option.
                          Align closed contours: The machining direction can be reversed for all selected closed (!)
                          contours simultaneously. To do so, select the contours and specify the direction of the con-
                          tours using the Align closed contours > Clockwise / Counterclockwise function from the
                          shortcut menu. The starting point and end point are interchanged automatically.

                                         If you change the machining direction, you should change the cutter position as
                                         well.

                          Connect contours: Select contours and connect them with one another using the Connect
                          contours function from the shortcut menu. Only adjacent contours can be connected with
                          one another.

      Strategy

                Tool position

                The right selection of the cutter position depends on the direction of the polyline (5).

                Auto climb (1): The direction of the contour is automatically adjusted in such a way that

                Oneway (1): Machining is always performed in the same direction.

      Interior corners

      Fillet interior corners: Smooth filleting (rounding) of internal milling paths for contour pockets
      or islands.

      (1) Fillet interior corners enabled, Trim to milling area disabled.

                         Fit step: The value defined under Infeed for the vertical stepdown is automatically adjusted in

           Tool

           T-slot cutting on 3D model

                                       Roughing and finishing of T-slots along plane contours.

                                       Allowances for every area of the slot may be defined separately. Different axial infeed modes
                                       allow a free definition of Z infeed. Multiple tool reference points ensure precise milling
                                       results. Collision control and infeed movements based on a 3D model.

           Tool

                         The T-slot cutter tool type is supported. The cutting edges of the disc may be either square,
                         rounded or chamfered.
                         It is possible to select different tool reference points.

                                        An adjusted postprocessor is required to use different tool reference points (Tip
                                        and Disc top). To adjust your postprocessor, please contact your OPEN MIND
                                        partner.

                         A distinction is drawn between the following options when selecting the tool reference point:
                         The tool reference point is:
                         · Disabled: The toolpath is calculated for the tool tip.
                         · Enabled and Tip (1) is selected: The toolpath is calculated for the tool tip (Tip is the

                               default name used for the tool reference point that can be adjusted!).
                         · Enabled and Disc top (2) is selected: The toolpath is output for the top of the disc (Disc

                               top is the default name used for the tool reference point that can be adjusted!).
                         (A) Upper cutting edge (2) / Lower cutting edge (1) = chamfer
                         (B) Upper cutting edge (2) / Lower cutting edge (1) = radius
                         (C) Upper cutting edge (2) / Lower cutting edge (1)= sharp

hyperMILL                8-49
8 2D machining                       Tool
         T-slot cutting on 3D model

      Contours  Free geometry
                Use free tip geometry for collision check: A free tip geometry is taken into account during the
                collision check and simulation. For further information on tools, see section Defining a tool.

                Specify the path of the T-slot using contours. A separate contour is required for each side to

      Boundary  Spring path: For closed contours, an additional finish pass is performed for each machining
                plane. This removes fine machining cavities. Define the number of empty cuts to be per-
                formed using Pass number.

                Path compensation
                See the information in section Path compensation.

                Retract mode
                The retract mode defines the Z level where the system executes horizontal infeed move-
                ments. The mode set is valid for all machining directions (incl. approach, retract and return
                movement macros) and for the profiles machined with them. Exception: Machining in zigzag
                mode without return macro.
                Clearance distance: All retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance dis-
                tance. Starting and end positions of an infeed movement in rapid are displaced in Z direction
                in order to guarantee a collision-free linear infeed movement. The clearance distance is
                added to these positions.
                Clearance plane: All retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance plane.

                Clearance
                Clearance plane and clearance distance apply in the direction of the Z axis of the current
                frame.
                Clearance plane: Plane for rapid tool movements. Specification in absolute dimensions.
                Define the height by right-clicking on the icon. Select the desired contour.
                Clearance distance: distance to be defined to the toolpath to be milled. Above the clearance
                distance, infeed takes place as rapid in the Z direction (A); below the clearance distance
                infeed takes place at the Z feedrate (B).
                Side clearance: Minimum distance in lateral direction from the surface of the model.

                Trim
                Trim to stock: The stock defined on the Setup dialogue page is used to trim the toolpaths.
                Use Offset to enter a distance to the stock.
                Keep tool down: The toolpath is not trimmed on the stock. The feedrate can be increased for
                the toolpath outside the stock with the Feedrate repositioning value. No unnecessary retract
                movements take place at clearance distance or clearance plane.

               Macros    Manual: Several options are available for the approach and retract movements.
                         Perpendicular (1): Perpendicular to contour tangent, enter length.
                         Quarter circle (2): In a quarter circle, enter radius.
                         Tangential (3): On contour tangent, enter length.
                         Half circle (4): In a half circle, enter radius.

                         Macro extension (1): Only available for quarter circle. The macro is extended by the speci-
                         fied value. This guarantees that the tool can fully retract from the groove without leaving
                         behind any material (such as chippings/shavings). This is particularly important for axial
                         infeed from bottom to top (see chap. Strategy).

                         Contour extension (open contours only)

                         Click Start / End (1) to extend the contour (of the toolpath) by the specified amount for the
                         approach / retract movement.

           Parameters
                         Infeed mode
                         Zigzag direct: the machining direction changes per section. The infeed movement follows
                         the shortest path. The horizontal stepover between two adjacent sections takes place with
                         the machining feedrate (G1) (1).

                         active frame.

hyperMILL                Macros
                         Return macro: Extend the approach and retract path of the tool by a distance (3) specified by
                         the approach factor and retract factor in the plane of the current machining. Displayed in (1)
                         for zigzag direct stepover mode, and in (2) for zigzag smooth. A factor > 0.5 for approach
                         factor and retract factor ensures that before and after performing a cut, a tool is outside the
                         area to be machined.

           Playback Milling

                                       The playback method can be used for simple milling work such as face milling of a clamping
                                       surface in a fast and flexible manner. The path is generated under specification of the
                                       selected cutter diameter by moving the mouse over the corresponding areas. It is also possi-
                                       ble to create a boundary for further machinings.

           Contours

                                                       Unlike other 2D cycles, you cannot select contours for Playback Milling.
                                                       Furthermore, the tool always moves along the selected contour.

                                       Playback path

                                                       Contours: Click one of the icons if you want to create or modify a playback path.
                                       Note that the settings for displaying the tool are only displayed if a corresponding tool has
                                       been selected.
                                       Top: Specify the Z value of the playback contour.
                                       Perpendicular infeed X / Perpendicular infeed Y: Depending on the tool diameter used, the
                                       intersection degree of the drawn toolpath is determined in the relevant direction (value = 0.2
                                       > intersection degree = 20%).
                                       Offset model XY: Accuracy for the tool collision check against the model used (= wall dis-
                                       tance).
                                       Fillet radius: The toolpath drawn is rounded with the specified fillet radius. This applies to
                                       perpendicular and freely drawn contours.
                                       Coordinate grid: Accuracy of the transfer of X/Y coordinates when specifying the position of
                                       the toolpath.

hyperMILL                (1) Allow only perpendicular paths: Only perpendicular paths are possible.
                         (2) Show playback paths as surface: Displays the playback path as a surface.

                         (5) Activate collision avoidance: There must be a defined model or milling area. The tool is
                         retracted, while taking account of the offset defined for the model.

                         collision check is carried out for the path drawn.

                         Infeed strategy
                         Roughing / finishing along the selected contour. The infeed (stepover) distance is calculated

         Plunge Milling

                         Rapid retract: Retract movement is executed in rapid mode.

                         allowance XY / allowance Z: toolpath offset in the lateral or Z direction.

                         Scallop height (2): available for finishing only. The tool is run so that the defined scallop
                         height is observed. Specify the automatically calculated lateral distance for tool grooving with
                         the value for the scallop height value, and the minimum infeed in the XY plane with the min.
                         stepover.

                         For the roughing infeed strategy, the retract movement is always linear (1). For the finishing
                         infeed strategy, the retract movement can be linear (1) or circular (2).

                         With Retract distance (4), specify the distance of retract motion from the plunge motion, and
                         with the axial retract angle (5) the angle for the retract motion in axial direction. Allowed val-
                         ues for the axial retract angle for vertical retract movement or withdrawal of for the roughing
                         infeed strategy are between 0 and 90°, and for circular retract movement between 0 and
                         180°.

                         With the plane retract angle (6), specify the angle for the retract motion in the XY plane (only
                         available for roughing infeed strategy). Allowed values for the plane retract angle are
                         between 0 and 90°.
