9 3D machining
         3D Collision check

3D machining

     Available machining cycles

                                 Arbitrary Stock Roughing: Z constant stock removal of pre-fabricated blanks of any shape
                                 with the option of stock model update. Machining proceeds parallel to the specified contour
                                 or parallel to axis.

                                 Optimised Roughing: Roughing and rest roughing of any workpieces. Calculate toolpaths for
                                 standard pocket shapes such as rectangular and circular pockets. The model geometry and
                                 stock model geometry will be taken into consideration to calculate highly efficient toolpaths
                                 and reduce direction changes ("high speed cutting"). Machine remaining rest material areas
                                 based on the generated "resulting stock".
                                 Profile Finishing: Allows multi-surface, collision-free milling with different guide curve strate-
                                 gies; optional slope-dependent machining. An XY optimised strategy is offered for the X and
                                 Y machining profiles.

                                 Z Level Finishing: Z constant finishing with optional slope-dependent machining. By adapting
                                 the vertical stepdown values to the surface flow especially for steep surfaces, unnecessary
                                 fine infeed increments are avoided and an optimal line distance is thus guaranteed.

                                 Shape level finishing: Z-Level machining for steep areas. Optionally, plane machining can be
                                 replaced by cuts parallel to any shape.

                                 Iso Machining: The milling paths follow the ISO lines (U, V) so that they are optimally
                                 adapted to the surface curve.

                                 Free Path Milling: Milling of free defined 3D contours. Multiple vertical stepdown and ramped
                                 transition between milling paths are possible.

                                 Plane Machining: Face Milling of planar surfaces with pocket strategy. Automatic plane level
                                 detection or manual selection of surfaces. The stockmodel can be used for trimming.

                                 Complete Finishing: Z Level Finishing with automatic pocket-shaped machining of flat areas.

                                 Equidistant Finishing: Finishing with constant infeed on surface; particularly suitable for high-
                                 speed milling. Machining takes place equidistantly within a closed guide curve or flowing
                                 between two guide curves.

                                 Form Pocket: Finishing of pockets with free-form floor.

                                 Pencil Milling: Automatic detection and machining of grooves.
                                 Automatic Rest Machining: Remachining of separate rest material areas left during a finish-
                                 ing cycle.

                                 Rework Machining: Machining of pre-calculated toolpaths from a reference job where the
                                 toolpaths could not be machined due to detected collisions. For the rework machining, a dif-
                                 ferent tool is applied to avoid the previously detected collision areas from the reference job.

                                 Rib / Groove Machining: Roughing and finishing of ribs and grooves or limited groups thereof
                                 in one job for side surfaces and floor areas respectively.
                                 Cutting Edge: Optimised machining of cutting edges using curve-based pre-roughing (strat-
                                 egy: manual curve) in 3D mode, followed by rest machining in 2D mode (strategy: reference
                                 cycle).

     3D Collision check

                                 Collision monitoring is assured by the following factors:

                                 1. Milling area/turning area: 3D collision models are the part of the CAD model defined as
                                        a milling area or turning area (also see section Milling area, Turning area, Clamping
                                        area).

                                 2. Frame: The orientation of the frame system determines which of the surfaces included
                                        in a machining area can be milled. The system machines only those surfaces which are
                                        visible from the tool axis.

                                 3. Clearance plane and distance: These parameters limit the areas for rapid tool move-
                                        ments (see section Safety).

9-2                          hyperMILL
           3D machining                           9 Machining parameters

                         In addition to the automatic collision check performed for the tool tip, the tool shank, tool
                         holder and extension can also be checked for collisions (see section Check tool).

                                        No collision check is made for tools with free geometry.

           Machining parameters

                                       The basic processing parameters include information on collision detection in Z direction
                                       (clearance distance and plane, retract mode), vertical machining area (surface, depth, allow-
                                       ance), and vertical and horizontal infeed.

                                       Safety
                                       Clearance plane and clearance distance apply in the direction of the Z axis of the current
                                       frame.

                                               Clearance plane (1): Plane for rapid tool movements. Specification in absolute dimen-
                                       sions Define the clearance plane by right-clicking on the icon. Select a point and confirm the
                                       selection.

                                                       Traversing movements on the clearance plane are not checked with regard to
                                                       collisions. Therefore this plane must be placed at a sufficient distance above
                                                       the surface of the workpiece.

                                       Clearance distance (2): distance to be defined to the toolpath to be milled. Above the clear-
                                       ance distance, infeed takes place as rapid in the Z direction (A); below the clearance dis-
                                       tance infeed takes place at the Z feedrate (B).

                                       Machining area
                                       The vertical machining area is defined by the values for Top and Bottom of the workpiece.
                                       Top (3): maximum Z value in the current job.
                                       Depth (4): minimum Z value in the current job.

                                               Manual top / Manual bottom: Specify the values for top and bottom directly on the
                                       model by clicking the icon. Manually defined values are not associative. If changes are made
                                       to the model geometry, the values will not automatically change as well.

hyperMILL                9-3
9 3D machining
         Machining parameters

                               Infeed
                               Vertical stepdown (1): The vertical stepdown determines the number of machining planes.
                               Allowance (2): remaining material on the workpiece. Calculated in direction of the surface
                               normals. Added to the clearance parameter during machining (see section Check tool).

                                              Exception: for the 3D Arbitrary Stock Roughing cycle, the distance between the
                                              tool and the stock and model is specified by the defined clearance only.
                                              If the XY allowance is negative, endmills are not allowed.
                                              If a bullnose endmill is used, the negative XY allowance must be smaller or
                                              equal to the tool radius minus the corner radius: tool radius (5 mm) - corner
                                              radius (4mm) = 1mm.
                                              The stock allowance only applies for surfaces. For areas where there are no
                                              surfaces present there will be no stock allowance calculated.

                               Z constant machining: In the last machining level, the allowance only applies in X and Y
                               direction, not in Z direction. The specification of negative stock allowances is possible as
                               long as the sum of (negative) stock allowance and tool corner radius does not become nega-
                               tive.
                               When specifying negative stock allowances, the surface gaps must not exceed the following
                               maximum values (risk of "nose-diving"): 2 x (tool radius + negative offset).
                               Limitations: If the sum of the allowances is negative, the total amount must be less than the
                               tool radius - machining tolerance.
                               Example: tool radius = 5.00 mm, machining tolerance = 0.01 mm, allowance = -3.0 mm.
                               Additional allowance XY must be greater than -1.99 mm, e.g. - 1.98, for |-3.00mm +(-
                               1.98mm)| < 5.00mm -0.01mm.
                               The polyhedron offset is also taken into account as the stock allowance (see dialogue Milling
                               area > Definition). If several values are defined here, only the smallest value is taken into
                               account.
                               Horizontal stepover (3): infeed in the machining plane (XY plane) is specified as length
                               dimension, or as a factor of the tool diameter: J:ae/T:Dia (= infeed width/tool diameter). Ref-
                               erence to different definitions is given at the appropriate places.

                         Retract mode

                         The retract mode defines the Z level where the system executes horizontal infeed move-
                         ments. The mode set is valid for all machining directions (incl. approach, retract and return
                         movement macros) and for the profiles machined with them. Exception: Machining in zigzag
                         mode without return macro.

                         Clearance distance (1): all retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance dis-
                         tance. Starting and end positions of an infeed movement in rapid are displaced in Z direction
                         in order to guarantee a collision-free linear infeed movement. The clearance distance is
                         added to these positions.

                         Clearance plane (2): all retract and infeed movements are executed via the clearance plane.

           Strategy parameters

                                       Different strategy parameters are available, depending on the machining cycle. Explanations
                                       are provided in the respective machining cycle sections.

                                       Cutting mode

                                       Climb milling, conventional milling: in the case of contour-parallel machining with continuous
                                       orientation, the following definitions apply: climb milling and conventional milling relate to
                                       clockwise rotating tools. To perform climb milling with an anticlockwise rotating tool, select
                                       conventional milling. For climb milling with right-handed tools the following machining direc-
                                       tions are valid:

                                       (1) Outside machining in counterclockwise direction.

9 3D machining                                                         Subdivision of the machining areas
         Boundary  (2) Inside machining in counterclockwise direction.

     Boundary

                   Define the machining area, the edge behaviour of the tool at the machining boundaries (tool
                   reference), the plunge point for the machining.

                   Different methods are available for defining boundaries, depending on the machining cycle.
                   Explanations are provided in the respective machining cycle sections

     Subdivision of the machining areas

                                 The subdivision of the workpiece into different machining areas uses the following criteria:
                                 · Geometric criteria: surface curvature, main direction, characteristic extension, position

                                        in space of the surface
                                 · Suitable tool type
                                 · Optimum milling strategy.

     Independent machining areas

                                 Efficient machining with short machining times and minimized finishing times can often only
                                 be carried out if the workpiece has been subdivided carefully into different machining areas
                                 (particular surfaces, group of surfaces).

                                 If independent machining areas with the same machining direction, the same machining
                                 strategy, and the same tool with the same orientation of the frame are detected during clas-
                                 sification into milling areas, these areas can be machined together in one cycle.

                                 In order to avoid steps and tool marks, the machining areas should not overlap and should
                                 not be too close together. If this is not possible, the boundaries should be combined into one
                                 machining area.

                   To avoid unwanted nose-diving of the tool, the boundary area and the edges of
                   the milling surfaces must not contain any surfaces the tool cannot access (slots,
                   for example).

                   Milling surfaces must not contain any double or superimposed surfaces.

                                 Areas within a boundary, for example in the case of problems with the milling strategy, can
                                 be excluded from machining.

     Machining area definition
                                 The definition of the machining area is either based on Boundary (1), or milling surfaces (2).

           Subdivision of the machining areas

           If no machining area has been defined for a milling cycle, the system interprets the limita-
           tions of the workpiece, adding an internally determined offset as machining boundaries.

                          To avoid empty cuts due to the internal offset, you should always specify the
                          blank boundaries as machining area for machining stock which has not been
                          pre-formed.

           Surfaces that are not visible (1) from the `perspective' of the tool axis (Z axis of the frame
           system) are excluded from machining.

hyperMILL  Strategy

                  Boundary curve: Use boundaries to manually limit the area to be machined.
           Closed curves can be used as boundaries, for example Polylines (2D/3D), Splines, Circles.
           The Z position of the boundaries is not taken into account, so that 2D curves are satisfactory.
           3D curves are projected into the XY-plane.
           One or more boundaries are permissible, and they may overlap for the purpose of area
           delimitation.
           If no boundary is selected, the component's boundaries are used as machining boundaries,
           taking into consideration any defined allowances, any top/bottom values, and the direction of
           the defined frame.
           The minimum distance between the boundary curve and actual machining area should be
           the cutter radius + machining allowance.

         Boundary

                          Milling surfaces: Use milling surfaces to define the area to be machined.
                   Milling surfaces are used to calculate a boundary automatically.
                   Milling surfaces can be delimited with a manual boundary (3D Profile Finishing). For more
                   information on defining manual boundaries within milling surfaces, see chap. Boundary.

                   Stop surfaces

                           Use stop surfaces to define the area of the CAD model on which no machining takes
                   place. Always use stop surfaces whenever you need to ensure that the tool does not touch
                   the stop surfaces.
                   The following applies to the cycles 3D Profile Finishing, 3D Z Level Finishing and 3D Auto-
                   matic Rest Machining: You can define stop surfaces as part of the Boundary curve strategy
                   or as part of the Milling surfaces strategy.
                   Use all other surfaces: all (other) surfaces of the workpiece that are not used for milling are
                   automatically defined as stop surfaces excluded from machining.

                           Manual selection: Manual definition of stop surfaces to be excluded from machining.
                   Offset: the offset of the stop surfaces extends the area excluded from machining by the
                   specified value.

                   Examples
                   The following examples illustrate the relationship between milling surfaces and stop sur-
                   faces. Colour coding: Milling area (entire model), Milling surfaces (blue), Stop surfaces (red).
                   Example 1: the manual selection option for stop surfaces has been enabled, and stop sur-
                   faces have been selected. The surface of the cog is defined as a milling surface, whereas
                   the bordering surfaces are defined as stop surfaces.
                   Example 2: the manual selection option for stop surfaces has been enabled, and stop sur-
                   faces have been selected. The surface of the cog is defined as a stop surface, whereas the
                   bordering surfaces are defined as milling surfaces. The combination of milling and stop sur-
                   faces enables simple yet precise delimiting of the machining area

                   Example 3: the manual selection option for stop surfaces has been enabled, and stop sur-
                   faces (A) have been selected. Machining ends at the stop surface. The tool does not touch
                   the stop surface.

                   Example 4: the manual selection option for stop surfaces has been enabled, and no stop
                   surfaces have been selected. The machining does not end at surface 1, because it is not
                   defined as a stop surface. The tool touches surface B.

           Subdivision of the machining areas

           Soft bounding: Only available for ball mills. Machining does not stop when the tool makes
           contact with the bounding surface (1), but when it exceeds the surface by the blending factor
           (2). This factor is based on the tool radius (standard = 0.05 x tool radius). Permitted values
           are between 0.02 and 0.2. In this way, full machining of the milling surface (4) is ensured.

hyperMILL  Use the All other surfaces option to set all areas not defined as milling surfaces (3) or stop
           surfaces as bounding surfaces (1). Select the stop surfaces manually.
           Use the Manual option to manually select the stop and bounding surfaces.

                          tangentially or that continue vertically downward from their edge as bounding
                          surfaces (1).

           Tool reference
           During some machining cycle a definition of the traverse area in dependence on the bound-
           ary curve is possible. The following methods are available, depending on the cycle:
           Toward: the milling path ends as soon as there is contact between the tool shank and the
           boundary (1). This ensures that already machined surfaces lying outside the boundary are
           not touched. Machining with exact boundary. This may result in unmachined areas (2).

                                                                                                                                                 9-9
9 3D machining     Subdivision of the machining areas
         Boundary

                   On top: machining of the defined area until the tool axis is on top of the boundary (1). The
                   tool axis can never move beyond the boundary.

                   Offset: any given offset value can be chosen. A positive value enlarges the boundary, while
                   a negative value reduces it. With nested boundaries, a positive offset value enlarges the
                   outer boundaries and reduces the inner boundaries (vice versa with negative offsets). An off-
                   set of 0 corresponds to the On mode. The offset option is suitable for pre-machining with
                   rough boundary. Here too, unmachined areas may result.
                   Past: the tool axis leaves the boundary. The milling path ends as soon as there is no longer
                   contact between the tool shaft and the boundary (1). For machining with an exact boundary.
                   Without neighbouring surfaces there is a danger of "nose-diving". This is advantageous
                   when machining raised surface areas (2): complete machining of border areas. Cavities (3):
                   No "nose-diving" of the cutter in the border area.

                   Contact: The milling path ends as soon as there is no longer contact between the tool geom-
                   etry and the surface limited by the boundary (1). This ensures complete machining of the
                   surface. Depending on the slope angle of the surface, the boundary may be crossed. With-
                   out neighbouring surfaces there is a danger of "nose-diving".

                   Tolerance (3): This is only possible for contact edge behaviour. Offsets the boundary with
                   the given distance, thereby avoiding the risk of "nose-diving". In general, an offset value of
                   0.2 mm is sufficient. Note that in some cases, in particular single surface situations, a finer
                   setting may be required. Due to technical limitations, only values > 0 are allowed.

         Macros
                 Plunge macro
                 Various plunge strategies for infeed movement to the next machining level are available for
                 all level-by-level machining cycles (except Z Level Finishing). Axial (A): the infeed movement
                 is executed as a linear movement in Z direction.
                 Use the axial plunge macro for:
                 · Infeed without stock removal (user-defined plunge point is outside of stock or bound-

                       ary).
                 · Pre-drilling at the existing user-defined plunge point.
                 · Axial plunging with a tool suitable for vertical chip removal.
                 Helical (B): used to remove the stock of 3D pockets. Helix radius (1): offset of the cutter cen-
                 tre point relative to the axis of the helix (= Z axis through plunge point). Angle (2): lead angle
                 of the helix. The number of revolutions executed by the tool in the course of the infeed move-
                 ment is computed from the value of the vertical stepdown and the lead angle of the helix.
                 The helix direction is defined by the selected orientation (climb/conventional milling).
                 Ramp (C): ramping-in proceeds along the first milling path. Angle (3): enter the lead angle of
                 the ramp.

                 Approach macro / Retract macro
                 Retract macros are additional motions during infeed on the first milling path of a job, infeeds
                 between the milling paths via the clearance plane or clearance distance. The following
                 approach macros are available depending on the machining cycle: Axial, Perpendicular, Cir-
                 cular, Tangential as well as the ramp macro for level-by-level material removal.

                                During roughing, the approach macros only apply to the Finish pass during
                                machining parallel to the axis.

                 Retract macros are additional motions during retraction after the last milling path of a cycle,
                 retraction for horizontal stepover between the milling paths via the clearance plane or clear-
                 ance distance. The following approach macros are available depending on the machining
                 cycle.
                 Axial (1): linear movement along the tool axis towards or away from the part. Enter length of
                 movement. Closed and concave (inner) contours.
                 Circular (2): approach and retract movements are performed in a quarter circle arc. Enter
                 radius of the circle.

                Accuracy when extending or reducing the tool (see the calculate lengthoption).

                Calculate length

                The Reduce and Extend options are available if a holder, extension or spindle is defined.
                Only the Reduce option is available for all 5X cycles.

                Extend (1): if there is a tool extension, holder or spindle collision, hyperMILL will calculate a
                larger tool reach, based on the tool reach defined for the tool. So there is no limit to the max-
                imum tool reach ­ the maximum possible tool reach of a real tool is simply ignored! This is
                the preferred option if the selected tool is available in different lengths (e.g., short, long, extra
                long) and the length calculation has not yet determined the suitable real tool for the assem-
                bly. In this case, the tool is merely a geometry description with an unlimited shank length.

                Reduce (2): HyperMILL calculates the shortest possible collision-free tool reach, based on
                the defined tool reach of the tool. This is the preferred option if you only want to calculate tool
                lengths that are also actually possible for the tool selected in the assembly. In this assembly,
                you must select the maximum tool reach as the tool reach.

           3D machining                                  9 Setup
           Collision checks for areas outside the stock

                          Displaying the calculated tool length

                          If the same tool used in several jobs, the tool length calculated by hyperMILL is displayed. In
                          this instance, after creating the toolpath file(s), select the tool in the browser and select the
                          usage function in the shortcut menu.

                          For unresolvable collision

                          Unresolvable collisions may occur if:

                          · It is not possible to avoid a collision in 5X machining as a result of a change to the tool
                                orientation.

                          · In 3D machining, it is not possible to resolve a collision involving the tool extension,
                                holder and/or spindle by extending the tool (see calculating the tool length) or a collision
                                will occur with the thick shank.

                          If a collision cannot be avoided by changing the tool orientation (5X) or tool length calcula-
                          tion, various options are available for the machining strategies:
                          Stop: the toolpath calculation stops when a collision occurs (applies for all machining strate-
                          gies).

                          Clip: the toolpath is fully calculated. Only the collision-free areas of the toolpaths are output.
                          As a result of rework machining with another tool and/or another tool inclination, the tool-
                          paths found in the collision can be tracked and checked for collisions (applies to all 3D
                          machining strategies).

                          Collision avoidance: with this option, the collision avoidance tool is side-stepped so that the
                          material with the steepest possible tool can be machined as deeply as possible.

                          The toolpaths calculated for the Clip option are used as the basis for the 3D
                          Rework Machiningcycle.

                          An area is determined and graphically displayed within the 3D Automatic Rest
                          Material Machining cycle. Any further machining occurs within the following
                          cycle only: 3D Automatic Rest Material Machining.

                          When the Collision avoidance function is used, a milling area that is not within the stock is
                          also protected against collisions. If the milling area that is outside of the stock only consists
                          of perpendicular surfaces, no collision avoidance takes place; instead, the milling path output
                          is suppressed.

           Collision checks for areas outside the stock

                                       If the part of the milling area that is outside the stock also needs to be checked for collisions
                                       (for example, for defining clamping devices), this area must also contain a shroud surface.

           Tapered tools

                          Tapered tools are checked for collisions for all 5X machining and the machining strategies
                          3D Profile Finishing, 3D Equidistant Finishing and 3D Rework Machining. Compared to cal-

                          culating the machining process with a tool without a tapered cutting edge, the tooltip (ball)

                          may lose contact with the surface during 3D operations.

                NC parameters

                Stop before execution: A stop marker in the toolpath causes the tool to stop. Besides ena-

                Ignore small pockets: in order to protect the tool, pockets whose traversing route on the
                plane is smaller than or the same size as the tool radius are not machined. Enable this func-
                tion for tools that cannot cut over centre (see illustration). Disable this function for tools that
                can cut over centre.

                output in the NC program. Greater distances are subdivided into a corresponding number of
                G1 movements of the specified length. Controlling the G1 length avoids too strong accelera-

                tions of the machine on large planar surfaces.

hyperMILL                 9-19
9 3D machining                     Tools
         Arbitrary Stock Roughing

      Arbitrary Stock Roughing

                                  Z constant machining of pre-fabricated blanks of any shape. Machining proceeds parallel to
                                  the specified contour or parallel to axis.

      Tools

             You can use ball mills, end mills and bullnose end mills. The Core Diameter, Core Height
             and Plunge Angle parameters control the plunge behaviour of the tool during pocket machin-
             ing.

             The following rule applies: if the core diameter and core height values are both 0, the tool
             performs a centre cut. If the plunge angle value in the job definition (see the Macros tab) is
             set to 0, the tool may not plunge. If, in the tool definition (under Technology, also see the tool
             database, ), the plunge angle value is defined as 0 but is set to 2 in the job definition (see the
             Macros tab), the value is coloured red and the following message is displayed:

             Macro plunge angle should be smaller than tool plunge angle.

             If you ignore this message, the value (2) defined on the Macros tab is automatically used in
             the calculation.

      Use bullnose end mills

                                  When working with bullnose endmills, material ridges may remain standing because the
                                  infeed distance is always calculated by considering the total tool diameter (1).

                                  Consider corner radius (2): the infeed (stepover) distance is based on the tool's inner shank
                                  (= shank diameter - 2x corner radius), thus avoiding material ridges.

           Tools

           Use tapered tools

                                       Tapered tools are supported. Please note that the cone of the tool does not depend on the
                                       chamfer length; instead, it is defined using the cone angle (1).

           Strategy

                         Machining Direction

                         Base the selection of the machining direction on the main extension of the machining area.
                         In order to obtain a vertical stepdown also for inclined surfaces, you should tilt the current
                         frame correspondingly, provided the machine tool has a swinging tool head.

                         Contour parallel: Machining is carried out parallel to the contour. The horizontal stepover is
                         executed vertically to the machining direction. The machining direction depends on the cut-
                         ting mode selected (conventional milling/climb milling).

hyperMILL                Machining sequence
                         The tool border behaviour defined on the Boundary dialogue page applies to all strategies.
                         Plane (1): stock removal is carried out plane by plane. If there are several boundaries, these
                         are machined in sequence. If a user-defined plunge point has also been specified, machin-
                         ing only takes place within the related boundary.
                         Pocket (2): stock removal with infeed optimisation: cavities are machined in sequence.

      Planar mode

      Inside-out (1): stock removal takes place parallel to the contour from the inside outwards.

      Rapid in: (2): the redundant paths resulting from the boundary are traversed in rapid mode.
      The tool reference in boundary is set to past.
      Optimised in: (3): in particular as regards more complex models, this option leads to optimi-
      sation of retract movements and avoidance of unnecessary milling movements. Machining is
      carried out from the outside in along the contour.

      Cutting Mode
      For information on the cutting mode, see section Cutting mode.

                                   If climb milling is chosen as the cutting mode, then this is the preferred cutting
                                   mode. However, if necessary for machining, the cutting mode can be changed
                                   from climb milling to conventional milling when calculating the toolpath during
                                   the 3D Arbitrary Stock Roughing cycle.

      Toolpath fillets

      In parallel contour machining, the tools can be smoothed in the plane.

      Radius for horizontal infeed (1): the horizontal infeed between the tool paths is executed with
      an approach and departure radius.

      Fillet radius (2): Abrupt changes in direction within the cutting toolpaths are rounded with the
      specified radius.

                         detection is enabled, this stock allowance also applies to the Z direction.

                         Example 1: roughing a pocket with a final horizontal stock allowance of 1 mm, and at the
                         same time finishing the bottom of the pocket (stock allowance = 0 mm):

                         walls should have a final allowance of 1 mm.

                         walls should not have an allowance.

      Max. step height: Enable if large axial infeeds are possible and, despite this, a continuous
      allowance is to be achieved. An initial downwards vertical stepdown (1) is executed. The
      remaining material on inclined walls is then removed from bottom to top according to the
      defined Max. step height (2). Valid values for the Max. step height parameter must be less
      than or equal to the Vertical stepdown. The actual step height may differ from the Max. step
      height.

      Example calculation of the actual step height:

      Vertical stepdown = 7, Max. step height = 2

      7: 2 = 3.5, rounded up = 4.

      7:4 = 1.75 = actual step height.

                     The strategy is particularly suitable for the high-performance machining of
                     sloped walls and flat transitions.

      Max. step height not enabled (1), Max. step height enabled (2).

                         Automatic (2): if the defined vertical stepdown is greater than the distance between two sur-

      Additional parameters

      Minimal stock removal: Value for the minimum material width between the stock and the
      model in order for material to be removed. If the material width is lower than the defined
      value, no material is removed. For values greater than 0, collision avoidance is automatically
      enabled, thus ensuring that the tool is continuously monitored against the tracked stock.
      Recommendation for calculating the minimum removal: stock tolerance + machining toler-
      ance + desired minimum removal = minimum stock removal. If the Minimal stock removal
      function is enabled, the Vertical stepdown value can be exceeded by up to 25%.

      Finish pass all levels: if this option is enabled, it ensures the tool moves along the defined
      contour, even if no material is cleared. If there is still some rest material, this is cleared first
      and then the spring path is traversed. You should always enable this option if minor changes
      were made to the allowance between two machining passes.

           High Performance Roughing

                                    Introduction
                                       With the High Performance Roughing option, OPEN MIND provides an additional roughing
                                       technology that is characterised by the following features:
                                       · Constant load on the tool and machine during the entire machining sequence.
                                       · Feedrates that are adjusted dynamically to the machining situation
                                       · Machining is always performed using climb milling.
                                       · Feedrate for fast positioning movements

                                                       Please note: You need to purchase a separate licence to use the High Perfor-
                                                       mance Mode. Please contact your OPEN MIND dealer.

                                       High Performance Roughing
                                       High Performance Mode: Enable in order to use the High Performance Mode
                                       Opening cut: Enable if an opening cut should be made.
                                       Zigzag: Enable if machining with alternating orientation/cutting mode is required.
                                       Two different strategies are available for High Performance Mode: Opening cut and Side mill
                                      only. The following applies to both strategies: the toolpaths created with hyperMILL are opti-
                                       mised in terms of the minimum machining time at maximum removal rate, taking into account
                                       dynamic feedrate values for different machining situations.

                                                       The following also applies to both strategies: The Fillet radius parameter must
                                                       be at least 5% of the tool diameter.

                                       Opening cut (1): if this option is enabled, narrow, inaccessible areas (A) with several vertical
                                      stepdowns (full cut) can be opened. A trochoidal strategy may be used. hyperMILL deter-
                                       mines the most suitable strategy for the particular machining situation internally in terms of
                                       the shortest overall machining time.
                                       Side mill only (2): if this option is enabled, no full cut behaviour is allowed. Narrow, inacces-
                                       sible areas (A) are opened with trochoidal movements.

hyperMILL                9-27
9 3D machining                     Tools
         Arbitrary Stock Roughing

      Reposition

      The following applies to the two strategies Opening cut and Side mill only:

      Safety (1): axial movement (in the Z direction) away from the plane currently being
      machined. Default value: Clearance distance * 0.1.

      Feedrate: Value for the maximum achievable feedrate for all movements to reposition the
      tool without material removal.

      Infeed

      Dense area stepover (factor) (1): Lateral infeed for trochoidal movements in narrow, inac-
      cessible areas. The value is multiplied by the Stepover (factor of diameter). A reduction in
      the horizontal stepover in narrow areas may be particularly useful for hard materials.

      Plunge feedrate: Minimum feedrate for plunge movement in closed pockets that cannot be
      accessed from the outside.

      Opening cut

      Adapt the vertical stepdown and the feedrate to the particular machining situation.

      Vertical stepdown (1): The number of stepovers for the vertical stepdown is calculated from
      the vertical stepdown defined on the parameters tab (total infeed).
      Example: If the total infeed is 2 and the vertical stepdown for the opening cut is 0.5, machin-
      ing occurs in 4 infeeds.

      Feedrate: Maximum feedrate for the opening cut.

      Min. feedrate: Enable to specify the minimum feedrate for the opening cut.

hyperMILL                               A change in the feedrate for the opening cut may change the machining strat-
                                        egy for narrow areas (trochoidal > full cut).
                                       hyperMILL determines the most suitable strategy internally in terms of the
                                        shortest overall machining time, taking into account the feedrate value.

                         Entry feedrate
                         A targeted feedrate adjustment at the moment of entry into the material can be especially
                         useful with hard workpiece materials.
                         Factor side entry regulates the lateral approach (not when the position is tangential to the
                         contour) from outside and is referenced to the feedrate XY of the tool.
                         Factor plunge entry affects the helical or ramp plunge into the material from above. This fac-
                         tor is calculated with plunge feedrate.

                         Zigzag
                         Zag feedrate (factor): factor influencing the feedrate of the opposite direction. If climb milling
                         is chosen as cutting mode, the opposite direction feedrate, i.e. the conventional milling fee-
                         drate, is reduced by the specified factor. The 0.8 factor means a feedrate reduction of 20%.

                         Boundary
                         User-defined plunge points are also available for High Performance Mode. Information in
                         section Boundary.

                         Limitations
                         If machining is performed in High Performance Mode a number of standard functions in the
                         Arbitrary Stock Roughing cycle are not available or are limited to a certain setting. In detail,
                         the following default settings currently apply:
                         Strategy tab

                         Machining sequence
                         By default, stock removal of cavities or pockets takes place level-by-level. High Performance
                         Roughing has therefore limited suitability for subsequent machining tasks as no pocket sort-
                         ing takes place.

                         Planar mode
                         By default, infeed is performed optimised in.

                         Cutting mode
                         Machining is always performed using climb milling.

              angle of the helix. The number of revolutions executed by the tool in the course of the infeed

         Optimised Roughing

      Optimised Roughing

                                  Z Level Roughing and Rest Machining of components of any shape.

                                  Machining in Roughing mode can either be performed with the Adaptive Pocket strategy or
                                  the conventional roughing method.

                                  With the Adaptive Pocket strategy, the geometry of rectangular and circular pockets is fitted
                                  into the roughing area in order to calculate highly efficient toolpaths (`High speed cutting').

                                  As a result, higher feedrates can be achieved, direction changes are reduced and linear
                                  machine movements lead to a high dynamic.

                                  In Rest roughing mode, machine remaining rest material areas based on the generated
                                  "resulting stock".

      Tool

                             The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill and lollipop. The
                             Use adaptive pocket option is not available for ball mills.
                             For information on tool definitions, see section Defining a tool in the hyperMILL browser.

                             Free geometry
                             Use free tip geometry for calculation: Use a free tip geometry to calculate the toolpath. The
                             exact positioning makes it possible to optimally incline the area to be machined.

      Strategy

                             Machining mode

                             Machining in Roughing mode can either be performed with the Adaptive Pocket strategy or
                             the conventional roughing method. With the Adaptive Pocket strategy, the geometry of rec-
                             tangular and circular pockets is fitted into the roughing area in order to calculate highly effi-
                             cient toolpaths (`High speed cutting').

                             In Rest material mode, machine the rest material areas remaining after a roughing job based
                             on the resulting stock.

                             High feed machining: Only available for Adaptive Pocket machining jobs. Enable in order to
                             machine with large lateral but small vertical infeed and high feedrate.

                             · The lateral infeed (1) is based on the defined scallop height (2).

9-36                               hyperMILL
           3D machining                            9 Optimised Roughing
           Strategy
                         · A lateral infeed > 50% of the tool diameter is possible.
                         · Complete machining of corners (3).
                         · Smooth rolling in at the start (4).
                         Example: lateral infeed: 22 mm, tool diameter: 35 mm

                         Toolpath fillets

                         Smooth the toolpaths in the plane.

                         Radius for horizontal infeed: The horizontal infeed between the tool paths is rounded with

                         Fillet radius: Abrupt changes in direction are rounded with the specified radius (2).

                         Fillet all toolpaths: Model contour corners are rounded with this radius, with the result that

           3D machining        9 Profile Finishing
           Tools

           Profile Finishing

                                       Allows multi-surface, collision-free milling with different guide curve strategies. Selected
                                       areas can be machined in slope mode.

           Tools

                               The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill and lollipop.

                               Exceptions: Profile Finishing in scallop height mode only supports ball mills,
                               and slope-dependent machining only supports bullnose endmills and ballmills.

                               When using tapered tools, collision avoidance is possible by taking into account the conical
                               shape of the tool for the toolpaths.

                               For further information on selecting a tool and defining tool parameters, see section Defining
                               a tool.

           Strategy

                               Infeed strategy

                               The following are defined in the infeed strategy area:
                               · The profile of the tool movements via a profile definition (standard profiles, free pro-

                                     files).

                               · The type of cut for the tool (Ascending, Descending, Ascending and descending)

                               · The infeed mode between the end point of the first milling path and the start point of the
                                     following milling path.

                               The options that are available in the Profile definition, Type of cut and Infeed mode areas are
                               explained in the following sections using examples.

           Profile definition

                               If a profile has not been defined, the defined boundary (strategy: Boundary curve ) or the
                               boundary for the defined milling surfaces (strategy: Milling surfaces) is used automatically as
                               the profile.

hyperMILL                                                                                                                    9-45
9 3D machining              Strategy
         Profile Finishing

                            When the X axis and Y axis options are used, the X or Y axis of the frame is used as the
                            guide curve.

                            With all the other options, the guide curves are freely definable, which allows the milling
                            paths to be optimally adapted to the surface.

                            Machining angle: Enter the rotation angle required for machining.

                            The machining and infeed directions are based on the guide curves. This setting is the
                            standard setting.

                            Reverse direction
                            Both the milling and infeed direction can be customised in order to make optimal adjust-
                            ments to the milling paths to the surface.
                            Milling path: Reverses the machining direction.
                            Horizontal stepover: Reverses the infeed direction.

                                           Via the selected directions the starting point of machining is defined as well.

                            X axis, Y axis

                            The machining area is to be limited via a boundary. The guide curve for machining is the X
                            axis. In the default setting, the first milling path runs in the positive X direction and the first
                            infeed movement is executed to the left of this, that is, in the positive Y direction.

                            Reverse direction

                            Infeed strategy X axis (A), Y axis (B), Zigzag direct machining.

                            (1) Without reversal, (2) Milling path reversed, (3) Horizontal stepover reversed, (4) Both
                            directions reversed.

                            XY optimised finishing

                            Final fine finishing job step for removing machining marks which can result during Profile Fin-
                            ishingwith standard profiles. This automatic operation uses the profile that is opposite to the
                            selected default profile (X, Y axis) and covers those areas that are machined inadequately
                            using the selected profile.

                            This finish pass can be executed before (option: Before) or after (option: After) machining
                            with the selected standard profile but it can also be used on its own (option: Only optimisa-
                            tion).

                            Slope dependent machining is not available for XY-optimised finishing.

           Strategy

                         Offset

                         A free profile is used as guide curve (1). The toolpaths are computed according to the hori-
                         zontal stepover and are equidistant to the course and length of the guide curve. For open
                         guide curves, the machining area is limited with a boundary (2). In the default setting, the first
                         milling path runs in the direction of the guide curve and the first infeed movement is executed
                         to the left of the first milling path.

hyperMILL                9-49
9 3D machining              Strategy
         Profile Finishing

                            With closed guide curves, machining is from the outside in (1). In the default setting, it is from
                            the inside out (2). If the boundary is a closed guide curve, you can execute 3D pocketing.

                            Normal
                            Profiles are calculated perpendicular to the guide curve (1). The limiting boundary deter-
                            mines the profile length (2). In the default setting, the first milling path runs in the direction of
                            the normal to the left of the guide curve and the horizontal stepover is executed in the direc-
                            tion of the guide curve. Particularly suitable for rest material areas in steep surfaces or
                            recessed grounds.

                                           A strong bend in the guide curve can result in overlaps of the normal line pro-
                                           files.

                            Ruled

                            Ruled profiles require two guide curves that do not intersect and that have the same direc-
                            tion.

9-50                                  hyperMILL
           3D machining                              9 Profile Finishing
           Strategy
                         Reverse direction
                         If the guide curves are in an opposed direction, reverse the direction of one guide curve
                         using the 1st profile or 2nd profile option.
                         In the default setting, the first milling path runs from the inner (shorter) to the outer (longer)
                         guide curve (1) and the horizontal stepover is applied to the outer (longer) guide curve (2).

                         This type of machining defines a natural limitation between the two guide curves. In addition,
                         a defined boundary limits the machining area.

                         Use the tool reference parameters (Boundary dialogue page) to control the behaviour of the
                         tool at the guide curves. A boundary does not have to be defined.

                         Application areas: Finishing of corners, Machining of symmetrical parts.

                         If the internal guideline is defined as a point, and the outer guideline as a closed contour,
                         machining is executed radially (1).

                         Flow profile

                         Two guide curves (1, 2), which do not intersect and that have the same direction, are to be
                         defined as profiles. If the guide curves are in an opposed direction, reverse the direction of
                         one guide curve.

9 3D machining              Strategy
         Profile Finishing

                            Reverse direction

                            If the guide curves are in an opposed direction, reverse the direction of one guide curve
                            using the 1st profile or 2nd profile option.

                            In the case of closed curves, the start positions must be aligned, that is, are not displaced
                            from one another. In the default setting, the first milling path runs on the inner (shorter) guide
                            curve and the first infeed is executed to the left of the first milling path.

                            Synchronise toolpaths

                            Synchronisation lines (1, 2): Connection lines or curves between the two guide curves (3, 4)
                            that influence the calculation of the distances on the inner guide curve. Surface machining
                            can be controlled, and the infeed (stepover) distance adjusted, via a variable arrangement of
                            the synchronization lines.

                            Guide curve

                            Machining on a guide curve or in a narrow strip parallel to a guide curve. Any 2D or 3D
                            curves and splines can be used as guide curves. More than one guide curve are permitted
                            per cycle. The guide curve is treated as the positive X axis.

           Strategy

                         Offset area

                         Use the from and to parameters to define a positive (X+) or negative (X-) distance to the
                         guide curve, within which machining will take place. If from and to are identical, only one
                         path is machined.

hyperMILL                Pocket
                         Pre-machined pockets are finished with the pocket profile. Closed 3D contours can be used
                         as the profile. One or more pocket profiles can be defined per cycle. When pocket profiles
                         are inside one another, island detection is automatic.

9 3D machining              Strategy
         Profile Finishing

      Type of cut

                            When the type of cut is set to Ascending, upward cutting takes place. Application: Roughing
                            close to the surface to remove material (allowance) from a preceding roughing operation (1).

                            When the type of cut is set to Descending, drill cutting takes place. Application: Recess
                            machining of steep walls (2).

                            When the type of cut is set to Up and down, the milling path follows the surface (3) of the
                            model. Standard method for Finishing. The type of cut does not apply to pocket profile.

      Infeed mode

                            The infeed mode describes the type of the horizontal stepover between the endpoint of a NC
                            path and the starting point of the following path. The Infeed mode does not apply to the
                            Pocket profile.

                            With the options Zigzag direct and Zigzag smooth, the machining direction changes after
                            each passed profile. An approach macro is used for the infeed to the first milling path and a
                            retract macro is used for retraction after the last milling path.

9-54                                  hyperMILL
           3D machining  9 Profile Finishing
           Strategy

                                        If the linear movement would cause damage to the workpiece, the system
                                        guides the tool with surface contact (no material being removed) around the
                                        workpiece.

                         Zigzag direct: If no return macro is enabled (1), the infeed movement is carried out on the
                         shortest path in the machining feedrate (G1) on the surface. If a return macro is enabled (2),
                         every retract and infeed movement is corrected by the selected retract and approach macro.
                         Depending on the defined retract mode, the horizontal stepover occurs at the clearance dis-
                         tance in G1 or at the clearance plane in G0.

hyperMILL                9-55
9 3D machining              Strategy
         Profile Finishing

                            Zigzag smooth: The infeed between the milling paths is the shape of loop. These loops
                            reduce jolting and the mechanical load on the machine is reduced. This strategy is primarily
                            intended for high-speed milling. The limiting boundary may be traversed when moving along
                            the loops.

                            With the Diagonal and Parallel options, the machining direction is always the same and
                            defined by the profile direction. The horizontal stepover is performed relative to the defined
                            retract mode to the security clearance in G1 or security plane in G0. Each retract and infeed
                            movement is corrected by the selected approach and retract macro.

                            When the Diagonal option (1) is used, the infeed is diagonal from the end point to the next
                            start point. When the Parallel (2) option is used, the tool initially retracts parallel to the gener-
                            ated milling path to the start point of the (vertical) infeed movement. This is followed by a
                            horizontal stepover using the shortest distance possible.

                            Machining mode
                            The machining of surfaces with a large slope angle frequently leads to unsatisfactory results
                            during Profile Finishing as a large amount of rest material remains. To save machining time,
                            steep surface areas can be optionally excluded from machining, in dependence on their
                            slope, by specifying a maximum surface slope angle.
                            Slope mode: Enable if slope-dependent machining should take place and use from to define
                            the lower limit and to to define the upper limit of the surface slope of the surfaces to be
                            machined.

                                           Slope dependent machining is only possible with bullnose endmills and ball
                                           mills. The steep areas not machined here can be machined with the 3D Z Level
                                           Finishing cycle in Slope mode. Here, the flat areas are excluded from machin-
                                           ing.

           Strategy
                         Grouping toolpaths: Machining areas are combined and the number of fast travel move-
                         ments is reduced, particularly in the case of nested boundaries or in slope-dependent

                         (1) Option not activated, (2) Option activated.

                         Smooth overlap: Only available for slope-dependent machining. Enable if you want the tool-

                            Vertical infeed mode

                            The vertical infeed mode defines the mode of computation for the vertical distances between
                            the milling paths.

                            Only finishing: Only a finishing path is created.

                            Constant vertical stepdown: The stepdown takes place with a fixed vertical increment.
                            Parallel vertical stepdown: The vertical stepdown takes place parallel to the top of the work-
                            piece. Define the Vertical stepdown and the Material height.

                            Stock allowance

                            Additional allowance XY: This additional horizontal stock allowance allows machining to take
                            place with different stock allowances for the bottom and side walls of the machining area.

                            Horizontal infeed mode

                            The infeed mode defines the mode of computation for the distance between the particular
                            NC paths.

                            The computation of the path distance for ruled profiles and flow profiles can be
                            controlled via user-defined synchronization lines.

                            Constant stepover (1): Infeed with fixed horizontal increment. The vertical distance between
                            the toolpaths (Z-Levels) is constant for all Z-levels Specify the horizontal stepover. Machin-
                            ing of steep surfaces causes steps in the surface. Possible remedies: Machining at an angle
                            (turning the workpiece around the Z axis) Select Scallop height mode (see below) For round
                            parts select one of the guide curve strategies.

                            Scallop height (2): Machining is only possible with ball mills. A predefined scallop height is
                            not exceeded even on steep side surfaces. The Z-distance between the toolpaths depends
                            on the surface curvature and steepness. The complete Z-level is taken into consideration
                            and the smallest value found is used to determine the stepdown.

                            Scallop height value: Enter the required scallop height. The Scallop height infeed mode will
                            significantly increase the calculation time for the milling paths.

                            Minimum horizontal stepover: Limits the distance between the milling paths. Avoids too fine
                            a stepdown when the given scallop height cannot be retained because of very steep side
                            walls. Apply this for machining areas with very steep side walls (steepness > 40°) and very
                            smooth surfaces.

                         Constant on curve projection: A guide curve (1) is projected onto the surfaces and stepped
                         equally on the basis of the specified infeed. This significantly improves surface quality. The
                         minimum horizontal stepover limits the distance of the paths, particularly in steep areas.
                         Only one profile (spline, line, curve) can be defined. Vertical surfaces cannot be machined.

           3D machining  9 Z Level Finishing
           Strategy

           Z Level Finishing

                                       Z constant finishing with optional slope-dependent machining.

                                       By adapting the vertical stepdown values to the surface flow especially for steep surfaces,
                                       unnecessary fine infeed increments are avoided and an optimal line distance is thus guaran-
                                       teed.

           Strategy      Tools, frame
                         The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill, woodruff and lol-
                         lipop.
                         Exceptions: Level finishing in scallop height mode does not support end mills, while slope-
                         dependent machining only supports bullnose endmills and ballmills.

                                        Tapered tools may be used, but the conical shape is not used in the toolpath
                                        collision avoidance calculations. Therefore please ensure that you perform a
                                        visual inspection through simulation to verify the results.

                         Lollipop mills can be used for undercut machining.
                         For information on selecting the tool, defining tool parameters and selecting the frame, see
                         section Defining a tool and section NC system and frames.

                         Machining sequence
                         Plane (1): machining is carried out level by level. In each Z-level the selected approach and
                         retract macros will be executed.
                         Pocket (2): Contour pockets or islands are machined in sequence.
                         If there are several boundaries, these are machined in sequence. If a user-defined plunge
                         point is also present, machining only takes place within the related boundary.
                         In addition, select cutting mode and infeed mode.
                         The vertical infeed (stepdown) is carried out level by level. In each Z-level the selected
                         approach and retract macros will be executed. In addition, select cutting mode and infeed
                         mode.

hyperMILL                9-63
9 3D machining              Strategy
         Z Level Finishing

                            Prefer spiral: Machining is performed in one continuous toolpath with a complete (1) or an
                            approximate spiral-shaped (2) vertical stepdown. Macros are only carried out at the start and
                            the end of the path. In addition, select the cutting mode. Slope dependent machining is not
                            available for spiral-shaped infeed.

                            Connect strategy

                            Ramp connect: Level-by-level machining with ramp-shaped, filleted stepdown between the
                            levels. The last toolpath will be closed. Advantage compared to the complete spiral machin-
                            ing is the shorter calculation time while obtaining the same surface quality results.

                            Connect factor: Defines the length of the ramp as follows: Ramp length = Tool diameter x
                            Factor. This value should be defined with consideration of the stepdown distance and the
                            machine kinematics. If the connect factor is 0, infeed takes place in a complete spiral-shaped
                            vertical path.

                            The first and last toolpaths are machined as closed paths in one level. Between these there
                            will be a spiral-shaped toolpath.

                            Zigzag: Machining with alternating orientation. The selected approach and retract macros
                            are executed for the approach of the first NC path and the retraction from the last passed NC
                            path.

                            If a Return macro is activated, every retract and infeed movement is corrected by the
                            selected retract and approach macro.

9-64                                  hyperMILL
           3D machining                              9 Z Level Finishing
           Strategy
                         Infeed mode
                         The infeed mode controls the stepdown to the next level within a machining area.
                         Rapid: When moving between two levels, a rapid movement to the clearance distance/plane
                         takes place between the approach and retract macros of the two levels. This mode is always
                         used during level-by-level machining when multiple pockets are to be machined.
                         Direct (1): The infeed movement from the end point of the retract macro to the start point of
                         the approach macro is carried out on the shortest path at the feedrate.
                         Smooth (2): The stepdown between the end position of the retract macro and the start point
                         of the approach macro are filleted (rounded).
                         If this infeed mode is used in combination with circular approach and retract macros, the
                         result will be a helical transition between the toolpaths. Such loop-shaped paths reduce jolt-
                         ing and mechanical load on the machine.

hyperMILL                Cutting Mode
                         For information on climb milling and conventional milling, see section Cutting mode.

                         Toolpath fillets
                         Fillet interior corners: Smooth filleting (rounding) of internal milling paths for contour pockets
                         or islands.
                         Fillet radius: Abrupt changes in direction within the cutting toolpaths are rounded with the
                         specified radius.

                         Machining mode
                         Slope mode: During Z Level Finishing, the machining of surfaces with a small slope angle
                         only leads to unsatisfactory quality (a lot of rest material). To save time these surface areas
                         can be excluded from machining with the Slope mode in dependence on their slope angle.
                         Slope-dependent machining is only possible with bullnose endmills and ball mills, and can-
                         not be used in conjunction with a spiral stepdown.
                         Slope angle: Enter the minimum surface slope angle. Only those areas will be machined
                         which have a larger slope angle.
                         The flat areas not machined here can be machined with the 3D Finishing cycle in slope
                         mode. There the steep surface areas are excluded from machining.
                         Smooth overlap: Only available for slope-dependent machining. Enable if you want the tool-
                         paths of flat and steep areas to overlap. The overlap (1) ensures a very high level of surface
                         quality in the transition area between flat and steep surfaces. (2) Transition area activated,
                         (3) Transition area not activated.

                                                                                                                                                             9-65
9 3D machining                                                                  Strategy
         Z Level Finishing

                            The overlap area is visualised in the graphic for illustrative purposes only. This area is not
                            graphically highlighted in the model.

                            (4) 3D Profile Finishing, (5) 3D Z Level Shape Finishing

                            Options
                            Bottom to top milling: Activate when machining is to take place from bottom to top.

      Parameters

                            Basic Machining Parameters
                            Notes on definition of basic machining parameters:

                            Top, Bottom                                         see section Machining area
