9-66                                                                                                             hyperMILL
           3D machining                              9 Z Level Finishing
           Strategy
                         Vertical infeed mode
                         The infeed mode defines the mode of computation for the distance between the particular
                         NC paths.
                         Constant stepdown (1): machining with a fixed infeed depth. Enter the increment for the ver-
                         tical stepdown.
                         Scallop height (2): a pre-defined scallop height is not exceeded during machining. The Z-dis-
                         tance between the toolpaths depends on the surface curvature and steepness. It is calcu-
                         lated over the cutting plane and the smallest value found is used for machining.

hyperMILL                Scallop height value: enter the required scallop height. Please note that the infeed mode
                         scallop height will significantly increase the calculation time.
                         Minimum vertical stepdown: limits the distance between the milling paths. Avoids too fine a
                         stepdown when the given scallop height cannot be retained because of very steep side
                         walls.
                         Apply this for machining areas with very steep side walls (steepness > 40°) and very smooth
                         surfaces.
                         Maximal vertical stepdown: Upper limit for the vertical distance of the toolpaths for prevent-
                         ing tool breakages.

                         Plane level detection
                         Off: Defined vertical stepdown is adhered to for each roughing level, irrespective of the sur-
                         face of the workpiece.
                         Automatic (1): If the defined vertical stepdown value is greater than the distance between
                         two surfaces of the workpiece, the system automatically inserts an intermediate step with a
                         smaller vertical stepdown value for the planar surfaces of the workpiece.
                         Only planar faces (2): available only for the constant stepdown mode. Only the plane-parallel
                         surfaces inside the boundary are machined, but not cleared. Therefore, you must use
                         another machining strategy to clear the planar surfaces. Planar surfaces on the same level
                         as the top or bottom are not recognized in this mode. Therefore please increase/reduce the
                         Top/Bottom settings accordingly.

      Boundary              Path compensation
                            The Compensated path function may be used for path compensation. Information in section
                            Path compensation. If the compensated path option is enabled and the Return macro disa-
                            bled, a warning is given and the return macro is activated. If the macro length is 0, it is
                            aborted with an error.

                            If no boundary is defined, the outside contours of the model are used as the machining
                            boundaries. One or more boundaries are permitted that may be one inside the other to limit
                            the area; however, they may not be nested several times. The boundary curve (1) is valid for
                            the axis position of the tool.
                            For further information, see section Machining area definition

                            Plunge point (1): Enable to define the XY coordinates at which the infeed in Z takes place
                            onto the next finishing level. If the option is not enabled, hyperMILL automatically looks for
                            the point with the greatest milling depth (2) and uses the corresponding XY coordinates for
                            the plunge point (P). If this results in areas that cannot be reached from a plunge point, the
                            system automatically defines several plunge points.

9-68                                  hyperMILL
           3D machining  9 Z Level Finishing
           Strategy

                         Only one plunge point can be defined manually for each cycle. All areas to be machined
                         within the cycle must be approachable from this point. Areas, which are invisible for the tool
                         axis, cannot be machined. The plunge point must be situated at the place with the greatest
                         bottom stock value.

                         End with plunge point: If a plunge point is defined, machining can end at the defined plunge
                         point. The retract movement then takes place at the plunge point.

                         Trim to stock: Enable to use the stock to trim the toolpaths. A defined Offset value is taken
                         into account.

                         Trim to milling area: Enable to use a milling area to trim the toolpaths. The tool does not
                         touch the model. Available for ball mills and bullnose end mills.

                         (1) Trim to milling area is not activated. (2) Trim to milling area is activated. (3) Trim to milling
                         area is activated, offset is 2. The offset is calculated from the tool contact point horizontally to
                         the milling area. (4) Trim to milling area is activated, offset is 0. An offset of 0 means that the
                         toolpath is trimmed at the first contact point to the milling area, and for this reason this setting
                         is not recommended.

              Macros        Boundary projection
                            The defined boundary can be projected in any desired direction in order to better limit the
9-70                        area to be machined. This is particularly useful when the boundary can be defined more eas-
                            ily from another direction than that of the frame. The boundary can only be projected when
                            ball mills are used. For further information, see section Boundary projection.

                            Approach and retract macros are used to define the tool approach at the start point and the
                            tool retraction from the end point of the machining. This behaviour can either be defined
                            manually or calculated automatically.

                            Macro mode
                            Automatic: The approach and retract macros are calculated automatically.
                            Manual: Define the approach and retract macros manually.

                            Approach macro / Retract macro
                            Smooth: The approach or retract movement is performed smoothly in a circular motion.
                            Length: Length of the approach/retract movement.
                            Lateral/Axial clearance: Clearance in the axial or X/Y direction that can be travelled without a
                            collision.
                            Max. axial lift: Maximum length of lifting movement in the axial direction.
                            The following tool movements are available as approach and retract behaviour for the Man-
                            ual macro mode: Perpendicular, Circular, Tangential. Ramp (only as an approach macro).
                            These additional tool movements are only ever carried out if they do not result in a collision.
                            For further information, see section Macros.

                            Feedrate macros
                            Feedrate for approach and retract macros. If no feedrate is defined here, the macros are run
                            with the Feedrate XY that is defined on the Tool dialogue page.

                            Return macro
                            If Return macro is enabled, horizontal stepover is executed between the milling paths via the
                            clearance plane or clearance distance. The activated approach or retract macro is executed
                            for each retract or infeed movement.
                            Macro simultaneous: Available for the cycles 5X Z Level Finishing, 5X Swarf Cutting one
                            Curve and 5X Shape Offset Finishing. The transition to the macro movement takes place
                            without abruptly changing direction and without slowing down the machining speed. Visible
                            machining marks are avoided.

           Shape level finishing

                                       Z-Level machining for steep areas. Optionally, the z-level cuts can be replaced by cuts paral-
                                       lel to any shape.

                                       The shape offset option requires a selection of bottom surfaces which form a significantly
                                       larger area in Job frame XY projection.

                                       This reduces retract movements for appropriate geometry. Conical tools may be used.

           Tools         The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill and lollipop. For
           Strategy      information on tool definitions, see section Defining a tool in the hyperMILL browser.

                         Machining options
                         Edges only: Only available for the Shape offset mode. All lateral walls will be machined in a
                         single axial infeed. The value of the Surface parameter will not be considered.
                         Side walls: all lateral walls will be machined in multiple axial infeeds. The area to be
                         machined (1) is specified using the boundary curves or milling surfaces. For information on
                         machining sequence and cutting mode, see section and section Cutting mode.

                         Mode
                         Shape offset (A): The shape of the toolpaths follows the defined bottom surfaces (2). Sur-
                         face (3) and depth (4) must be defined as an offset to the bottom surfaces. Machining below
                         the bottom surfaces is not possible. The parameter depth must therefore be > = 0.
                         Z-Plane (B): Machining is carried out level by level. Surface (3) and depth (4) are defined
                         automatically by hyperMILL based on the defined model. Alternatively, both can also be
                         manually defined directly on the model.

hyperMILL                9-73
9 3D machining                  Strategy
         Shape level finishing

                                Machining sequence
                                Axial sorting: Areas like corners or pockets are sorted axially and machined consecutively,
                                so that empty paths and machining times are reduced.
                                Prefer spiral: Machining is performed in one continuous toolpath with a complete or an
                                approximate spiral-shaped, vertical stepdown.
                                Allow zigzag: Machining occurs with an alternating orientation/cutting mode.

                                Geometry
                                Bottom surfaces (2): additional surfaces with which the shape of the toolpaths and the verti-
                                cal machining area are defined.

                                               If no milling surfaces or a boundary curve are defined, the bottom faces (seen
                                               from Z direction) must include the entire model. If no milling surfaces or a
                                               boundary curve are defined, the bottom surfaces (seen from the Z direction)
                                               must include the machining area.

                                Toolpath fillets
                                Fillet radius (1): Abrupt changes in direction within the cutting toolpaths are rounded with the
                                specified radius.

           Tools

           Iso Machining

                                       This cycle is primarily used for the exact machining of individual or less continuous surfaces.
                                       The milling paths follow the course of ISO lines (U, V) so that they are optimally adapted to
                                       the surface flow.

                                       Several neighbouring surfaces can be machined in one job step if a flowing transition exists
                                       between the ISO lines of these surfaces and the surfaces are not trimmed. Above all, excel-
                                       lent milling profiles result for rounded surfaces.

                                       Trimmed surfaces within the machining area will not be machined coherently. Each surface
                                       will be machined individually.

           Tools         You can use the following milling tools as reference and machining tools. These include: Ball
           Strategy      mill, End mill, Bullnose end mill.

                         Tapered tools may be used, but the conical shape is not used in the toolpath
                         collision avoidance calculations.

                         Therefore please ensure that you perform a visual inspection through simula-
                         tion to verify the results.

                         Information on:

                         Selecting the tool            see section Defining a tool
                         Defining the tool parameters  see section Defining a tool
                         Selecting the frame           see section NC system and frames

                         Strategy

                         Iso orientation: The milling paths follow the course of the ISO lines (U, V) of the selected sur-
                         faces.

hyperMILL                                                                                9-77
9 3D machining                                                                                                  Strategy
         Iso Machining
                        To machine neighbouring surfaces within a boundary, the surfaces must meet without any
                        gaps and flowing transitions of the ISO lines are required at the common edge curves.
                        Jumps or changes in direction are not permitted.
                        If two surfaces border each other with ISO parameters that flow into each other, but whose U
                        and V lines are defined in an opposing manner (1), the ISO lines of the second surface are
                        automatically adapted to those of the first surface (2).

                        Global orientation: The milling paths run crossways or parallel to the longest boundary curve
                        of the selected surfaces. The selected surfaces should not have more than two adjacent
                        faces. Adjacent here also includes contact via a common boundary curve, but not contact via
                        isolated points.

                        Example:

                        (1) All selected surfaces have a maximum of two adjacent faces and are suitable for machin-
                        ing. The resulting milling paths are optimal.

                        (2) The surfaces 1 to 4 have three adjacent faces each and are not suitable for machining.
                        The resulting milling paths are not optimal.

                        Iso machining is particularly suitable for surfaces that are arranged in a chain or
                        circular manner.

9-78                    hyperMILL

           Strategy

                         surfaces is not relevant for the Global orientation strategy.
                         Machining direction
                         U parameter / V parameter: Define the machining direction and infeed direction. Available for
                         the Iso orientation strategy.

                         In the default setting, the first milling path runs in the positive direction of the selected ISO
                         parameter and the first infeed movement to the next milling path is executed in the positive
                         direction of the other ISO parameter.

                         Crossway / Flow: Define the machining direction and infeed direction. Available for the
                         Global orientation strategy. The machining direction is either crossway (1) or flow (2), that is,
                         parallel to the longest boundary curve of the selected surfaces.

                          frame.

                          confirm the selection.

         Complete Finishing

      Complete Finishing

                                  Z-level finishing of flat and steep surfaces, with optional pocket-shaped machining of flat

                             (3) Transition area not activated.

                             graphically highlighted in the model.

         Equidistant Finishing

      Equidistant Finishing

                                  Finishing with constant infeed that ensures a high surface quality, even with steep surfaces,
                                  while simultaneously reducing the cutter load. Particularly suitable for high-speed milling.

      Strategy

                                Infeed strategy
                                Equidistant: Machining with constant infeed.
                                Profiles (1): It is possible to select multiple closed profiles (boundaries) that are not nested.

                                Offset: The selected profile curves are offset with the defined value (positive/negative).
                                Use as 3D curve: The selected profile curves are not projected onto the machining surfaces.
                                Machining always takes place parallel to a contour and the limited area is machined in Axis
                                mode. The path ends when the tool axis is located on the curve.

                                Path direction / Stepover direction
                                The path direction is either Clockwise or Counterclockwise. The stepover direction is either
                                inside-out or outside-in.

9-96                                      hyperMILL
           3D machining                            9 Equidistant Finishing
           Strategy
                         Toolpath connection
                         Skip first path: The first toolpath (1) is calculated but not machined. Avoids double machining
                         when the selected machining curve has been extracted from the toolpath in the last machin-
                         ing plane of a preceding plane-by-plane cycle (for example, Z Level Finishing).
                         Connect factor: Length and rounding of the ramp-shaped transition between the planes,
                         depending on the tool diameter.
                         Ramp length = Tool diameter x Connect factor.
                         The Connect factor value should be defined in relation to the path distance (infeed) and the
                         machine kinematics. The larger the factor, the smoother the connection transition between
                         the paths will be, but a larger factor will also increase the calculation time.
                         (2) Connect factor = 0.5, (3) Connect factor = 2.

                         Flow: This strategy is particularly suitable for HSC machining.

                         Profiles: Two guide curves (1, 2), which do not intersect and that have the same direction,
                         must be defined as profiles.

hyperMILL                9-97
9 3D machining                  Strategy
         Equidistant Finishing

                                Additional surfaces

                                (A) Machining of steep areas through selection of profile curves (1 and 2) and Drive surfaces
                                (3). The defined profile curves must lie on the selected drive surface areas. This method
                                ensures that, even in steep areas, no residual stock (4) remains, as could be the case when
                                applying the Flow (B) infeed strategy.

                                Reverse direction

                                If the guide curves are in an opposed direction, reverse the direction of one guide curve (1st
                                profile / 2nd profile). In the case of closed curves, the start positions must be aligned, that is,
                                are not displaced from one another. In the default setting, the first milling path runs on the
                                inner (shorter) guide curve and the first infeed is executed to the left of the first milling path.

                                Synchronise toolpaths

                                Equal (A): The two guide curves are divided up into the same number of segments. The start
                                and end points of the respective part segments are linked.

                                Distance (B): Here synchronization uses lines with the shortest distance in each case
                                between the first and second guide curve. Make sure that a unique point on the second
                                curve is allocated to each point on the first curve, and that this second point has the shortest
                                distance to the first point from the direction of the tool axis.

9-98                                      hyperMILL
           3D machining                                                      9 Equidistant Finishing

           Form Pocket

                                       Finishing of pockets with free-form floor.

                                       Here, the pocket contour is automatically determined based on a reference plane (R-PLN).
                                       Within this contour, the milling paths are calculated parallel to the contour from the inside
                                       outward and are projected onto the pocket floor. In this way, free-form surfaces of the male
                                       and female moulds of a deep-drawing tool can be produced within the pocket geometry of
                                       the supporting base in one work step.

           Tools         The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill and bullnose end mill.
           Strategy      Information on:

                         Selecting the tool            see section Defining a tool
                         Defining the tool parameters  see section Defining a tool
                         Selecting the frame           see section NC system and frames

                         Machining sequence

                         Plane (1): machining is carried out level by level. In each Z-level the selected approach and
                         retract macros will be executed. If there are several boundaries, these are machined in
                         sequence. If a user-defined starting point is also present, machining only takes place within
                         the related boundary.

                         Pocket (2): Stock removal with infeed optimisation. Cavities are machined in sequence.

         Pencil Milling

       Pencil Milling

                                   Automatically recognise grooves of a model and generate toolpaths running parallel to the
                                   contour for each groove. The grooves can be cut free by a rough cut with a reference tool, in
                                   order to guarantee for the following machining of the adjacent surfaces an accurate
                                   approach and retract behaviour of the tool. The Pencil Milling cycle is mainly used as a
                                   preparation for High Speed Milling.

       Tools

                         The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill, bullnose end mill and lollipop.

                         Tapered tools may be used, but the conical shape is not used in the toolpath collision avoid-
                         ance calculations. When using tapered tools, please ensure that you perform a visual check
                         for collisions using a simulation.

                         Information on:

                         Selecting the tool            see section Defining a tool
                         Defining the tool parameters  see section Defining a tool
                         Selecting the frame           see section NC system and frames

9-106                                                                                    hyperMILL
           3D machining                                9 Pencil Milling
           Tools
                         Reference tool
                         The reference tool is used to calculate the grooves. It is of the same type as the machining
                         tool. The reference tool is defined based on the diameter. As a rule of thumb: You want the
                         diameter of the reference tool to be up to 20% greater than the diameter of the machining
                         tool.

           Strategy                     The reference diameter should be selected so that the reference tool can no
                                        longer completely remove the stock of the groove. In other words, there should
                                        always be two contact points with the surface so that the groove can be recog-
                                        nised.

                         Frame
                         The frame orientation is valid for computing the grooves as well as for machining.

                         Cutting mode
                         Select the required cutting mode. The cutting mode is valid for all machining areas if machin-
                         ing is not slope-dependent and is valid for flat machining areas if machining is slope-depend-
                         ent. Climb milling (1), Conventional milling (2).

hyperMILL                Machining mode
                         Off: Machining is carried out over all areas with climb or conventional milling.
                         Tilt angle (1): Face slope angle, from which the machining strategy changes. Define for all
                         slope dependent machining options.

9 3D machining                     Tools
         Automatic Rest Machining

       Automatic Rest Machining

                                   Remachining of separate rest material areas left during a finishing cycle. Based on roughing
                                   or finishing paths that have already been created, unmachined areas are automatically
                                   detected. These areas are machined with smaller tools or by changing parameter settings,
                                   without air cuts. Slope-dependent machining and the choice between different machining
                                   strategies are also possible.

       Tools

              As well as reference tool or as machining tool the following cutter types can be used: Ball
              mill, Lollipop and Bullnose end mill.
              The following applies to cavities: To ensure tidy machining without any remaining material
              ridges, the cavity width must not exceed the following value: 1.8 x tool diameter.
              With bullnose endmills, even deepest material areas can be machined more easily and tidily.

              Reference
              The reference tool is used for the computation of the rest material areas.
              Type: Type of reference tool may be different from type of machining tool. When the Rest
              material reference cycle option is enabled, the previously unmachined rest material area is
              selected as the area to be machined.
              Diameter: A requirement is: Reference tool > machining tool.

                             If you select bullnose end mill as a reference tool type, machining is only possi-
                             ble in entire part mode!

9-110  Machining Strategy

                                   Rest material optimisation
                                   The following applies to the Cavities and open areas and Only cavities optimisation meth-
                                   ods:
                                   Steep areas in cavities always undergo Z constant machining while flat areas in cavities (bot-
                                   toms) are always machined parallel to the contour.
                                   The following optimisation methods are available:

                                                                                                                                                           hyperMILL
           3D machining   9 Automatic Rest Machining
           Tools

           Standard

                          There is no optimisation when machining the rest material. This strategy corresponds to
                          standard machining in earlier hyperMILL versions. Machining can be non-slope-dependent
                          or slope-dependent.

           Cavities and open areas

                                       Both cavities and open (accessible) areas are machined. Slope-dependent machining is
                                       automatically activated.

                          Machining mode

                          Slope dependent machining - All areas: Steep areas in cavities always undergo Z-constant
                          machining, while flat areas in cavities (grounds) are always machined parallel to the contour.
                          Steep and flat areas can be machined using the Normal, Parallel or Z-Level strategies.

                          Slope dependent machining - Steep areas: Steep areas in cavities undergo Z-constant
                          machining. Steep areas within openly accessible areas can be machined using the Z-Level,
                          Parallel and Normal strategies.

                          Slope dependent machining - Flat areas: Cavities are not machined! Flat areas within openly
                          accessible areas can be machined using the Parallel or Normal strategies.

           Only cavities

                          Only cavities are machined. Slope-dependent machining is automatically activated.

                          Machining mode

                          Slope dependent machining - All areas: Steep areas in cavities always undergo Z-constant
                          machining, while flat areas in cavities (grounds) are always machined parallel to the contour.

                          Slope dependent machining - Steep areas: Steep areas in cavities undergo Z-constant
                          machining. Flat areas are not machined.

         Rework Machining

       Rework Machining

                                   Machining of pre-calculated toolpaths which were generated in a reference job using the Clip
                                   option, but could not be machined due to detected collisions. A different tool is used for the
                                   Rework Machining to avoid collisions at the respective areas.

                                   The reference job must be selected from the jobs already defined. The reference can be
                                   changed subsequently on the Setup dialogue page.

       Tools

                           The following cutter types can be used: ball mill, end mill and bullnose end mill.

                           When using tapered tools, the conical shape of the tool can be taken into account for the
                           path calculations during the tool check (see the Setup dialogue page).

                           Information on:

                           Selecting the tool            see section Defining a tool
                           Defining the tool parameters  see section Defining a tool
                           Selecting the frame           see section NC system and frames

       Parameters

                           Rework area
                           Toolpath: machining takes place along the toolpaths already machined in the reference job.
                           Collision path: milling takes place along the paths that the reference job could calculate, but
                           not machine due to collisions.
                           Connect smooth: This option smoothly connects toolpaths that run close to one another.
                           Also see the Zigzag option.

                           Stock allowance
                           Remaining allowance on the model.
                           For information on the definition of the basic machining parameters Security distance and
                           Security plane, see section Safety.

Appendix

      Application Settings

      Overview

                The Application Settings program allows you to configure your OPEN MIND software. The
                following settings are possible:

      Area of application

                                  For: Shows the area of application for the application settings.
                                  <System>: The settings apply to all users of the system.
                                  [Username]: The settings apply to the current user.

      Language

                Shows all languages registered for this program version. Selecting the relevant language
                switches the language for hyperMILL and auxiliary programs (hyperVIEW, OPEN MIND Tool
                Database etc.), but the hyperCAD-S setting remains unchanged.

                [Language]: Displays the language configured for the current user.
                [Language] <System>: Displays the language configured for all users of the system.
                After this option is selected, the active user returns to using the currently active system lan-
                guage. When the system language is changed, the language is also changed again for this
                user.

      Registered applications

                                  List of registered applications.
                                  Programs registered for all users are displayed in gray. Unless the Application Settings pro-
                                  gram is started with administrator privileges, it will not be possible to edit or delete these
                                  entries.
                                  Programs that are registered for the currently active user are displayed in black and can be
                                  edited and/or deleted by the currently active user.
                                  New: Add new application to the applications list.
                                  Edit / Delete: Edit or remove the existing application from list of registered applications.
                                  Key: Name used by OPEN MIND programs to start the application.
                                  Name: User-defined application name.
                                  Program: Complete path name under which the application is installed.
                                  Arguments: Users can enter additional parameters.

                               Show Eutron and Sentinel hardlocks
                                  Shows the Eutron and Sentinel dongles used on the computer.

13-2                                                                                                          hyperMILL
           Appendix        1 ReportDesigner
           Introduction

           ReportDesigner

           Introduction

                          The OPEN MIND ReportDesigner provides the user with a tool to adjust the display of joblist-
                          based or tool list-based documentation (reports) from hyperMILL to the requirements of their
                          particular company.

                          Content may be adjusted in the sense of the scope of the data to be returned in the report as
                          well as its sequence, text format, colour and other properties regarding the display of this
                          data.

           Initial Steps

                          The user can use the ReportDesigner to prepare a report layout in the form of an XSL file.

                          The report layout consists of a hierarchical structure of visible elements such as tables,
                          images, text areas, and so on, and of logical elements such as conditions, loops and place-

                          holders for the actual dataset of the report.

           Menu and Toolbar

                                       The ReportDesigner is a typical editor program, i.e. the user uses it to open a file, makes
                                       changes to that file, and then saves the results as a file.

                                       After opening the file, an element must first be selected from the structure. This can then be
                                       copied, moved and removed. Other functions may be possible depending on the currently
                                       selected element, such as editing the specific properties and adding possible child elements.
                                       A separate menu is available to insert specific new elements into the structure, while impor-
                                       tant elements can also be inserted directly from the toolbar. The Tools menu item contains
                                       additional complex functions which may become necessary in some situations.

                                    Creating a New Report
                                      A range of report layouts for various types and languages are installed together with hyper-
                                      MILL and are available to the user immediately and directly within hyperMILL.
                                       It is often sufficient to simply adjust these templates to your company's requirements. How-
                                       ever, in some cases it may also be necessary to design a report layout from scratch.

                                       The dialogue for this task can be found in the File > New menu item. The report type, e.g. a
                                       joblist report, the language and the output format, are all specified in this dialogue.

           Preview Area

                          The left area of the ReportDesigner is used to display a preview of the report output with
                          placeholders representing the actual data. Changes to the structure or properties of an ele-

                          ment are updated immediately in the preview.

           Structure View

                                       The right area, known as the structure view, is used to edit a report layout. In this area, the
                                       user can select an element to edit its properties, as well as add new elements if necessary.

                                       The context inside the report dataset, which is referenced e.g. when inserting placeholders,
                                       appears above the tree.

                                       Logical elements, such as placeholders and loops, are highlighted blue in the tree view while
                                       visible elements are displayed in normal black.

                                       It is possible to make direct changes to the properties of visible and logical elements in the
                                       lower Properties dialogue.

           Properties Dialogue

                                       The properties of the various elements in the structure of a report layout can be adjusted in
                                       the Properties dialogue.

hyperMILL                  13-3
1 Appendix                        Test Execution
         ReportDesigner

                                  For visible elements (p, div, span, th, td, ...), it is possible to change text properties such as
                                  font, size, bold/italic, colour, margins, borders and alignment. Other visible elements such as
                                  tables (table) and images (img) have other changeable properties.
                                  The CSS Styles tab is additionally available for all visible elements. This tab is used to
                                  clearly show and also, if necessary, change the display of the element.
                                  Logical elements (xsl:if, xsl:for-each, xsl:value-of, ...) also have specific attributes which can
                                  be individually adjusted here.

      Test Execution

                                  Particularly at the beginning, it can make sense to directly test even small changes to the
                                  report layout, that is, generate an actual report using the modified report layout. For this pur-
                                  pose, the File menu contains the Execute menu item. Enter the path to the ReportGenerator
                                 (hyperMILL installation directory) and the report dataset (for a job list, the file extension is
                                  .rda) here. Your company may also use a shared image directory. Specify this directory
                                  under Images.

      Visible Elements

                                  The visible elements in a report layout correspond to the well-known HTML format. Users
                                  familiar with HTML will quickly come to grips with these concepts.

      Text Areas and Properties

                                  The main text area in the ReportDesigner is the paragraph (p). A paragraph initially only con-
                                  tains the letters of the text contained inside this paragraph.
                                  The format properties for the paragraph can be displayed and if necessary changed by
                                  selecting the p in the structure view. Note that every change affects the entire paragraph.
                                  If the user wants to highlight a single word in bold or italic, for example, a separate structure
                                  element must first be inserted into a text range (span) for this specific purpose and then for-
                                  matted with the bold or italic property.
                                  Cells in a table or positions in a list can also be regarded as text ranges and their format
                                  properties adjusted correspondingly.
                                  The following displays typical Text properties.

                         Borders

13-4                                              hyperMILL
           Appendix                   1 ReportDesigner
           Text Areas and Properties

           Margins
           CSS styles
           Element properties

hyperMILL                             13-5
1 Appendix               Tables, rows and columns
         ReportDesigner

      Tables, rows and columns

                                  Tables are an important visible element for the display of values in a report. Tables are suit-
                                  able to graphically structure the overall output of a report, as well as to list the individual val-
                                  ues of a dataset.

                                  Tables (table) are divided into an optional header area (thead) and one or more table body
                                  areas (tbody).

                                  The header area can be used to e.g. display the headings of a tabular list, while the values
                                  can be specified as a placeholder using a loop (xsl:for-each) in the rows (tr) and columns (td)
                                  of a table body.
                                  In this way, you can generate a tabular list of the used tools with the respective tool proper-
                                  ties.
                                  Another function of tables is to specify the display areas inside a page. To do so, the dimen-
                                  sions of the columns are specified explicitly, e.g. a table with a width of 100% can be divided
                                  into three columns with widths of 25%, 50% and 25%. It is alternatively possible to specify
                                  widths in pixels using the abbreviation px. In this way, the user can divide the page into sev-
                                  eral display areas and position images or text ranges as needed. Further structure elements
                                  can then be hierarchically created inside the display areas.

      Simple and Numbered Lists

                                  The ReportDesigner provides functions for ordered and unordered lists. The difference is
                                  simply in the numbering of the list elements, i.e. ordered lists are automatically numbered as
                                  1, 2, 3, ... or A, B, C, ...

      Images and Graphics

                                  Image files in the GIF, PNG and JPG formats can be integrated into the report layout in the
                                  ReportDesigner as static images (img). Images can also be dynamically embedded for tools.
                                  This means that images of the tools are automatically created during report generation and
                                  shown in the report output.

                                  The difference between static and dynamic images is that the paths to static images do not
                                  change and they can therefore be fixed in the report layout. Dynamic images relate to a spe-
                                  cific job or tool, for example, and are read from the report dataset and entered in the report
                                  layout using a placeholder.

      Logical Elements

                                  In addition to visible elements, which are used to format the report output, the ReportDe-
                                  signer also provides a range of logical elements, which can be used to embed the data from
                                  a job list or tool dataset in the report output.

                                  Note that the underlying dataset of e.g. a job list is hierarchically structured in its own right.
                                  The ReportDesigner helps the user insert placeholders and loops by only making properties
                                  and possible loops belonging to the current data element available for selection, depending
                                  on the context.

                               Placeholders

                                  Job lists, jobs, tools and other data elements have specific properties such as designation,
                                  numbering, length, colour etc.

                                  Depending on the context in the report dataset, the user can insert individual properties of,
                                  for example, a job into the report layout using a placeholder (xsl:value-of). The possible job
                                  properties are made available in the selection dialogue, and are then applied to the place-
                                  holder's select attribute.

                                  Placeholders can be inserted from the Insert > Value Of ... menu item.

                                  The possible attributes, in this case those of the tool, are selected depending on the context
                                  in the report dataset.
                                  Sometimes it may be necessary to specifically access properties of the superordinate ele-
                                  ment or other elements in the report dataset, or formatting functions. The ReportDesigner
                                  uses the xpath query language for this purpose, which means that the user can enter arbi-

13-6                                               hyperMILL
           Appendix                                                1 ReportDesigner
           Logical Elements

                             trary other xpath expressions in the select attribute with knowledge of the structure of the
                             dataset.

                             xsl and xpath offer an enormous range of options, which are not described in further detail
                             here. A number of tutorials and a wide range of documentation are available on the internet.

                             Loops and Repetition
                             Every report dataset is built around a hierarchical structure. A job list, for example, consists
                             of a list of individual jobs and an additional list of used tools.

                             A list of jobs can be visualised in a number of ways, e.g. as an overview in a table or as a list
                             of pages, each of which shows an individual job.

                             For display, it is first necessary to create a loop to cover all jobs in the job list. In the first
                             example case, this loop is used to display the table rows.

                             In the second case, each iteration of the loop displays an entire page. Loops are available
                             under the Insert > For all ... menu item.

                             Because tables with a loop structure are required in many cases, the Tools menu contains
                             the Dynamic table menu item to bring these common steps together in one place.

                             The following structure is inserted:

hyperMILL                                                          13-7
1 Appendix                                                                                    Conditions
         ReportDesigner

      Conditions

                         Inside the loop, it may be necessary to only display certain elements, for example jobs with a
                         particular property. To achieve this, the user can use a condition to filter the output. The
                         Insert > Condition menu item allows such filters to be inserted.

      Other functions

                                  The Tools menu in the ReportDesigner contains a few special functions for the calculation of
                                  certain values.

      MinTlength

                         The MinTlength function is used to output the shortest length of a tool in a job list. If a tool is
                         used several times, only the tool with the shortest required length will be used. This prevents
                         tools from being output multiple times.

      Zmax-Zmin

                         Output of the relative and axial heights of a tool path (z-height).

      System Requirements

                                  · Internet Explorer 8
                                  · MS Office 2007 or higher
                                  · Windows XP, Windows Vista, Windows 7

           Introduction

           FAQs / Contacting your OPEN MIND partner

           Introduction

                         The information in this document is addressed to all hyperMILL/hyperCAD-S users. It pro-
                         vides tips and answers in the event of unexpected problems that may arise when working
                         with hyperMILL or hyperCAD-S. The information contained here also complements the
                         known documentations and training materials.

           Frequently asked questions

                                       The first section provides you with additional hints and tricks (divided into subject areas) for
                                      the efficient usage of hyperMILL / hyperCAD-S.

                                       If you cannot solve your problem by means of the FAQs, please contact the OPEN MIND
                                       supportor your OPEN MIND partner. In order to be able to investigate your issue efficiently
                                       and resolve it as quickly as possible, we require some information from you, which is sum-
                                       marised in section Contacting the OPEN MIND partner.

           hyperMILL installation

                         hyperMILL in hyperCAD/thinkdesign

                         I have installed hyperMILL, but thehyperMILL toolbar is not available.

                         Close hyperMILL, go to the C:\Program Files\OPEN MIND\Settings Wizard\[version number]
                         directory of your current hyperMILL installation and start the hyperMILL switch (double-click
                         SwitchUi.exe).

                                      Select the desired hyperMILL version, select the CAD systemand the Languageand then
                                       click Switch.

       Post Processors

                                New post processor
                                  I have got a new post processor. How to proceed?
                                   a. note the hints
                                   Please follow the hints, added to the post processor delivery.
                                   If necessary, please consult your OPEN MIND partner.
                                   b. Installation
                                   For information on installing a postprocessor, see section .
                                   c. Creating a configuration file.
                                   Please adapt all parameters of the configuration file (*.def file) belonging to the post proces-
                                   sor, which are especially important for your purposes.

                                                                                                                                                           hyperMILL
           Appendix                    FAQs / Contacting your OPEN MIND partner  1
           Frequently asked questions

hyperMILL  For information on adapting the configuration, see section .
           The adaptation of the configuration file is a continuous process. Depending on the frequency
           of the usage of the postprocessor with different tool path files, this process can take several
           months, if necessary.
           d. Testing
           Please test the new post processor with typical tool path files [according to your usual
           needs]. Please don't use a current project for this, but (if possible) please use preferably a
           workpiece, which is not used for commercial purposes.
           If only a commercial workpiece is available, please only use toolpaths that maintain a
           defined distance to the workpiece for testing.
           First, please test single toolpaths, i.e., single jobs without tool changes. Afterwards, the test-
           ing procedure can be enhanced and the single jobs tested before, can be tested with
           machining priority including tool change.

           Post processor update
           I have received an update of an post processor. How to proceed?
           To implement the current changes of your post processor, please proceed as follows:
           a. Back up
           Firstly please back up all the existing postprocessors, to prevent them from unintended over-
           writing by newly provided postprocessor files. Doing so means that the original postproces-
           sor files will be available as backup files further on.
           b. Apply adjustments to an update
           Please include the adjustments made to the post processor's configuration file(s) in the post
           processor update. If necessary, please consult your OPEN MIND partner.

                          The configuration file is a text file. You can compare the updated file with the
                          existing file und let display the differences into a textfile editor.

           c. Adjust specified path
           If you saved the updated postprocessor files (oma files) in another directory (different from
           the directory usually used) or if you renamed the updated file, you also need to adjust the
           path in the machine administration of hyperVIEW (hyperVIEW menu > Edit > Machine
           Administration > New > General > Machine Properties > Postprocessor).

                          Please always save the updated files in a separate directory to prevent them
                          from being overwritten by accident. Please inform the administrator of your
                         hyperMILL installation about the updated postprocessor, so that the administra-
                          tor will use the latest postprocessor file for subsequent installations, for exam-
                         ple, after a new hyperMILL Release.
                          If the updated postprocessor is used by several persons in your company, all
                          these persons should be informed about every update.

           d. Testing:
           Updated postprocessors have to be tested (as well as new postprocessors).

           Automatic postprocessor updates
           Are updates automatically shipped?
           No. Updates are neither generated automatically nor shipped. Therefore you should contact
           your OPEN MIND partner once a year, to find out about the availability of a postprocessor
           update.

           Adjustments of the postprocessor
           I want to have a adjustment of the NC output of the post processor? How to proceed?

                                                                                                                                              13-11
1 Appendix                                         Frequently asked questions
         FAQs / Contacting your OPEN MIND partner

       Please contact your OPEN MIND partner. The information, named in the following is
       required for handling your request:

       a. Which postprocessor should be updated?
       Please use the hyperVIEW > function > Machine Properties > Postprocessor > Info.

       You can copy all information of the Postprocessor information dialogue directly into the clip-
       board and save it to a text file.

13-12  b. Creating an hvz file (including NC file).
       Please generate a hvz file from all operations (jobs), you have post processed together. For
       further information, see section or section CAD and hvz file of this document).
       Please make sure to generate this hvz file after postprocessing in order to ensure that the
       corresponding NC file exists.
       c. Documenting the desired changes.
       Please document the desired change using a specific hyperMILL project and inform your
       OPEN MIND partner in detail about all functions you wish to have in the new postprocessor.
       For this purpose, please generate a new NC file and also a text file that describes the
       desired changes (please use the corresponding machine and/or the CNC control manuals, if
       necessary).
       d. CAD file
       Maybe the CAD file including job list, you used for generating the hvz file (see section b) is
       also necessary. Please also provide this data to your OPEN MIND partner on request.

                      Please note: Adjustments to a postprocessor may incur additional fees! Your
                      OPEN MIND partner will inform you, before expenses are incurred.

       Postprocessor and new hyperMILL

       Do I have to install a new postprocessor after a new hyperMILL release?
       OPEN MIND endeavours to ensure compatibility with existing postprpocessors with its new
       releases. However, you can check the behaviour of the postprocessor after the initiation of
       the new hyperMILL release.
       We recommend doing this based on the last project that was edited and postprocessed
       before the new hyperMILL release went live. If the toolpaths are not recalculated in the new
       hyperMILL release, the new hyperMILL release should generate exactly the same NC pro-
       grams. Furthermore, OPEN MIND recommends that you check the toolpaths typically used
       in your applications.
       Examples: If you primarily program 2D toolpaths with hyperMILL, you should check some of
       the 2D toolpaths. If you primarily generate 5X machinings, please compare some 5X tool-
       paths.
       However, if the results deviate from the usual NC output in a new release, please first check
       if the postprocessor files last provided for hyperMILL were installed by your administrator
       when the new hyperMILL release was implemented. If the deviations in the NC output per-
       sist, please proceed as instructed in section Adjustments of the postprocessor.
       Please also contact your OPEN MIND partner and inform him or her about this incompatible
       behaviour following the installation of a new hyperMILL release. Your OPEN MIND partner
       will analyse the incompatible behaviour and provide further information.
       Furthermore, after installing a new hyperMILL release, you should check whether a new
       postprocessor release is also be available. Please see the related information in section
       Automatic postprocessor updates.
